Marquis Suí escaped.
Dòu Dān captured his barbarian chariot,
along with his barbarian charioteer, the Junior Master.
In autumn,
Suí and Chǔ made peace,
but the Viscount of Chǔ was initially unwilling to agree.
Dòu Bó Bǐ said,
"Heaven is removing their affliction;
Suí cannot yet be conquered."
So they made a covenant and returned.
B2.8.3 In winter,
the King ordered Guō Zhòng to install Mín, the younger brother of Marquis Āi of Jìn, in Jìn.
B2.8.4 The Duke of Jì came
and then escorted the Queen back to Jì,
as was proper.
A2.9 "The Ninth Year of Duke Huán - Annals"
A2.9.1 In the spring of the ninth year,
Jì Jì Jiāng returned to the capital.
A2.9.2 Summer, fourth month.
A2.9.3 Autumn, seventh month.
A2.9.4 In winter,
the Earl of Cáo (曹伯, Cáo Bó) sent his heir apparent, Shègū (射姑), to court.
B2.9 *Commentary on the Ninth Year of Duke Huán* (桓公九年傳, Huán Gōng Jiǔ Nián Zhuàn)
B2.9.1 In the spring of the ninth year,
Jì Jìjiāng (紀季姜) returned to the capital.
Of all the daughters of the feudal lords who travel,
only the Queen is recorded.
B2.9.2 The Viscount of Bā (巴子, Bā Zǐ) sent Hán Fú (韓服) to inform Chǔ (楚),
requesting to establish friendship with Dèng (鄧).
The Viscount of Chǔ (楚子, Chǔ Zǐ) sent Dào Shuò (道朔) to lead the Bā envoy
to present gifts to Dèng.
The people of Yōu (鄾), a southern border town of Dèng, attacked
and seized the gifts,
killing Dào Shuò and the Bā envoy.
The Viscount of Chǔ sent Wěi Zhāng (薳章) to reproach Dèng.
The people of Dèng did not accept.
In summer,
Chǔ sent Dòu Lián (鬭廉) to lead troops, together with the Bā troops, to besiege Yōu.
Dèng sent Yǎng Shēng (養甥) and
Dān Shēng (聃甥) to lead troops to rescue Yōu.
They pursued the Bā troops three times,
but were unsuccessful.
Dòu Lián arranged his troops in formation within the Bā troops
to fight,
and then retreated north.
The people of Dèng pursued them.
They turned their backs on the Bā army
and attacked them from both sides.
The Dèng army was greatly defeated.
The people of Yōu collapsed at night.
B2.9.3 In autumn,
Guó Zhòng, Ruì Bó, Liáng Bó, Xún Hóu, and Jiǎ Bó attacked Qūwò.
B2.9.4 In winter,
the eldest son of the ruler of Cáo came to court.
He was treated as a top minister;
this was proper protocol.
A feast was held for the eldest son of Cáo.
At the beginning of the offering,
when the music was played, he sighed.
Shī Fǔ said:
"The eldest son of Cáo must have worries!
This is not the place to sigh."
A2.10 *Huán Gōng* Year 10 *Jīng*
A2.10.1 In the spring of the tenth year,
on the day *gēngshēn* of the first month of the king,
Cáo Bó Zhōngshēng died.
A2.10.2 In the fifth month of summer,
Cáo Huán Gōng was buried.
A2.10.3 In autumn,
the duke met with the Marquis of Wèi at Táoqiū,
Did not obtain it.
A2.10.4 In the twelfth month of winter, on the Bǐngwǔ day, the Marquis of Qí, the Marquis of Wèi, and the Earl of Zhèng came to fight at Láng.
the Marquis of Qí,
the Marquis of Wèi,
and the Earl of Zhèng came to battle at Láng.
B2.10 *The Tenth Year of Duke Huán*
B2.10.1 In the spring of the tenth year, Duke Huán of Cáo died.
B2.10.2 Guó Zhòng slandered his grand master Zhān Fù to the King.
Zhān Fù had grounds for defense and led the King's army to attack Guó.
In summer, the Duke of Guó fled to Yú.
B2.10.3 In autumn, the people of Qín escorted Rùi Bó Wàn into Rùi.
B2.10.4 Initially, Shū of Yú possessed a jade treasure, and the Duke of Yú sought it.
He did not present it.
Afterwards, he regretted it, saying,
"There is a saying in Zhōu:
'A commoner is not guilty, but possessing jade is the cause of his ruin.'
What use do I have for this? It will only invite disaster."
Is it because of seeking profit that he is doing harm?"
Thereupon he presented it.
He then asked for his treasured sword.
Shū said,
"This is insatiable.
Being insatiable,
it will bring disaster upon me."
Consequently, he attacked Yú Gōng.
Therefore, Yú Gōng fled and took refuge in Gòngchí.
B2.10.5 In winter,
Qí, Wèi,
and Zhèng came to fight at Láng;
we had a reason.
Initially,
the Northern Róng were troubling Qí.
The feudal lords came to their rescue.
Zhèng Gōngzǐ Hū had merit in this.
The people of Qí provided provisions to the feudal lords,
and had Lǔ rank second to them.
Lǔ, based on the Zhou ranking system, placed Zhèng after them.
The people of Zhèng were angered
and requested assistance from Qí.
The people of Qí used the army of Wèi to assist them,
therefore it is not referred to as an invasion.
First writing Qí and Wèi,
is due to their royal rank.
A2.11 *Duke Huán's Eleventh Year Chronicle*
A2.11.1 In the eleventh year, spring, first month,
people from Qí,
people from Wèi,
and people from Zhèng formed an alliance at È cáo.
A2.11.2 In summer, fifth month, Guǐ wèi day,
Bó Wùshēng of Zhèng died.
A2.11.3 In autumn, seventh month,
Zhèng Zhuāng Gōng was buried.
A2.11.4 In the ninth month,
the people of Sòng captured Zhèng Jì Zhòng.
Tū returned to Zhèng.
Zhèng Hū fled to Wèi.
A2.11.5 Róu met with Gōng of Sòng,
Marquis of Chén, and
Uncle Cài to form an alliance at Zhé.
A2.11.6 The Duke met with Gōng of Sòng at Fū Zhōng.
A2.11.7 In winter, twelfth month,
the Duke met with Gōng of Sòng at Kàn.
B2.11 "Commentary on the Eleventh Year of Duke Huán"
B2.11.1 In the eleventh year, spring,
Qí, Wèi,
Zhèng, and Sòng formed an alliance at Ècáo.
B2.11.2 Chǔ general Qū Xiá was about to make an alliance with Èr and Zhěn.
The Yún people encamped at Púsāo,
intending to join Suí, Jiǎo, Zhōu, and Liǎo in attacking the Chǔ army.
Mò Áo was troubled by this.
Dòu Lián said:
"The Yún people are encamped in the suburbs,
they will certainly be unwary.
Moreover, they are daily expecting the arrival of the four cities.
You, my lord, should station yourself in the suburbs of Yǐng,
to defend against the four cities,
and I will use a sharp force to attack Yún by night.
Yún has a sense of security
and relies on its city walls,
they have no will to fight.
If we defeat the Yún army,
the four cities will certainly abandon them."
Mò Áo said:
"Why not request reinforcements from the king?"
He replied:
"Victory in battle lies in harmony,
not in numbers.
The inability of Shāng and Zhōu to resist,
is something you have heard of, my lord.
Having already formed an army to go out,
what reinforcements are needed?"
Mò Áo said:
"[Bǔ zhī?] (Shall we divine?)"
He replied:
"[Bǔ yǐ jué yí.] (Divination is to resolve doubts.)
[Bù yí], (If there is no doubt,)
[hé bǔ?] (why divine?)"
Thereupon, he defeated the army of Yún at Púsāo,
and finally concluded the alliance and returned.
B2.11.3 [Zhèng Zhāo Gōng] (Duke Zhao of Zheng)'s defeat by the Northern Rong.
The people of Qi were going to give him a wife.
Duke Zhao declined.
[Jì Zhòng] said:
"[Bì qǔ zhī.] (You must take her.)
[Jūn duō nèi chǒng], (Your lord has many favorites,)
[zǐ wú dà yuán], (your son has no great support,)
[jiāng bù lì.] (he will not be established.)
[Sān gōngzǐ jiē jūn yě.] (The three sons are all lords.)"
He did not follow his advice.
In summer,
[Zhèng Zhuāng Gōng] (Duke Zhuang of Zheng) died.
Initially,
[Jì Fēngrén Zhòngzú] (Ji Fengren Zhongzu),
was favored by Duke Zhuang.
Duke Zhuang made him a minister.
He married [Dèng Màn] to the duke,
and she gave birth to Duke Zhao.
Therefore, [Jì Zhòng] established him.
The daughter of the [Sòng Yōng] clan was given to Duke Zhuang of Zheng,
It is said that Yōng Jí,
gave birth to Duke Lì.
The Yōng lineage,
was favored by Duke Zhuāng of Sòng,
therefore he induced Jì Zhòng and arrested him,
saying:
"If you do not establish Tū,
you will die."
He also arrested Duke Lì
and demanded a bribe.
Jì Zhòng made a covenant with the people of Sòng,
to return Duke Lì and establish him.
In the autumn, the ninth month, on the day dīnghài,
Duke Zhāo fled to Wèi.
On the day jǐhài,
Duke Lì was established.
A2.12 *Huán Gōng, Year 12, Annals*
A2.12.1 In the twelfth year, spring, first month.
A2.12.2 In summer, sixth month, on the day rén yín,
the Duke met with the Marquis of Qǐ,
and the Viscount of Jǔ, and made a covenant at Qūchí.
A2.12.3 In autumn, seventh month, on the day dīnghài,
the Duke met with Duke of Sòng,
and the people of Yān, and made a covenant at Gǔqiū.
A2.12.4 In the eighth month, on the day rén chén,
Hóu Yuè of Chén died.
A2.12.5 The Duke met with Duke of Sòng at Xū.
A2.12.6 In the eleventh month of winter,
the Duke met with the Duke of Sòng at Guī.
A2.12.7 On the day bǐng xū,
the Duke met with Bó of Zhèng,
and they formed an alliance at Wǔfǔ.
A2.12.8 On the day bǐng xū,
Hóu Jìn of Wèi died.
A2.12.9 In the twelfth month,
the army of Zhèng and [the Duke] attacked Sòng.
On the day dīng wèi,
they fought at Sòng.
B2.12 *Commentary on the Twelfth Year of Duke Huán*
B2.12.1 In the summer of the twelfth year,
they formed an alliance at Qūchí,
to make peace between Qǐ and
Jǔ.
B2.12.2 The Duke wanted to make peace between Sòng and Zhèng.
In autumn,
Duke Zhuāng of Lǔ and Duke Chéng of Sòng made an alliance at the hill of Jūdú.
Duke Chéng of Sòng was not to be trusted,
therefore, they met again at Xū.
In winter,
they met again at Guī.
Duke Chéng of Sòng broke the peace agreement,
so he made an alliance with Duke Zhuāng of Zhèng at Wǔfǔ,
and then led troops to attack Sòng,
and fought there,
because Sòng lacked trustworthiness.
The gentleman said:
"If trustworthiness is not maintained,
an alliance is of no benefit.
The Book of Poetry says:
'The gentleman makes repeated alliances,
and chaos is thereby prolonged.'
This is due to a lack of trustworthiness."
B2.12.3 Chǔ attacked Jiǎo,
and encamped at its south gate.
Mò'áo Qū Xiá said:
"Jiǎo is small and imprudent,
and being imprudent, it has few plans.
Please, do not prevent the woodcutters from tempting them."
They followed his advice.
The people of Jiǎo captured thirty men.
The next day,
the people of Jiǎo rushed out,
driving the Chǔ laborers into the mountains.
The Chǔ (楚) people encamped at its north gate,
and ambushed them at the foot of the mountains.
They greatly defeated them.
They made an alliance under the city walls and returned.
B2.12.4 Regarding the campaign to attack Jiǎo (絞),
the Chǔ (楚) army crossed the Péng (彭) River in separate groups.
The people of Luó (羅) wanted to attack them.
They sent Bó Jiā (伯嘉) to spy on them.
He circled around three times to count them.
A2.13 *Huán Gōng* (桓公) Year 13 *Jīng* (經)
A2.13.1 In the spring, second month, of the thirteenth year,
the Duke met with the Marquis of Jǐ (紀),
and the Count of Zhèng (鄭).
On *jǐsì* (己巳),
he fought with the Marquis of Qí (齊),
the Duke of Sòng (宋),
the Marquis of Wèi (衛),
and the people of Yān (燕).
The armies of Qí (齊),
Sòng (宋),
Wèi (衛),
and Yān (燕) were utterly defeated.
A2.13.2 In the third month,
the Duke Xuān (宣) of Wèi (衛) was buried.
A2.13.3 In summer,
Great floods.
A2.13.4 In the seventh month of autumn.
A2.13.5 In the tenth month of winter.
B2.13 *Commentary on the Thirteenth Year of Duke Huán*
B2.13.1 In the spring of the thirteenth year,
Qū Xiá of Chǔ attacked Luó,
Dòu Bóbǐ saw him off.
Upon his return,
he said to his charioteer,
"Mò Áo will certainly be defeated.
His gait is lofty,
his heart is not steadfast."
Thereupon, he met with the ruler of Chǔ
and said,
"You must send reinforcements!"
The ruler of Chǔ declined.
He went in and told his wife, Dèng Màn.
Dèng Màn said,
"The Grand Master is probably not referring to the masses,
but rather is saying that you, my lord, should cherish the common people with trust,
instruct the various officials with virtue,
and awe Mò Áo with punishments.
Mò Áo is emboldened by the campaign at Pú Sāo,
and will act on his own accord.
bì Xiǎo Luó.
If Your Lordship does not pacify them,
would they not be prepared?
Indeed, I urged Your Lordship to instruct the troops
and to be fond of pacifying them,
to summon the various officials
and encourage them with virtuous commands,
to see Mò Áo
and inform him that Heaven does not easily grant favors.
If not,
how could I not know that the Chǔ army has departed in full?"
The Chǔ ruler sent a Lài man to pursue them,
but he did not catch up.
Mò Áo sent a message throughout the army, saying:
"Those who remonstrate will be punished!"
When they reached Yān,
they crossed the river in disorder,
and consequently, there was no order at all.
Furthermore, they were not prepared.
When they reached Luó,
Luó and the Lú Róng armies attacked them together,
inflicting a great defeat.
Mò Áo hanged himself in a desolate valley.
The commanders were imprisoned in Yě Fù
to await punishment.
The Chǔ ruler said:
"It is my fault."
He released them all.
B2.13.2 Sòng frequently demanded tributes from Zhèng.
Zhèng, unable to bear this burden,
therefore, along with Jǐ,
Lǔ, and Qí, fought with Sòng,
Wèi, and Yān.
The record of where they fought is not written,
because it was later.
B2.13.3 The people of Zhèng came to request a restoration of friendship.
A2.14 *Huán Gōng* Year 14 *Jīng*
A2.14.1 In the spring, the first month, of the fourteenth year,
the Duke met with the Earl of Zhèng in Cáo.
A2.14.2 There was no ice.
A2.14.3 In summer, the fifth month,
the Earl of Zhèng sent his younger brother Yǔ to come and make a covenant.
A2.14.4 In autumn, the eighth month, *rénshēn*,
the *yùlǐn* (imperial granary) burned down.
A2.14.5 On *yǐhài*,
the autumn sacrifice was performed.
A2.14.6 In winter, the twelfth month, *dīngsì*,
the Marquis Lùfù of Qí died.
A2.14.7 The people of Sòng, along with the people of Qí,
The people of Cài,
the people of Wèi,
and the people of Chén attacked Zhèng.
B2.14 *Commentary on the Fourteenth Year of Duke Huán*
B2.14.1 In the spring of the fourteenth year,
there was a meeting at Cáo.
The people of Cáo provided grain,
which was proper.
B2.14.2 In the summer,
Zǐ Rén of Zhèng came to renew the alliance
and to repair the meeting at Cáo.
B2.14.3 In the autumn, on the day rénshēn of the eighth month,
the Yùlǐn (imperial granary) burned.
On the day yǐhài,
the *cháng* (autumn sacrifice) was performed.
This was recorded in the chronicles,
as it did no harm.
B2.14.4 In the winter,
the people of Sòng, along with the lords of other states, attacked Zhèng
to avenge the battle of Sòng.
They burned the Qú Gate.
They entered
and reached the great avenue.
They attacked the eastern suburbs
and took Niúshǒu.
They took beams from the great palace and returned with them
To make a rafter for the gate of Lú.
A2.15 *Huán Gōng* Year 15, *Jīng* (Annals)
A2.15.1 In the fifteenth year, spring, second month,
the Heavenly King sent *Jiā Fǔ* to request carriages.
A2.15.2 Third month, *yǐ wèi* day,
the Heavenly King passed away.
A2.15.3 Summer, fourth month, *jǐ sì* day,
the *Qí Xī Gōng* was buried.
A2.15.4 Fifth month,
*Zhèng Bó Tū* abruptly fled to *Cài*.
A2.15.5 The heir of *Zhèng*, *Hū*, returned to *Zhèng*.
A2.15.6 The Viscount of *Xǔ* entered *Xǔ*.
A2.15.7 The Duke met with the Marquis of *Qí* at *Ài*.
A2.15.8 The people of *Zhū*,
the people of *Móu*,
and the people of *Gé* came to court.
A2.15.9 Autumn, ninth month,
*Zhèng Bó Tū* entered *Lì*.
A2.15.10 In the eleventh month of winter,
the Duke met with the Duke of Sòng,
the Marquis of Wèi,
and the Marquis of Chén at Nài,
to attack Zhèng.
B2.15 *Zuǒ Zhuàn*, Year 15 of Duke Huán
B2.15.1 In the spring of the fifteenth year,
the King of Heaven sent Jiāfù to request carriages,
which was improper.
The feudal lords do not contribute carriages and
attire,
and the Son of Heaven does not privately seek wealth.
B2.15.2 Jì Zhòng held exclusive power,
and the Count of Zhèng was troubled by this.
He ordered his son-in-law Yōng Jiū to kill him.
He was going to feast him in the suburbs.
Yōng Jī knew of this,
and said to her mother:
"Who is closer, father or husband?"
Her mother said:
"Everyone can be a husband,
but there is only one father.
How can they be compared?"
Thereupon she told Jì Zhòng, saying:
"The Yōng family is leaving their home
and will feast you in the suburbs.
I am perplexed by it,
so I report it."
Jì Zhòng 祭仲 killed Yōng Jiū 雍糾,
and his corpse was displayed at the pond of the Zhōu 周 clan.
The Duke loaded it up and took it out,
saying,
"Scheming with women,
it is fitting that he died."
In summer,
Duke Lì 厲公 fled to Cài 蔡.
B2.15.3 In the sixth month, on the day yǐhài 乙亥,
Zhāo Gōng 昭公 entered.
B2.15.4 Shū 叔 of Xǔ 許 entered Xǔ 許.
B2.15.5 The Duke met with the Marquis of Qí 齊 at Ài 艾,
to plan the settling of Xǔ 許.
B2.15.6 In autumn,
the Earl of Zhèng 鄭, through the people of Lì 櫟, killed Tán Bó 檀伯,
and then resided in Lì 櫟.
B2.15.7 In winter,
there was a meeting at Nǎi 袲,
to plan an attack on Zhèng 鄭,
intending to reinstate Duke Lì 厲公.
They were unable to succeed and returned.
A2.16 *The Annals of the Sixteenth Year of Duke Huán 桓公*
A2.16.1 In the sixteenth year, in the first month of spring,
the Duke met with Duke of Sòng 宋公,
the Marquis of Cài 蔡侯,
Wèi Hóu was in Cáo.
A2.16.2 In the fourth month of summer,
the Duke met with Sòng Gōng,
Wèi Hóu,
Chén Hóu,
and Cài Hóu to attack Zhèng.
A2.16.3 In the seventh month of autumn,
the Duke returned from attacking Zhèng.
A2.16.4 In winter,
Xiàng was fortified.
A2.16.5 In the eleventh month,
Wèi Hóu Shuò fled to Qí.
B2.16 *Commentary on the Sixteenth Year of Duke Huán*
B2.16.1 In the first month of spring of the sixteenth year,
there was a meeting in Cáo
to plan an attack on Zhèng.
B2.16.2 In summer,
Zhèng was attacked.
B2.16.3 In the seventh month of autumn,
the Duke returned from attacking Zhèng,
observing the rite of *yǐ yǐn zhì*.
B2.16.4 In winter,
Chéng Xiàng.
Shū Shí yě.
B2.16.5 Initially,
Duke Xuān of Wèi had an illicit affair (烝) with Yí Jiāng,
and she gave birth to Jí Zǐ,
who was placed under the care of the Right Gōngzǐ.
The duke arranged a marriage for him in Qí,
but the bride was beautiful,
and the duke took her for himself.
She gave birth to Shòu and Shuò.
Shòu was placed under the care of the Left Gōngzǐ.
Yí Jiāng hanged herself.
Xuān Jiāng and Gōngzǐ Shuò plotted against Jí Zǐ.
The duke sent him to Qí.
He sent bandits to wait for him in Shēn,
intending to kill him.
Shòu Zǐ told him about it
and urged him to go back.
He refused,
saying:
"If I were to abandon my father's command,
what use would I be as a son?
It would only be acceptable if there was a country without a father."
When he was about to leave,
he was given wine to drink.
Shòu Zǐ carried his pennant ahead of him.
The thieves killed him.
Jízǐ arrived in haste,
and said:
"It is me they seek.
What crime did this man commit?
Please kill me instead!"
They killed him as well.
The two young lords had long resented Huì Gōng.
In the eleventh month,
Zuǒ Gōngzǐ Xiè and
Yòu Gōngzǐ Zhí installed Gōngzǐ Qiánmóu.
Huì Gōng fled to Qí.
A2.17 The 17th Year of Duke Huán
A2.17.1 In the spring, the first month, on bǐng chén,
the Duke met with the Marquis of Qí and
the Marquis of Jǐ, and they swore an oath at Huáng.
A2.17.2 In the second month, on bǐng wǔ,
the Duke met with Zhū Yífù,
and they swore an oath at Cuī.
A2.17.3 In the fifth month, on bǐng wǔ,
he engaged the Qí army in battle at Xī.
A2.17.4 In the sixth month, on dīng chǒu,
the Marquis of Cài, Fēngrén, died.
A2.17.5 In the eighth month of autumn,
Cài Jì voluntarily returned to Cài.
A2.17.6 On Guǐsì,
the Marquis Huán of Cài was buried.
A2.17.7 Then the people of Sòng and
the people of Wèi attacked Zhū.
A2.17.8 On the first day of the tenth month in winter,
there was a solar eclipse.
B2.17 *Commentary on the Seventeenth Year of Duke Huán*
B2.17.1 In the spring of the seventeenth year,
they made a covenant at Huáng to
reconcile Qí and Jǐ,
and also to discuss the affair of Wèi.
B2.17.2 Zhū Yífù also made a covenant at Cuī,
which followed the covenant at Miè.
B2.17.3 In summer,
they fought with the Qí army at Xī,
concerning a border dispute.
Thereupon the people of Qí invaded the borders of Lǔ,
and the border officials came to report it.
The Duke said:
"In border matters,
"Carefully guard the one thing,
and prepare for the unforeseen;
for now, exhaust all preparations.
When the time comes to fight,
what need is there to beg?"
B2.17.4 Marquess Huán of Cài died.
The people of Cài summoned Jì of Cài from Chén.
B2.17.5 In autumn,
Jì of Cài returned from Chén to Cài,
and the people of Cài praised him.
B2.17.6 They attacked Zhū,
it was the will of Sòng.
B2.17.7 In the winter, the first day of the tenth month,
there was a solar eclipse.
It was not recorded,
because the official failed to do so.
The Son of Heaven had a solar official,
and the lords of the states had a solar attendant.
The solar official was a high minister, in order to ascertain the days,
this was ritual.
The solar attendant did not miss the days,
to announce them to the various officials at court.
B2.17.8 Initially,
Bó of Zhèng was going to appoint Gāo Qúmí as a high minister.
Zhāo Gōng disliked him
and strongly advised against it,
but he did not listen.
When Zhāo Gōng ascended the throne,
Zhāo Gōng was established, fearing that [the people] would kill him.
On the day xīn mǎo,
he assassinated Zhāo Gōng and
established Gōngzǐ Wěi.
A gentleman said,
"Zhāo Gōng knew what was detested."
Gōngzǐ Dá said,
"Gāo Bó will probably be executed!
He is excessively restoring what is detested."
A2.18 *Huán Gōng 18th Year Classic*
A2.18.1 In the spring of the eighteenth year, the king's first month,
the Duke met with the Marquis of Qí at Luò.
The Duke and his wife, Jiāng Shì, then went to Qí.
A2.18.2 In the summer, the fourth month, on the day bǐng zǐ,
the Duke died in Qí.
A2.18.3 On the day dīng yǒu,
the Duke's funeral procession arrived from Qí.
A2.18.4 In the autumn, the seventh month.
A2.18.5 In the winter, the twelfth month, on the day jǐ chǒu,
we buried our lord, Huán Gōng.
B2.18 *Huán Gōng 18th Year Commentary*
B2.18.1 In the spring of the eighteenth year,
the Duke was about to travel,
and consequently went to Qí 齊 with Jiāng 姜.
Shēn Xū 申繻 said:
"A woman has her family,
a man has his household;
they should not violate each other.
This is called propriety.
To change this
will certainly lead to failure."
The Duke met with the Marquis of Qí 齊 at Luò 濼,
and consequently took Wén Jiāng 文姜 to Qí 齊.
The Marquis of Qí 齊 had illicit relations with her.
The Duke reproached her for it.
She informed the Marquis of Qí 齊.
In the fourth month, on the day bǐngzǐ 丙子,
he feasted the Duke.
He had Gōngzǐ Péngshēng 公子彭生 drive the Duke's carriage,
and the Duke died in the carriage.
The people of Lǔ 魯 reported to Qí 齊, saying:
"Our late lord, fearing Your Lordship's power,
did not dare to remain in peace,
and came to renew the old alliance.
The rites were completed, but he did not return;
there is no one to blame,
and this would be looked upon unfavorably by the various lords.
We ask that Péngshēng 彭生 be executed to appease them."
The people of Qí killed Péng Shēng.
B2.18.2 In autumn,
the Marquis of Qí encamped his troops at Shǒuzhǐ;
Zǐ Wěi met with him,
with Gāo Qúmí as his attendant.
On the day wùxū of the seventh month,
the people of Qí killed Zǐ Wěi,
and quartered Gāo Qúmí.
Jì Zhòng went to Chén to welcome the Zheng heir
and installed him.
On this journey,
Jì Zhòng was aware of it,
so he feigned illness and did not go.
People said:
"Jì Zhòng avoided it through his knowledge."
Zhòng said:
"Indeed."
B2.18.3 The Duke of Zhōu wanted to assassinate King Zhuāng
and install Prince Kè.
Xīn Bó informed the king,
and together with the king, they killed the Duke of Zhōu Hēi Jiān.
Prince Kè fled to Yān.
Initially,
Zǐ Yí was favored by King Huán,
and King Huán entrusted him to the Duke of Zhōu.
Xīn Bó advised, saying:
"Having two queens, matching consorts, dual governance, paired states,
is the root of disorder."
Zhōu Gōng did not follow it,
therefore it extended (to this point).
Zhuāng Gōng
A3.1 *Annals of the First Year of Zhuāng Gōng*
A3.1.1 In the first year, spring,
the king's first month (of the year).
A3.1.2 In the third month,
the Lady Sūn went to Qí.
A3.1.3 In summer,
Shàn Bó escorted the Wang Ji.
A3.1.4 In autumn,
they built the Wang Ji's residence outside (the city).
A3.1.5 In winter, the tenth month, yǐ-hài day,
Marquis Lín of Chén died.
A3.1.6 The King sent Róng Shū to bestow an order upon Duke Huán.
A3.1.7 The Wang Ji returned to Qí.
A3.1.8 The Qí army moved Jǐ Bīng,
Zī, and Wú.
B3.1 *Zhuāng Gōng Yuán Nián Zhuàn*
B3.1.1 In the first year, spring,
not mentioning the enthronement is
because Wén Jiāng left.
B3.1.2 In the third month,
the Lady went to Qí.
Not mentioning the Jiāng clan
shows a severing of ties, not considering her a relative;
this is in accordance with ritual.
B3.1.3 In the autumn,
the guest house for the King's daughter was built outside [the city].
This being "outside"
is in accordance with ritual.
A3.2 *Zhuāng Gōng Èr Nián Jīng*
A3.2.1 In the second year, spring,
in the second month of the King,
Chén Zhuāng Gōng was buried.
A3.2.2 In the summer,
Gōngzǐ Qìngfù led troops to attack Yúqiū.
A3.2.3 In the autumn, the seventh month,
Qí Wáng Jī died.
A3.2.4 In winter, the twelfth month,
the Lady, of the Jiāng clan, met with the Marquis of Qí in Zhuó.
A3.2.5 On yǐ-yǒu day,
Sòng Gōng Féng died.
B3.2 *Zhuāng Gōng Èr Nián Zhuàn*
B3.3 "Zuāng Gōng Three Years' Commentary"
B3.3.1 In the spring of the third year,
Nì joined with the Qí army to attack Wèi;
it was resented.
B3.3.2 In the fifth month of summer,
Huán Wáng was buried;
it was delayed.
B3.3.3 In the autumn,
Jǐ Jì surrendered Xī to Qí;
Jǐ began to split apart from this point on.
B3.3.4 In winter,
the Duke temporarily encamped at Huá,
intending to meet with the Earl of Zhèng
to discuss the matter of Jǐ.
The Earl of Zhèng declined on the grounds of difficulty.
In general, for armies,
one night's stay is called shè (舍),
two nights' stay is called xìn (信),
and staying longer than xìn is called cì (次).
A3.4 "Zuāng Gōng Four Years' Annals"
A3.4.1 In the spring of the fourth year,
in the second month of the King,
the Lady Jiāng entertained the Marquis of Qí at Zhùqiū.
A3.4.2 In the third month,
Bó Jī of Jǐ died.
A3.4.3 In summer, the Marquis of Qí (Qí Hóu), the Marquis of Chén (Chén Hóu), and the Earl of Zhèng (Zhèng Bó) met at Chuí.
A3.4.4 The Marquis of Jǐ (Jǐ Hóu) greatly abandoned his state.
A3.4.5 In the sixth month, on the day yǐchǒu, the Marquis of Qí (Qí Hóu) buried Bó Jī, the wife of the Marquis of Jǐ (Jǐ Bó Jī).
B3.4 *Zuǒ Zhuàn* of the Fourth Year of Duke Zhuāng (Zhuāng Gōng)

B3.4.1 In the fourth year, in spring, in the first month of the King, King Wǔ of Chǔ (Chǔ Wǔ Wáng) died in Jīng, and commanded his army to Jíe, in order to attack Suí. He was about to depart and entered to inform his wife, Dèng Màn, saying, "My heart is agitated." Dèng Màn sighed and said, "The King's fortune is exhausted. To be full and then agitated is the way of Heaven. The former ruler knew this; therefore, when about to engage in military affairs and issue a major command, he agitated the King's heart."
A3.4.6 In autumn, the seventh month.
A3.4.7 In winter, the Duke and the people of Qí (Qí) hunted at Zhuó.
To be full and then to overflow is
the way of Heaven.
Our late lord knew this.
Therefore, when facing military affairs
and about to issue a major command,
he made the king's heart overflow.
If the army and its followers suffer no loss,
and the king dies on the road,
it is a blessing for the state."
The king then proceeded
and died beneath the Mánmù trees.
The Lìngyǐn Dòu Qí and the Mò'áo Qū Zhòng
cleared the roads, bridged the Zhà River,
and encamped the army near Suí.
The people of Suí were afraid
and sued for peace.
The Mò'áo, by the king's command, entered
to make a covenant with the Marquis of Suí,
and requested a meeting at the confluence of the Hàn River,
and then returned.
Only after crossing the Hàn River
was the death announced.
B3.4.2 The Marquis of Jǐ could not subdue Qí
to give it to Jǐ Jì.
In summer,
the Marquis of Jǐ largely abandoned his state,
fleeing the difficulties with Qí.
A3.5 *Annals of the Fifth Year of Duke Zhuāng*
A3.5.1 In the fifth year, in spring,
it was the king's first month.
A3.5.2 In summer,
Fūrén Jiāng Shì went to the army of Qí.
A3.5.3 In autumn,
Ní Lílái came to court.
A3.5.4 In winter,
the duke met with the people of Qí,
the people of Sòng,
the people of Chén,
and the people of Cài to attack Wèi.
B3.5 *Zuāng Gōng* Year 5 Commentary
B3.5.1 In the fifth year, in autumn,
Ní Lílái came to court.
His name was recorded,
but he had not received the king's mandate.
B3.5.2 In winter,
they attacked Wèi
to install Duke Huì.
A3.6 *Zuāng Gōng* Year 6 Annals
A3.6.1 In the sixth year, in spring,
In the first month of the year,
Wáng rén Zǐ Tū rescued Wèi.
A3.6.2 In summer, the sixth month,
Marquis Shuò of Wèi entered Wèi.
A3.6.3 In autumn,
the Duke returned from attacking Wèi.
A3.6.4 There was a plague of locusts.
A3.6.5 In winter,
the people of Qí came to return the captives of Wèi.
B3.6 *Zuǒ Zhuàn*, Year 6 of Duke Zhuāng
B3.6.1 In the spring of the sixth year,
the king's men rescued Wèi.
In summer,
the Marquis of Wèi entered,
exiled Gōngzǐ Qiánmóu to Zhōu,
exiled Níng Guì to Qín,
killed Zuǒ Gōngzǐ Xiè and
Yòu Gōngzǐ Zhí,
and then ascended the throne.
The noble man considers the two lords' installation of Qiánmóu as without measure.
For one who can secure his position
must measure the beginning and the end,
Only then can one establish impartiality.
Without knowing the root,
one does not make plans;
knowing that the root will not branch out,
one does not force it.
The *Book of Poetry* says:
"The root and branches last for a hundred generations."
B3.6.2 In winter,
the people of Qí 齊 came to return the treasures of Wèi 衛,
at the request of Wén Jiāng 文姜.
B3.6.3 King Wén of Chǔ 楚文王 attacked Shēn 申.
He passed through Dèng 鄧.
The Marquis of Dèng 鄧祁侯 said:
"He is my nephew."
He stopped and feasted him.
Zhuī Shēng 騅甥, Dān Shēng 聃甥, and Yǎng Shēng 養甥
requested to kill the Chǔ 楚 ruler.
The Marquis of Dèng 鄧侯 did not allow it.
The three *shēng* said:
"The one who will destroy the state of Dèng 鄧 is
surely this man.
If you do not plan early,
later you will regret it like Qí 齊.
Will you be able to plan then?
If you plan now,
this is the time."
The Marquis of Dèng 鄧侯 said:
"People will not eat my leftovers."
He replied,
"If you do not listen to the three ministers,
then the altars of the state will indeed not receive sacrifices,
and from where will you, the ruler, obtain any surplus?"
He did not listen.
The following year,
the Chǔ ruler attacked Dèng.
In the sixteenth year,
Chǔ again attacked Dèng,
and destroyed it.
A3.7 *Zhuāng Gōng* Year 7 *Jīng*
A3.7.1 In the seventh year, spring,
Lady Jiāng met with the Marquis of Qí at Fáng.
A3.7.2 In summer, the fourth month, *xīn mǎo*,
at night, the constant stars were not seen.
In the middle of the night,
stars fell like rain.
A3.7.3 In autumn,
there was a great flood.
A3.7.4 There was no wheat or
seedlings.
A3.7.5 In winter,
Lady Jiāng met with the Marquis of Qí at Gǔ.
B3.7 Commentary on the 7th Year of Duke Zhuāng
B3.7.1 In the spring of the 7th year,
Wén Jiāng met with the Marquis of Qí at Fáng;
Qí desired it.
B3.7.2 In summer,
the constant stars were not visible;
it was bright at night.
Stars fell like rain;
they came together with the rain.
B3.7.3 In autumn,
there was no wheat
or seedlings;
this did not harm the good grains.
A3.8 The Annals of the 8th Year of Duke Zhuāng
A3.8.1 In the spring of the 8th year,
in the royal first month,
the army encamped at Láng,
in order to wait for the people of Chén and
the people of Cài.
A3.8.2 On Jiǎwǔ,
the army was drilled.
A3.8.3 In summer,
the army and the Qí army besieged Chéng.
Chéng surrendered to the Qí army.
A3.8.4 In autumn,
the army returned.
A3.8.5 In the eleventh month, guǐwèi day, Qí Wúzhī assassinated his lord Zhū'ér.
B3.8 *Zuǒ Zhuàn*, Year 8 of Duke Zhuāng
B3.8.1 In the spring of the eighth year,
drilling troops at the ancestral temple
was proper.
B3.8.2 In summer,
our army and the Qí army besieged Chéng.
Chéng surrendered to the Qí army.
Zhòng Qìngfǔ requested to attack the Qí army.
The Duke said,
"It is not permissible.
Truly, I lack virtue.
What crime has the Qí army committed?
The fault lies with me.
The *Xià Shū* says,
'Gāoyáo diligently cultivated virtue,
when there is virtue,
then blessings descend.'
Let us diligently cultivate virtue
and await the time!"
In autumn,
the army returned.
Therefore, gentlemen praised Duke Zhuāng of Lǔ for this.
B3.8.3 The Marquis of Qí sent Lián Chēng and
Guǎn Zhìfù to garrison Kuíqiū,
going when the melons ripened,
saying:
"Replace them when the melons ripen."
The time for the garrison arrived,
but the duke inquired and they had not arrived.
They requested to be replaced,
but were not permitted.
Therefore, they plotted to rebel.
Duke Xī's younger brother was named Yí Zhòngnián,
who had a grandson named Gōngsūn Wúzhī,
who was favored by Duke Xī,
and whose clothing and ceremonial rank were like that of the heir apparent.
Duke Xiāng demoted him.
The two men (Lián Chēng and Guǎn Zhìfù) used this as a reason to rebel.
Lián Chēng had a younger sister in the duke's palace,
who was not favored.
He sent her to spy on the duke,
saying:
"If you succeed,
I will make you the wife of the duke."
In the twelfth month of winter,
the Marquis of Qí was traveling in Gūfén,
and then hunting in Bèiqiū.
He saw a large pig.
An attendant said,
"It is Gōngzǐ Péngshēng."
The duke was angry
and said,
"Péngshēng dares to appear!"
He shot at it.
The pig stood on its hind legs and squealed.
The duke was frightened
and fell from the chariot.
He injured his foot
and lost his shoe.
Upon returning, he demanded the shoe from the attendant Fèi.
Unable to find it,
he whipped him
until he bled.
Fèi ran out
and encountered a robber at the gate.
He was seized and bound.
Fèi said,
"What can I use to defend myself?"
He bared his back to show them.
They believed him.
Fèi requested to enter first.
He hid the duke and went out,
fought,
and died in the doorway.
Shí zhī Fēnrú died beneath the steps.
Then he entered and
killed Mèng Yáng 孟陽 on the bed.
He said,
"This is not the lord;
he doesn't resemble him."
Seeing Duke Xiāng's 襄公 feet under the door,
he then murdered him
and installed Wú Zhī 無知.
Initially,
when Duke Xiāng 襄公 came to power,
he lacked constancy.
Bào Shūyá 鮑叔牙 said,
"The lord causes the people to be negligent;
disorder will arise."
He escorted Gōngzǐ Xiǎobái 公子小白, the son of the duke, to flee to Jǔ 莒.
When the disorder arose,
Guǎn Yíwú 管夷吾 and Zhào Hū 召忽 escorted Gōngzǐ Jiū 公子糾 to come and seek refuge.
B3.8.4 Initially,
Gōngsūn Wúzhī 公孫無知 was cruel to Yōng Lǐn 雍廩.
A3.9 *Annals of the Ninth Year of Duke Zhuāng 莊公*
A3.9.1 In the spring of the ninth year,
the people of Qí 齊 killed Wú Zhī 無知.
A3.9.2 The duke and the great officers of Qí 齊 made a covenant in Mì 蔇.
A3.9.3 In the summer,
The Duke attacked Qí.
He intended to install Zǐ Jiū.
Qí Xiǎo Bái entered Qí.
A3.9.4 In the seventh month, on the day dīng yǒu,
the funeral of Duke Xiāng of Qí took place.
A3.9.5 In the eighth month, on the day gēng shēn,
we engaged the Qí army in battle at Gānshí,
and our army suffered a crushing defeat.
A3.9.6 In the ninth month,
the people of Qí captured and killed Zǐ Jiū.
A3.9.7 In winter,
the Zhū River was dredged.
B3.9 *Zuǒ Zhuàn*, Ninth Year of Duke Zhuāng
B3.9.1 In the spring of the ninth year,
Yōng Lǐn assassinated Wú Zhī.
B3.9.2 The Duke and the senior officials of Qí formed an alliance at Jì,
as Qí had no ruler.
B3.9.3 In summer,
the Duke attacked Qí,
intending to install Zǐ Jiū.
Duke Huán entered first from Jǔ.
B3.9.4 In autumn,
The Lǔ army and the Qí army fought at Gānshí,
and our army suffered a crushing defeat.
The duke lost his war chariot
and returned by relay carriage.
Qín Zǐ and Liáng Zǐ used the duke's flag
to clear the lower road,
and thus everyone stopped.
B3.9.5 Bào Shū led the army and came to say,
"Zǐ Jiū
is a relative.
Please, my lord, punish him.
Guǎn and Zhào are enemies.
Please let me receive them and be satisfied."
Thereupon, he killed Zǐ Jiū at Shēngdòu.
Zhào Hū died for him.
Guǎn Zhòng requested to be imprisoned.
Bào Shū accepted him,
and released him at Tángfù.
He returned and reported,
"Guǎn Yíwú is superior to Gāo Xī in governance.
It is permissible to make him prime minister."
The duke followed his advice.
A3.10 *The Tenth Year of Duke Zhuāng*
A3.10.1 In the tenth year, in spring,
in the first month of the king,
the duke defeated the Qí army at Chángsháo.
A3.10.2 In the second month,
the Duke attacked Sòng.
A3.10.3 In the third month,
the people of Sòng moved Sù.
A3.10.4 In the summer, the sixth month,
the Qí army and
the Sòng army were stationed at Láng.
The Duke defeated the Sòng army at Chéngqiū.
A3.10.5 In the autumn, the ninth month,
Jīng defeated the Cài army at Shēn,
and took Hóu Wǔ of Cài back as a captive.
A3.10.6 In the winter, the tenth month,
the Qí army extinguished Tán.
Tán Zǐ fled to Jǔ.
B3.10 *Zuāng Gōng, Year Ten, Commentary*
B3.10.1 In the spring of the tenth year,
the Qí army attacked us.
The Duke was about to fight.
Cáo Guì requested an audience.
His fellow villagers said:
"Those who eat meat (the nobles) plan it;
what business is it of yours?"
Guì said:
"Those who eat meat are base
and unable to plan for the distant future."
Thereupon he went in to see the Duke
and asked how to fight.
The Duke said:
"The comfort of clothing and food
I do not dare to monopolize;
I always share with others."
Guì answered:
"Small favors do not extend everywhere;
the people will not follow you."
The Duke said:
"Sacrificial animals and jade and silk
I dare not increase;
I always use them with sincerity."
Guì answered:
"Small sincerity does not inspire confidence;
the spirits will not bless you."
The Duke said:
"In large and small lawsuits,
even though I cannot examine them thoroughly,
I always deal with them according to the facts."
Guì answered:
"This is a matter of loyalty,
and you can fight on that basis.
If you fight,
then please allow me to follow."
The Duke rode in the same chariot with him.
They fought at Chángsháo.
The Duke was about to beat the drum.
Guì said:
"Not yet."
The Qí people beat the drum three times.
Guì said:
"Now you may!"
The Qí army was utterly defeated.
The Duke was about to pursue them.
Guì said:
"Not yet."
He got down
and examined their wheel tracks,
then mounted the carriage bar and looked out at them,
saying:
"Now you may!"
Thereupon they pursued the Qí army.
After they had won,
the Duke asked him the reason.
He replied:
"In battle, courage is everything.
The first drumbeat rouses the troops' courage,
the second diminishes it,
and the third exhausts it.
When their courage was exhausted and ours was full,
therefore we defeated them.
Moreover, a large state
It is difficult to fathom,
I feared there was an ambush.
I saw that their wheel tracks were disordered,
I observed that their flags were falling,
therefore I pursued them."
B3.10.2 In the sixth month of summer,
the Qí 齊 army and the Sòng 宋 army were stationed at Láng 郎.
Gōngzǐ Yǎn 公子偃 said:
"The Sòng 宋 army is not well-disciplined,
it can be defeated.
If Sòng 宋 is defeated,
Qí 齊 will surely return.
I request to attack them."
The Duke did not permit it.
He secretly went out from the Yú Mén 雩門,
covered in tiger skin and charged ahead to attack them.
The Duke followed him,
and greatly defeated the Sòng 宋 army at Chéngqiū 乘丘.
The Qí 齊 army then returned.
B3.10.3 Marquis Āi of Cài 蔡哀侯 married a woman from Chén 陳,
Marquis Xī 息侯 also married her.
As Lady Xī Guī 息媯 was returning [to her husband's state],
she passed through Cài 蔡.
The Marquis of Cài 蔡 said:
"She is my wife's sister."
He stopped her and met with her,
but did not treat her as a guest.
Marquis Xī 息侯 heard of this,
Enraged,
he sent word to King Wén of Chǔ, saying:
"If you attack me,
I will seek aid from Cài and then attack them."
The Chǔ ruler followed his advice.
In the ninth month of autumn,
Chǔ defeated the Cài army at Shēn,
and returned with the Marquis of Cài, Xiàn Wǔ, as a captive.
B3.10.4 When the Marquis of Qí was leaving,
he passed through Tán,
but Tán did not treat him with proper courtesy.
And when he returned,
all the lords offered congratulations,
but Tán still did not come.
In winter,
the Qí army destroyed Tán,
because Tán was disrespectful.
The ruler of Tán fled to Jǔ,
due to their former alliance.
A3.11 *Annals of the Eleventh Year of Duke Zhuāng*
A3.11.1 In the eleventh year, spring,
the king's first month.
A3.11.2 In summer, the fifth month,
on the day wù-yín,
the Duke defeated the Sòng army at Zī.
A3.11.3 In autumn,
there was a great flood in Sòng.
A3.11.4 In winter,
the King's daughter was married off to Qí.
B3.11 *Commentary on the Eleventh Year of Zhuāng Gōng*
B3.11.1 In the summer of the eleventh year,
Sòng, because of the incident at Chéngqiū,
invaded us.
The Duke defended against them.
The Sòng army had not yet formed ranks when we pressed them,
defeating them at Zī.
In all military matters,
if the enemy has not formed ranks, it is called
"defeating a certain army";
if they have all formed ranks, it is called "battle";
a great collapse is called "a crushing defeat."
Capturing leaders is called "a victory";
utterly defeating them is called "capturing a certain army";
if the capital's army is defeated, it is called
"the King's army suffered a crushing defeat at such-and-such place."
B3.11.2 In autumn,
Sòng was flooded.
The Duke sent someone to express condolences,
saying:
"Heaven sends excessive rain,
He was harmed by the sacrificial offerings.
How can he not be pitied?"
He replied,
"Indeed, I, the orphaned one, was disrespectful.
Heaven sent down this disaster,
and I further caused worry for the ruler.
I accept the disgrace of the commission."
Zāng Wénzhòng 曰:
"Sòng is probably going to rise!
Yǔ and Tāng blamed themselves for their faults,
and their rise was swift.
Jié and Zhòu blamed others,
and their fall was sudden.
Moreover, when a state has misfortune,
to call oneself 'the orphaned one'
is proper.
He speaks with fear and acts with propriety,
Qí shù hū!”
Shortly afterwards, it was heard that:
“This is the speech of Gōngzǐ Yùyuē.”
Zāngsūn Dá said:
“He is fit to be the ruler,
he has a heart that cares for the people.”
B3.11.3 In winter,
the Marquis of Qí came to welcome Gòng Jī.
B3.11.4 In the Battle of Chéngqiū,
the Duke used the gold púgū to shoot Nángōng Chángwàn,
the Duke's right-hand man Zhuǎn Sūnshēng grappled with him.
The people of Sòng requested him.
Duke of Sòng begrudged him,
saying:
“At first, I respected you;
now you
are a prisoner of Lǔ,
He encountered the Grand Steward Dū west of the East Palace
and killed him.
He installed Zǐ Yóu.
The numerous sons of the Duke fled to Xiāo.
Duke's son Yù Shuō fled to Bó.
Nángōng Niú and
Měng Huò led troops to besiege Bó.
In the tenth month of winter,
Xiāo Shū Dàxīn, along with the lineages of Dài, Wǔ, Xuān, Mù, and Zhuāng,
attacked it with the army of Cáo.
They killed Nángōng Niú in the army.
They killed Zǐ Yóu in Sòng and
installed Duke Huán.
Měng Huò fled to Wèi.
Nángōng Wàn fled to Chén,
using a cart to transport his mother,
arriving in a single day.
The people of Sòng requested Měng Huò from Wèi.
The people of Wèi were unwilling to give him up.
Shí Qízi said:
"That is not acceptable.
The evils of the world are all the same.
If he is hated in Sòng but protected by us,
what good does protecting him do?
To gain one man and lose a country,
to associate with evil and abandon goodness,
is not a wise plan."
The people of Wèi returned him.
They also invited Nángōng Wàn from Chén
to bribe them.
The people of Chén had women give him wine to drink,
and then wrapped him in rhinoceros hide.
By the time they reached Sòng,
his hands and feet were all visible.
The people of Sòng all minced him.
A3.13 *Annals of the Thirteenth Year of Duke Zhuāng*
A3.13.1 In the spring of the thirteenth year,
the Marquis of Qí,
the people of Sòng,
the people of Chén,
the people of Cài,
and the people of Zhū met at Běixìng.
A3.13.2 In the sixth month, summer,
the people of Qí extinguished Suì.
A3.13.3 In the seventh month, autumn.
A3.13.4 In winter,
the Duke met with the Marquis of Qí and made a covenant at Kē.
B3.13 *Commentary on the Thirteenth Year of Duke Zhuāng*
B3.13.1 In the spring of the thirteenth year,
they met at Běixìng,
In order to pacify the disturbances in Sòng.
Consequently, the people of Suì did not arrive.
In summer,
the people of Qí destroyed Suì and garrisoned it.
B3.13.2 In winter,
they made a covenant at Kē,
and only then did they achieve peace with Qí.
B3.13.3 The people of Sòng reneged on the meeting at Běixìng.
A3.14 *The Annals of the Fourteenth Year of Duke Zhuāng*
A3.14.1 In the spring of the fourteenth year,
the people of Qí,
the people of Chén,
and the people of Cáo attacked Sòng.
A3.14.2 In summer,
Shàn Bó convened a meeting to attack Sòng.
A3.14.3 In the seventh month of autumn,
Jīng invaded Cài.
A3.14.4 In winter,
Shàn Bó convened a meeting with the Marquis of Qí,
the Duke of Sòng,
the Marquis of Wèi,
and the Count of Zhèng at Juàn.
B3.14 *The Commentary on the Fourteenth Year of Duke Zhuāng*
B3.14.1 In the spring of the fourteenth year,
the lords attacked Sòng.
Qí requested troops from Zhōu.
In summer,
Dān Bó met with them.
They obtained an agreement from Sòng and returned.
B3.14.2 Duke Lì of Zhèng invaded Zhèng from Lì,
reaching Dàlíng,
and captured Fù Xiá.
Fù Xiá said:
"If you release me,
I will invite the ruler back."
They made a covenant with him and pardoned him.
On the jǐa-zǐ day of the sixth month,
Fù Xiá killed Zǐ of Zhèng and his two sons,
and invited Duke Lì back.
Initially,
an inner snake and an outer snake fought in the middle of the south gate of Zhèng,
and the inner snake died.
Six years later, Duke Lì entered.
The Duke heard of this
and asked Shēn Xū:
"Is there still a portent?"
He replied:
"What people dread,
their spirit takes advantage of it.
Portents arise from people.
If people have no flaws,
then monsters will not arise on their own.
If people abandon constancy,
then monsters will flourish,
therefore there are monsters."
Lì Gōng entered,
and then killed Fù Xiá.
He had someone tell Yuán Fán,
"Fù Xiá was disloyal.
Zhōu has a standing punishment for that,
and he has already been made to confess his crime.
Those who accepted me without any disloyalty,
I all promised them the duties of a senior official.
I wish to discuss this with you, my uncle.
Moreover, when I was in exile,
my uncle did not offer any support.
And upon my return,
you did not think of me,
I regret that."
Yuán Fán replied,
"Our former ruler, Duke Huán, ordered my ancestors to manage the ancestral tablets.
If the state has a ruler,
yet one's heart is turned outwards,
what disloyalty could be greater than that?
If one serves the state,
the people within the country,
who among them would not be a subject?
That I have no disloyal intentions
This is Heaven's decree.
Zǐ Yí has been in office
for fourteen years already;
and for those who plot to summon the ruler,
are there not perhaps two?
Of Duke Zhuāng's sons, there are still eight people,
if all use official positions and noble titles to offer bribes and encourage disloyalty,
and can accomplish their goals,
what will become of the ruler?
Your servant has received your command."
Then he hanged himself and died.
B3.14.3 Marquis Āi of Cài, because of the grudge over Shēn,
used rope to tie up Xī Guī and spoke of her to the ruler of Chǔ.
The ruler of Chǔ went to Xī,
using a feast as an entry to enjoy her,
and subsequently destroyed Xī.
He returned with Xī Guī,
who gave birth to Dǔ Áo and King Chéng.
She did not speak.
The ruler of Chǔ asked her.
She replied,
"I am but one woman,
who served two husbands,
even if I could not die,
what more can I say?"
The ruler of Chǔ, because the Marquis of Cài had destroyed Xī,
then attacked Cài.
In the seventh month of autumn,
Chǔ entered Cài.
The gentleman said:
"What the *Shāng Shū* calls
'Evil is easy to spread,
like a fire blazing across the plains,
it cannot be approached or drawn near,
yet it can still be extinguished,'
that is probably what happened to Āi Hóu of Cài!"
In winter,
there was a meeting at Juàn;
Sòng restored its former status.
In the fifteenth year, spring,
the Marquis of Qí,
the Duke of Sòng,
the Marquis of Chén,
the Marquis of Wèi,
and the Count of Zhèng met at Juàn.
In summer,
Lady Jiāng went to Qí.
In autumn,
the people of Sòng,
the people of Qí,
and the people of Zhū attacked Ní.
A3.15.4 The people of Zhèng invaded Sòng.
A3.15.5 Tenth month, winter.
B3.15 *Commentary on Year Fifteen of Duke Zhuāng*
B3.15.1 Fifteenth year, spring,
they met again there.
Qí began to be the hegemon.
B3.15.2 Autumn,
the lords attacked Ní on behalf of Sòng.
The people of Zhèng took advantage of this opportunity to invade Sòng.
A3.16 *Annals of Year Sixteen of Duke Zhuāng*
A3.16.1 Sixteenth year, spring,
first month of the king.
A3.16.2 Summer,
the people of Sòng,
the people of Qí,
the people of Wèi attacked Zhèng.
A3.16.3 Autumn,
Jīng attacked Zhèng.
A3.16.4 Twelfth month, winter,
the Marquis of Qí,
Sòng Gōng (宋公),
Chén Hóu (陳侯),
Wèi Hóu (衛侯),
Zhèng Bó (鄭伯),
Xǔ Nán (許男),
Huá Bó (滑伯),
and Téng Zǐ (滕子) formed an alliance at Yōu (幽).
A3.16.5 Zhū Zǐ Kè (邾子克) died.
B3.16 *Commentary on the Sixteenth Year of Duke Zhuāng* (莊公十六年傳)
B3.16.1 In the summer of the sixteenth year,
the lords attacked Zhèng (鄭)
because of Sòng (宋).
B3.16.2 The Zhèng Bó (鄭伯) entered from Lì (櫟) and
sent a slow report to Chǔ (楚).
In autumn,
Chǔ (楚) attacked Zhèng (鄭),
reaching Lì (櫟),
because of disrespect.
B3.16.3 The Zhèng Bó (鄭伯) punished those involved in the rebellion of Yōng Jiū (雍糾).
In the ninth month,
he killed Gōngzǐ È (公子閼)
and cut off the feet of Qiáng Chú (強鉏).
Gōngfù Dìngshū (公父定叔) fled to Wèi (衛).
After three years, he was restored,
saying:
"It is not permissible to allow Gòngshū to have no heir in Zhèng."
He was made to enter in the tenth month,
saying,
"It is an auspicious month;
let him complete the full number of months."
The gentleman said that Qiáng Chú
was unable to protect his feet.
B3.16.4 In winter,
they formed an alliance at Yōu;
it was Zhèng's accomplishment.
B3.16.5 The king sent the Duke of Guó to appoint the Earl of Qūwò
with one army to be the Marquis of Jìn.
B3.16.6 Initially,
Duke Wǔ of Jìn attacked Yí,
capturing Yí Guǐzhū.
Wěi Guó pleaded and released him.
Afterwards, he did not repay (the favor),
therefore Zǐ Guó instigated a rebellion,
saying to the people of Jìn,
"Attack Yí with me and take its land."
Consequently, he used the army of Jìn to attack Yí,
killing Yí Guǐzhū.
Zhōu Gōng Jìfù fled to Guó.
King Huì ascended the throne and reinstated him.
A3.17 *The 17th Year of Duke Zhuāng*
A3.17.1 In the spring of the seventeenth year,
the people of Qí captured Zhèng Zhān.
A3.17.2 In summer, the people of Qí were annihilated in Suì.
A3.17.3 In autumn, Zhèng Zhān fled from Qí and came here.
A3.17.4 In winter, there were many milu deer.
B3.17 *Commentary on the Seventeenth Year of Duke Zhuāng*
B3.17.1 In the spring of the seventeenth year, the people of Qí arrested Zhèng Zhān because Zhèng did not attend court.
B3.17.2 In summer, the Suì Yīn clan, the Hé clan, the Gōng Lóu clan, and the Xū Suì clan feasted the garrison of Qí. They got them drunk and killed them. The people of Qí were annihilated there.
A3.18 *Annals of the Eighteenth Year of Duke Zhuāng*
A3.18.1 In the spring of the eighteenth year, the third month of the king, there was a solar eclipse.
A3.18.2 In summer, the Duke pursued the Róng to the west of the Jì River.
A3.18.2 In summer,
the Duke pursued the Róng people to the west of the Jǐ River.
A3.18.3 In autumn,
there were yù (a kind of water monster).
A3.18.4 In winter, the tenth month.
B3.18 *Commentary on the Eighteenth Year of Duke Zhuāng*
B3.18.1 In the spring of the eighteenth year, Guó Gōng and Jìn Hóu paid court to the King.
The King treated them to sweet wine and ordered them to be pardoned (granted leniency).
Each was granted five *jue* of jade and four horses,
which was not in accordance with ritual.
When the King commands the feudal lords,
their titles and positions are different,
so the ritual offerings should also be of different numbers,
and one should not lend ritual to others.
B3.18.2 Guó Gōng, Jìn Hóu, and Zhèng Bó sent Yuán Zhuāng Gōng to escort the Queen back from Chén.
Chén Guī returned to the capital,
as the true Huì Hòu (Queen Huì).
B3.18.3 In summer,
the Duke pursued the Róng people to the west of the Jǐ River.
because it is taboo (to speak of it).
B3.18.4 In autumn,
there were *yù* (a kind of water sprite said to cause disease),
it was a disaster.
B3.18.5 Initially,
Chǔ Wǔwáng conquered Quán,
and sent Dòu Mín to govern it.
He rebelled,
was besieged and killed.
He moved Quán to Nàchù,
and sent Yán Áo to govern it.
When Wén Wáng ascended the throne,
he attacked Shēn with the Bā people,
and alarmed their army.
The Bā people rebelled against Chǔ and attacked Nàchù,
captured it,
and then encamped at the gate of Chǔ.
Yán Áo swam and escaped.
The Chǔ ruler killed him.
His clan caused disorder.
In winter,
the Bā people took advantage of this to attack Chǔ.
A3.19 "The Annals of the Nineteenth Year of Lord Zhuāng"
A3.19.1 In the nineteenth year, in spring,
the royal first month.
A3.19.2 In the fourth month of summer.
A3.19.3 In autumn,
Gōngzǐ Jié married off a Chén woman at Juàn,
and consequently formed an alliance with the Marquis of Qí and
Duke of Sòng.
A3.19.4 Lady Jiāngshì went to Jǔ.
A3.19.5 In winter,
the people of Qí,
the people of Sòng,
and the people of Chén attacked our western borders.
B3.19 *Commentary on the Nineteenth Year of Duke Zhuāng*
B3.19.1 In the spring of the nineteenth year,
the Viscount of Chǔ resisted them and was
greatly defeated at Jīn.
Returning,
Yùquán would not let him enter,
and so he attacked Huáng.
He defeated the Huáng army at Jílíng.
Returning,
when he reached Qiū,
he fell ill.
On the day Gēngshēn in the sixth month of summer,
he died.
Yù Quán was buried in the side chamber.
He also committed suicide
and was buried in Zhìhuáng.
Initially,
Yù Quán strongly advised the ruler of Chǔ.
The ruler of Chǔ did not listen.
He threatened him with soldiers,
and he obeyed out of fear.
Yù Quán said,
"I made the ruler fear me with soldiers;
there is no greater crime."
Thereupon he castrated himself.
The people of Chǔ made him a chief gatekeeper,
calling him Dà Bó.
They had his descendants manage it.
A gentleman said,
"Yù Quán can be said to have loved his ruler:
He advised him by subjecting himself to punishment,
and even in punishment he did not forget to guide his ruler towards goodness."
B3.19.2 Initially,
Wáng Yáo was favored by King Zhuāng,
and gave birth to Zǐ Tuí.
Zǐ Tuí was favored,
and Wěi Guó became his tutor.
When King Huì ascended the throne,
he took Wěi Guó's garden to make it a hunting park.
Biān Bó's palace was near the royal palace,
and the king took it.
The King seized the fields of Zǐ Qín Zhù Guì and Zhān Fù,
and also confiscated the emolument of the Chief Cook.
Therefore, Wěi Guó, Biān Bó, Shí Sù, Zhān Fù, and Zǐ Qín Zhù Guì started a rebellion,
relying on the Sū clan.
In the autumn,
the five grand officers supported Zǐ Tuí to attack the King,
but were unsuccessful,
and fled to Wēn.
Sū Zǐ supported Zǐ Tuí and fled to Wèi.
The army of Wèi and
the army of Yān attacked Zhōu.
In the winter,
Zǐ Tuí was enthroned.
A3.20 "Annals of the Twentieth Year of Duke Zhuāng"
A3.20.1 In the spring of the twentieth year,
in the second month of the King,
Lady Jiāng of the Consort went to Jǔ.
A3.20.2 In the summer,
Qí suffered a great disaster.
A3.20.3 In the autumn, the seventh month.
A3.20.4 In the winter,
the people of Qí attacked the Róng.
B3.20 "Commentary on the Twentieth Year of Duke Zhuāng"
B3.20.1 In the spring of the twentieth year,
the Zhèng Bó and the royal house
could not reconcile.
They captured Yàn Zhòngfù.
In summer,
the Zhèng Bó then escorted the king back.
The king resided at Lì.
In autumn,
the king and the Zhèng Bó entered Wū.
They then entered Chéngzhōu,
seized its treasures and returned.
In winter,
Prince Tuí entertained the five grand officers,
with music and all kinds of dances.
The Zhèng Bó heard of this,
and met with Guó Shū, saying:
"I have heard that:
if sorrow and joy are out of season,
calamity and misfortune will surely come.
Now Prince Tuí sings and dances tirelessly,
he is delighting in disaster!
When the Minister of Justice carries out executions,
the ruler refrains from holding celebrations,
how much more should he dare to delight in disaster?
Usurping the king's position,
what disaster could be greater?
Facing disaster and forgetting worry,
worry will surely reach you.
Why not accept the king!"
Guó Gōng said:
"It is my wish."
A3.21 *Zhuāng Gōng* Year 21 *Jīng*
A3.21.1 In the spring of the twenty-first year,
it was the king's first month.
A3.21.2 In the fifth month, on the day *xīnyǒu*,
Bó Tū of Zhèng died.
A3.21.3 In the seventh month, on the day *wùxū*,
Lady Jiāng Shì passed away.
A3.21.4 In the twelfth month,
Lì Gōng of Zhèng was buried.
B3.21 *Zhuāng Gōng* Year 21 *Zhuàn*
B3.21.1 In the spring of the twenty-first year,
there was the announcement of the agreement at Mǐ.
In summer,
they jointly attacked Wángchéng.
The Count of Zhèng escorted the king in through the Yǔ Gate.
Shū of Guó entered through the North Gate.
They killed Prince Tuí and five senior officials.
Zhèng Bó entertained the king at the western outskirts of Quē,
and the music was complete.
The king gave him the plans of Wǔ Gōng,
from Hǔláo eastward.
Yuán Bó said,
"Zhèng Bó is imitating,
he will also have misfortune."
In the fifth month,
Duke Lì of Zhèng died.
The king inspected the defense of Guó.
The Duke of Guó built a palace for the king at Bàng.
The king gave him Jiǔquán.
When the Zhèng Bó entertained the king,
the king gave him the queen's pánjiàn.
The Duke of Guó requested vessels,
and the king gave him a jué (wine cup).
From this, the Zhèng Bó began to be disliked by the king.
In winter,
the king returned from Guó.
A3.22 *Zhuāng Gōng's 22nd Year Chronicle*
A3.22.1 In the twenty-second year, in spring,
in the king's first month,
they performed a grand sacrifice to avert calamities.
A3.22.2 On guǐchǒu,
they buried my lesser ruler, Wén Jiāng.
A3.22.3 The people of Chén killed their young master Yù Kòu.
A3.22.4 Summer, fifth month.
A3.22.5 Autumn, seventh month, bǐng-shēn day,
(Duke Huán of Lǔ) made a covenant with Gāo Xī of Qí at Fáng.
A3.22.6 Winter,
the Duke went to Qí to offer betrothal gifts.
B3.22 *Zuǒ Zhuàn*, Twenty-second Year of Duke Zhuāng
B3.22.1 In the spring of the twenty-second year,
the people of Chén killed their crown prince Yù Kòu.
The Chén prince Wán and Zhuān-sūn fled to Qí.
Zhuān-sūn fled from Qí to (Lǔ).
The Marquis of Qí wanted to make Jìng Zhòng a minister.
He declined, saying:
"As a stranger and exile, I am fortunate to receive leniency,
and to benefit from benevolent governance,
to be excused from my unfamiliarity with instruction
and to be spared from punishment,
to be freed from burdens—
this is your kindness, my lord.
What I have received is already much.
How dare I disgrace a high position
and invite public criticism?
Please allow me to refuse with my death.
The *Book of Poetry* says,
"High and grand are the chariots,
beckoning me with bows.
Is it that I do not wish to go?
I fear my friends."
He was made the head of the artisans (*gōngzhèng*).
Drinking wine with Duke Huán,
he was enjoying himself.
The Duke said,
"Continue it with light."
He declined, saying,
"Your servant divined for the day,
but did not divine for the night;
I dare not."
The gentleman said,
"Wine is for accomplishing rites,
not continuing with licentiousness;
this is righteousness (*yì*).
Using the ruler to accomplish rites,
not admitting him to licentiousness,
this is benevolence (*rén*)."
Initially,
the Yì Shì clan divined about taking Jìngzhòng as a wife.
His wife divined about it,
and said,
"Auspicious.
It is said,
'The phoenix flies,
Harmonious sounds, clang clang.
A descendant of Yǒu Guī,
will be born into the Jiāng clan.
For five generations, he will prosper,
and be equal to a chief minister.
After eight generations,
none will compare to his capital.'"
Duke Lì of Chén,
came from Cài,
therefore, the people of Cài killed Wǔ Fǔ
and installed him.
He fathered Jìng Zhòng.
When he was young,
a Zhou historian came to see the Marquis of Chén with the *Zhou Yi*,
the Marquis of Chén had him divine;
he obtained "Contemplation" ䷓ changing to "Obstruction" ䷋,
and said:
"This is called
'Contemplating the light of the state,
it is advantageous to be a guest at the royal court.'
Will he replace Chén to possess the state?
If not in this place,
it will be in another state;
if not in his own person,
it will be in his descendants.
Light,
is far away and shines from elsewhere.
"Kūn"
represents earth;
"Xùn"
represents wind;
"Qián"
represents heaven;
wind becomes heaven; upon the earth,
it is a mountain.
Having materials from the mountain,
and illuminating it with the light of heaven,
therefore it resides upon the earth,
hence it is said,
"Contemplate the glory of the kingdom,
it is beneficial to be a guest at the royal court."
A courtyard filled with a hundred troops,
presenting them with jade and silk,
the beauty of heaven and earth is fully present therein,
hence it is said,
"It is beneficial to be a guest at the royal court."
It still has observation,
therefore it is said that it is in the rear!
The wind travels and becomes manifest on the earth,
therefore it is said that it is in a foreign land!
If it is in a foreign land,
it must be of the Jiāng surname.
Jiāng
is the descendant of Dàyuè.
Mountains and great peaks are paired with heaven.
Nothing can be great in two ways.
When Chén 衰 (shuāi) declines,
will this be its flourishing?"
When Chén first perished,
Chén Huánzǐ 陈桓子 began to become greater than Qí;
after its subsequent demise,
Chéngzǐ 成子 gained power.
A3.23 *Zhuāng Gōng* Year 23 *Jīng*
A3.23.1 In the spring of the twenty-third year,
the Duke arrived from Qí.
A3.23.2 Jì Shū 祭叔 came to pay a formal visit.
A3.23.3 In summer,
the Duke went to Qí to observe the *shè* sacrifice.
A3.23.4 The Duke arrived from Qí.
A3.23.5 The Jīng people came to pay a formal visit.
A3.23.6 The Duke and the Marquis of Qí met at Gǔ.
A3.23.7 Xiāo Shū 萧叔 paid court to the Duke.
A3.23.8 In autumn,
the pillars of the Dān Huán Palace were painted red.
A3.23.9 In the eleventh month of winter,
Bó (伯) Shègū (射姑), the ruler of Cáo (曹), died.
A3.23.10 In the twelfth month, on the day jiǎyín (甲寅),
the Duke met with the Marquis of Qí (齊) and formed an alliance at Hù (扈).
B3.23 *Zuǒ Zhuàn* (左傳), Year 23 of Duke Zhuāng (莊公)
B3.23.1 In the summer of the twenty-third year,
the Duke went to Qí (齊) to observe the shè (社) festival,
which was contrary to ritual propriety.
Cáo Guì (曹劌) admonished him, saying:
"It is not permissible.
Ritual propriety
is that by which the people are regulated.
Therefore, assemblies
are held to instruct in the principles governing superiors and inferiors,
and to establish limits on the use of resources;
audiences are held to rectify the meanings of ranks and dignities,
and to guide the order of elders and juniors;
military expeditions are undertaken to punish those who act contrary to these principles.
The feudal lords have the King,
and the King has his tours of inspection,
in order to practice these things on a grand scale.
If it is not for these purposes,
the ruler should not undertake such actions.
When the ruler undertakes an action, it must be recorded;
if the record is not in accordance with the law,
"What about a successor?"
B3.23.2 The clans of Duke Huán 桓 and Duke Zhuāng 莊 of Jìn 晉 were oppressive,
and Duke Xiàn 獻公 was troubled by them.
Shì Wěi 士蒍 said,
"If you remove Fù Zǐ 富子,
then plans can be made against the other sons of the duke."
The Duke said,
"You may try this matter."
Shì Wěi 士蒍 plotted with the other sons of the duke,
slandered Fù Zǐ 富子, and had him removed.
B3.23.3 In the autumn,
the pillars of the Huán 桓 Palace were painted red.
A3.24 *The Classic of the 24th Year of Duke Zhuāng*
A3.24.1 In the spring of the twenty-fourth year,
in the third month of the King,
the rafters of the Huán 桓 Palace were carved.
A3.24.2 The Viscount Zhuāng 莊 of Cáo 曹 was buried.
A3.24.3 In the summer,
the Duke went to Qí 齊 to welcome the daughter.
A3.24.4 In the autumn,
the Duke returned from Qí 齊.
A3.24.5 On the day dīngchǒu 丁丑 of the eighth month,
the Lady Jiāng 姜氏 entered.
A3.24.6 On the day of wù-yín, the wives of the senior officials were presented (to the court), using gifts.

B3.24 "Commentary on the Twenty-Fourth Year of Duke Zhuāng"
B3.24.1 In the spring of the twenty-fourth year, to carve the rafters, all of this was not in accordance with ritual.
Yù Sūn remonstrated, saying: "I have heard it said: 'Frugality and virtue are shared; extravagance and evil are great.'
The former lord possessed shared virtue, but you, my lord, are embracing great evil. Is this not unacceptable?"
But if you, my lord, include her among the greatest evils,
would that not be inappropriate?"
B3.24.2 In autumn,
Āi Jiāng arrived.
The Duke ordered the women of the ducal clan to meet her,
using gifts of silk.
This was contrary to propriety.
Yù Sūn said:
"A man's gifts
are, for greater items, jade and silk,
and for smaller items, birds,
to display their value.
A woman's gifts
do not exceed hazelnuts, chestnuts, dates, and dried meat,
to show reverence.
Now, men and women offer the same gifts,
which shows no distinction.
The distinction between men and women
is a great principle of the state;
and if the First Lady disrupts it,
would that not be inappropriate?"

Ritual, music, compassion, and love

He then married two women from the Róng people. Dà Róng Hú Jī gave birth to Chóng'ěr, and Xiǎo Róng Zǐ gave birth to Yíwú.
Jìn attacked the Lí Róng. The Lí Róng presented Lí Jī, both male and female,
as a gift.

Pú and Èr Qū

is the ancestral land of Your Lordship.
are the borders of Your Lordship.

and Chóng'ěr
and Yíwú rule Pú and Qū,

They made them all say,

The people of Zhèng were about to flee to Tóngqiū,

So they stopped.

"What is the reason for this?"
He replied, saying:
"When a state is about to rise,
a bright god descends,
to oversee its virtue;
when it is about to perish,
a god also descends,
to observe its wickedness.
Therefore, there are those who have obtained the favor of gods and prospered,
and there are also those who have perished because of it;
Yú, Xià,
Shāng, and Zhōu all had this."
The king said:
"What should be done?"
He replied:
"Offer it the things that it desires.
On the day of its arrival,
also offer it those things."
The king followed his advice.
Nèishǐ (內史), passing by,

and returning, said:
"Guó (虢) is sure to perish!
Cruel and tyrannical, yet listening to the gods."
The god resided in Shēn (莘) for six months.
The Guó (虢) ruler sent Zhù Yīng (祝應), Zōng Qū (宗區), and Shǐ Yín (史嚚) to offer sacrifices.

Shǐ Yín (史嚚) said:
"Guó (虢) is doomed to perish!
I have heard it said:
When a state is about to rise,
it listens to the people;
when it is about to perish,
it listens to the gods.
The gods,
being intelligent, discerning, upright, and unified,
act according to the people.
Guó (虢) is full of deficient virtue;
what land can it possibly obtain?"

If Heaven blesses the Grandson,

Bǔ Yǎn said:
"The descendants of Bì Wàn will surely be great.
*Wàn*

*Wèi*
means 'great name.'
To begin rewarding with this,
Heaven is initiating it.
The Son of Heaven calls them 'myriad people,'

Now his name is great,
to conform to the full number,
he will surely have a multitude."
Initially,
Bì Wàn divined about serving in Jin,
and encountered 《Tún》䷂ changing to 《Bǐ》
Xīn Liào interpreted it,
saying:
"Auspicious.
《Tún》 means solidity, 《Bǐ》 means entering,

《Zhèn》 is earth,
carriages follow horses,
Sufficient to dwell in,
eldest brother to it,
mother protects it,
the multitude returns to it,
the six limbs do not change,
united they can be secure,
at peace they can kill,

A4.2 "The Classic of the Second Year of Duke Mǐn"
A4.2.1 In the spring of the second year,
the king's first month,
the people of Qí moved to Yáng.
A4.2.2 In the summer, in the fifth month, on yǐ yǒu day,
there was a propitious grand sacrifice to Duke Zhuāng.
A4.2.3 In the autumn, in the eighth month, on xīn chǒu day,
the duke died.
A4.2.4 In the ninth month,
Lady Jiāng paid a visit to Zhū.
A4.2.5 Gōngzǐ Qìngfù fled to Jǔ.
A4.2.6 In winter,
Qí Gāozi came to form an alliance.
A4.2.7 In the twelfth month,
the Di barbarians invaded Wèi.
A4.2.8 Zhèng abandoned its army.
B4.2 "The Commentary on the Second Year of Duke Mǐn"
B4.2.1 In the spring of the second year,
the Duke of Guó defeated the Quǎnróng at the bend of the Wèi River.
Zhōu zhī Qiáo said:
"To have emolument without virtue
is a disaster.
Disaster will arrive soon."
Thereupon, he fled to Jìn.
B4.2.2 In the summer,
he hastily performed the great di sacrifice to Duke Zhuāng.
It was done hastily.
B4.2.3 Initially,
the duke's tutor seized the fields of Bǔ Yǐ,
and the duke did not prohibit it.
In the eighth month, on the day xīn chǒu,
Gòng Zhòng had Bǔ Yǐ assassinate the duke at the gate of Wǔ.
Chéng Jì accompanied Duke Xī to Zhū.
Gòng Zhòng fled to Jǔ.
Then they entered and
installed him.
He sought Gòng Zhòng from Jǔ with bribes,
and the people of Jǔ returned him.
When he reached Mì,
he sent Gōngzǐ Yú to request an audience.
He was not permitted,
so he went weeping.
Gòng Zhòng said:
"That is the voice of Xī Sī."
Thereupon, he hanged himself.
Duke Mǐn,
was the son of Shū Jiāng, the younger sister of Āi Jiāng,
therefore the people of Qí installed him.
Gòng Zhòng had illicit relations with Āi Jiāng,
and Āi Jiāng desired to establish him.
In the death of Duke Mǐn,
Āi Jiāng was complicit,
so she fled to Zhū.
The people of Qí seized her and killed her in Yí,
and returned with her corpse,
Duke Xī requested it and buried her.
B4.2.4 When Chéng Jì was about to be born,
Duke Huán sent the father of the diviner Chǔ Qiū
to divine it,
saying:
"It will be a boy,
his name will be Yǒu,
he will be at the ruler's right hand;
intervening between the two altars of the soil,
He will be an assistant to the ducal house.
If the Jì clan perishes,
then Lǔ will not prosper."
They divined again,
and obtained 《Dà Yǒu》 ䷍ changing to 《Qián》
䷀ which said:
"Together they return to the father,
showing respect as the ruler desires."
When he was born,
there was a character on his hand that said "Friend,"
so he was named accordingly.
B4.2.5 In the twelfth month of winter,
the Dí people attacked Wèi.
Duke Yì of Wèi loved cranes,
and some cranes had carriages.
When they were about to fight,
the people receiving armor all said:
"Send the cranes!
The cranes actually have salaries and ranks,
how can we fight?"
The Duke gave Shí Qízǐ a jade pendant,
and gave Níng Zhuāngzǐ arrows,
and made them guard,
saying:
"Use these to assist the state,
and choose what is beneficial to do."
He gave his wife embroidered clothing,
saying:
「Tīng yú èr zi!」"Listen to these two sons!"
Qú Kǒng yù róng,

Chū,

The people of Qi had Zhao Bo commit incest with Xuan Jiang;
he refused;
they forced him.

Duke Wen, because of the many troubles of Wei,
first went to Qi.
When the state was defeated,
Duke Huan of Song met him at the River,
crossing it at night.
Of the remnant people of Wei, there were seven hundred and thirty men and women;
adding the people of Gong
and Teng,
there were five thousand people.
They established Duke Dai to reside at Cao.
Lady Mu of Xu composed the poem "Zai Chi".
The Marquis of Qi sent Gongzi Wu Kui to lead three hundred chariots,
and three thousand armored soldiers to garrison Cao.
They returned to the duke a chariot team, five sets of ceremonial robes, and three hundred each of cattle, sheep, pigs, chickens, and dogs, as well as door materials.
They returned to the lady a fish carriage and sixty jin of heavy brocade.
B4.2.6 The people of Zheng hated Gao Ke,
so they had him lead troops to encamp on the bank of the River,
and for a long time did not summon him back.
The army collapsed and returned,
and Gao Ke fled to Chen.
The people of Zheng composed the poem "Qing Ren" about him.
B4.2.7 The Marquis of Jin had Crown Prince Shen Sheng attack the Gao Luo clan of East Mountain.
Li Ke advised him, saying:
"The Crown Prince presents the ancestral sacrifices,
Shèjì zhī zīshèng, The millet offerings for the altars of soil and grain,
yǐ zhāoxī shì jūn shàn zhě yě, are overseen morning and evening by the one who supervises the ruler's meals;
gù yuē zhǒngzǐ. therefore, he is called the *zhǒngzǐ* (eldest son).

yǒu shǒu zé cóng. when there is someone to guard the capital, he follows.
Cóng yuē fǔjūn, Following is called 'assisting the army';
shǒu yuē jiānguó, guarding is called 'overseeing the state';
gǔ zhī zhì yě. this is the system of antiquity.

shì jūnlǚ, and declarations to the troops

bǐngmìng zé bù wēi, if it receives orders, it will not be awe-inspiring;
zhuānmìng zé bù xiào, if it issues orders on its own, it will be unfilial.
Gù jūn zhī sìshì bù kěyǐ shuài shī. Therefore, the heir apparent of the ruler should not lead the army.

jiāng yān yòng zhī? what use will there be for it?

Jūn qí shě zhī!" Your Lordship should abandon this plan!"
Gōng yuē: The Duke said:
"Guǎrén yǒu zǐ, "I, your lord, have sons,
wèi zhī qí shéi lì yān!" [but] do not yet know which one to establish as heir!"
Bù duì ér tuì. He did not reply and withdrew.
Jiàn tàizǐ. He saw the heir apparent.
Tàizǐ yuē: The heir apparent said:
"Am I to be deposed?"
He replied:
"Instruct him in governing the people,
teach him about military affairs,
(if) not reverent, that is to be feared,
why depose (him)?
Moreover, you fear being unfilial,
do not fear not being established.
Cultivate yourself and do not blame others,
then you will be spared from hardship."
The Heir Apparent led the army,
the Duke clothed him in one-sided (special ceremonial) garments,
and adorned him with a golden *jue* (thumb ring/ornament).
Hú Tū drove the chariot,
Xiān Yǒu was the right-hand man.
Liáng Yú Zǐ Yǎng drove for Hǎn Yí,
Xiān Dānmù was the right-hand man.
The *Dàfū* of Yángshé was the commander.
Xiān Yǒu said:
"To wear one-sided garments,
and to grasp the essentials of war,
is in this journey,
you must strive for it!
One-sidedness (impartiality) will have no evil,
the essentials of war keep away disaster,
with yourself free from disaster,
what else is there to worry about?"
Hú Tū sighed and said:
"Time is the indicator of events,
clothing is the emblem of the person,
and the pendant is the banner of one's true heart.
Therefore, if one reveres his duty,
his mandate begins accordingly;
if one attends to his person,
his clothing will be pure;
if one uses his true heart,
his pendant will be appropriate.
Now, the mandate ends with time,
which is to conceal his affairs;
wearing mottled clothing
distances his person;
wearing gold *jue* pendants
abandons his true heart.
To distance with clothing,
to conceal with time;
mottled clothing is cold,
winter is deadly,
gold is cold,
and *jue* pendants signify separation;
how can one rely on this?
Even if one wishes to exert himself,
can the barbarians be exterminated?"
Liáng Yú Zǐyǎng said:
"The one who leads the army
receives his mandate at the ancestral temple,
and receives the sacrificial meat at the altar of the earth;
Although I wish to encourage him,
can the Dí be exterminated?"
Liáng Yú Zi Yǎng said:
"He who commands the army
receives orders at the ancestral temple,
receives the sacrificial meat at the altar of the soil,
and has regular attire.
If he does not obtain [victory] and acts irregularly,
his fate can be known.
To die without fulfilling filial duty
is not as good as fleeing."
Hǎn Yí said:
"Irregular behavior is inconstant,
and the gold ring will not return.
Even if it did return, what would be the point?
The ruler has made up his mind."
Xiān Dān Mù said:
"This attire,
a madman is hindering.
He says
'Exterminate the enemy and return,'
can the enemy be exterminated?
Even if the enemy is exterminated,
there will still be internal slander,
it is better to disobey him."
Hú Tū wanted to leave.
Yáng Shé Dàfū said:
"You must not.
Disobeying orders is unfilial,
abandoning duty is disloyal.
Although you know it is dangerous,
wickedness cannot be embraced.
You must die for it!"
The Crown Prince was about to battle.
I no longer respect you.”
