A5.1 *The Annals of the First Year of Duke Xi*
A5.1.1 In the first year, in spring,
the Duke of Sòng,
the Count of Zhèng,
the Count of Cáo,
and the people of Zhū at Chēng.
A5.1.8 In the ninth month,
the duke defeated the army of Zhū at Yǎn.
A5.1.9 In the winter, the tenth month, on the day rén-wǔ,
Gōngzǐ Yǒu led the army and defeated the Jǔ army at Lì,
capturing Jǔ Ná.
A5.1.10 In the twelfth month, on the day dīng-sì,
the funeral procession of the Lady arrived from Qí.
B5.1 *Commentary on the First Year of Duke Xī*
B5.1.1 In the first year, spring,
there is no mention of ascending the throne;
it's because the Duke went out.
The Duke went out and then returned,
but it is not recorded,
because it is being concealed.
Concealing the evils of the state
is a matter of propriety.
B5.1.2 The feudal lords rescued Xíng.
The people of Xíng scattered,
fleeing to the army.
The army then pursued the Dí 狄 people,
prepared the instruments of Xíng 邢,
and moved them [there];
the army was not selfish in this.
B5.1.3 In summer,
Xíng 邢 moved to Yíyí 夷儀,
the lords built a city for them,
to relieve their suffering.
Generally, when lords and senior officials
relieve suffering,
divide calamities,
and punish crimes,
this is proper.
B5.1.4 In autumn,
the Chǔ 楚 people attacked Zhèng 鄭,
Zhèng 鄭 then sought the help of Qí 齊 as before.
They made a covenant at Luò 犖,
to plan the rescue of Zhèng 鄭.
B5.1.5 In the ninth month,
the Duke defeated the Zhū 邾 army at Yǎn 偃,
they were the garrison of Xūqiū 虛丘 returning home.
B5.1.6 In winter,
the people of Jǔ 莒 came seeking bribes,
Gōngzǐ Yǒu 公子友 defeated them at Lì 酈,
and captured the younger brother of the ruler of Jǔ 莒, Ná 挐.
This was not a high-ranking official,
so they rejoiced at his capture.
The Duke granted Jì Yǒu 季友 land in Wènyáng 汶陽 and Fèi 費.
B5.1.7 The Lady's (fūrén shì) funeral procession arrived from Qí.
The Gentlemen (jūnzǐ) considered the people of Qí's killing of Āi Jiāng to be excessive.
Women
are those who follow others.
A5.2 *Annals of Duke Xī, Year 2*
A5.2.1 In the spring of the second year, in the first month of the king,
the city of Chǔqiū was fortified.
A5.2.2 In the summer, the fifth month, on the day Xīnsì,
our minor ruler, Āi Jiāng, was buried.
A5.2.3 The army of Yú,
and the army of Jìn, destroyed Xiàyáng.
A5.2.4 In the autumn, the ninth month,
the Marquis of Qí,
the Duke of Sòng,
the people of Jiāng,
and the people of Huáng formed an alliance at Guàn.
A5.2.5 In the winter, the tenth month,
there was no rain.
A5.2.6 The people of Chǔ invaded Zhèng.
B5.2 *Commentary on Duke Xī, Year 2*
B5.2.1 In the spring of the second year,
the various lords fortified Chǔqiū 楚丘 and enfeoffed Wèi 衛 there.
It is not recorded who attended the alliance,
because it was later.
B5.2.2 Xún Xī 荀息 of Jìn 晉 requested to borrow a passage through Yú 虞 with the horses of Qūchǎn 屈產 and the jade of Chuíjí 垂棘 in order to attack Guó 虢.
The Duke [of Jìn 晉] said,
"These are my treasures."
Xún Xī 荀息 replied, "If we obtain a passage through Yú 虞,
it will be like an outer treasury."
The Duke [of Jìn 晉] said, "[Gōng Zhīqí] 宮之奇 is still there."
Xún Xī 荀息 replied, "The personality of Gōng Zhīqí 宮之奇
is weak and unable to strongly remonstrate.
Moreover, he grew up with the ruler,
and the ruler is close to him.
Even if he remonstrates,
he will not be listened to."
Then he sent Xún Xī 荀息 to borrow a passage through Yú 虞,
saying, "Jì 冀 was unrighteous,
entered from Diānlíng 顛軨,
and attacked the three gates of Míng 鄍.
Now that Jì 冀 is sick,
it is all due to you, my lord.
Now Guó 虢 is unrighteous,
They are harbored in the lodging,
to encroach upon the southern borders of our humble state.
I dare to request passage
to plead their guilt before Guó."
Yú Gōng (虞公) granted it,
and even offered to attack Guó first.
Gōng Zhīqí (宮之奇) advised against it,
but he did not listen,
and consequently raised an army.
In summer,
Jin's Lì Kè (里克) and Xún Xī (荀息) led troops
to join with the Yú army
to attack Guó,
destroying Xiàyáng (下陽).
The record's priority to Yú
is a matter of bribes.
B5.2.3 In autumn,
they formed an alliance at Guàn (貫),
causing the subjugation of Jiāng (江)
and Huáng (黃).
B5.2.4 Qí's (齊) eunuch Diāo (貂) first
disclosed military information at Duōyú (多魚).
B5.2.5 The Duke of Guó defeated the Róng at Sāngtián (桑田).
Jin's Bǔ Yǎn (卜偃) said:
"Guó is sure to perish.
They are not afraid of losing Xiàyáng,
and yet they have merit,
this is Heaven taking away their wisdom
and increase their suffering.
He will certainly replace Jìn
and not care for his people.
It cannot be done in five years."
B5.2.6 In winter,
the Chǔ 楚 people attacked Zhèng 鄭,
Dòu Zhāng 鬭章 imprisoned Zhèng Dānbó 鄭聃伯.

"You are in the Northern Sea, and I am in the Southern Sea.
Guǎrén chǔ Nánhǎi, [I, the寡人, dwell in the South Sea,]
wéi shì fēng mǎ niú bù xiāng jí yě, [truly it is a place where even wind-blown horses and cattle do not reach,]
bù yú jūn zhī shè wú dì yě, [I did not expect you, Sir, to set foot on my land,]
hé gù?" [for what reason?"]
Guǎn Zhòng duì yuē: [Guǎn Zhòng replied:]
"Xī Zhào Kāng Gōng mìng wǒ xiān jūn Dàgōng yuē: [“In the past, Duke Kāng of Zhào commanded my late lord, Duke Dàgōng, saying:]
'Wǔ hóu [“The Five Marquises,]
jiǔ bó, [Nine Earls,]
nǚ shí zhēng zhī, [you are to truly subdue them,]
yǐ jiā fǔ Zhōu shì!' [in order to assist the House of Zhōu!"’]
Cì wǒ xiān jūn lǚ, [He bestowed upon my late lord territory,]
dōng zhì yú hǎi, [eastward to the sea,]
xī zhì yú hé, [westward to the Hé River,]
nán zhì yú Mùlíng, [southward to Mount Mùlíng,]
běi zhì yú Wúdì. [northward to Wúdì.]
Ěr gòng bāo máo bù rù, [If your tribute of bundled reeds does not arrive,]
wáng jì bù gòng, [and you do not contribute to the royal sacrifices,]
wú yǐ suō jiǔ, [making it impossible to strain the wine,]
guǎrén shì zhēng. [then I will come to punish you.]
Zhāo Wáng nán zhēng ér bù fù, [King Zhāo campaigned to the south and did not return,]
guǎrén shì wèn." [I am here to inquire about that."’]
Duì yuē: [He replied:]
"Gòng zhī bù rù, [“That the tribute did not arrive,]
guǎ jūn zhī zuì yě, [is the fault of my ruler,]
gǎn bù gòng gěi? [how dare we not provide it?]
Zhāo Wáng zhī bù fù, [As for King Zhāo not returning,]
jūn qí wèn zhū shuǐ bīn!" [Sir, you should ask the riverbanks about that!"’]
Shī jìn, [The army advanced,]
Next to Xíng 陘.
In summer,
the Chǔzi 楚子 sent Qū Wán 屈完 to the army.
The army retreated and
camped next to Zhàolíng 召陵.
The Marquis of Qí 齊侯 displayed the armies of the various lords,
and rode with Qū Wán 屈完 to observe them.
The Marquis of Qí 齊侯 said:
"Is it not for my sake [that they are here]?
I am continuing the friendship of my late lord.
How would it be to share my liking?"
He replied:
"Your Lordship graciously seeks blessings for the altars of our humble state,
deigning to receive our ruler,
which is the wish of our ruler."
The Marquis of Qí 齊侯 said:
"With this multitude to fight,
who could resist it?
With this to attack cities,
what city could not be conquered?"
He replied:
"If your Lordship were to pacify the lords with virtue,
who would dare not submit?
If your Lordship were to use force,
Chǔ 楚 would use the Fāngchéng 方城 mountains as its walls,
and the Hàn 漢 river as its moat.
Even with your Lordship's multitude,
there would be no use for it."
Qū Wán and the various lords formed an alliance.
B5.4.2 Chén Yuán Tāo Tú said to Zhèng Shēn Hóu:
"If the army passes between Chén and
Zhèng,
the state will surely suffer greatly.
If it goes out to the east,
review troops in the Eastern Yi,
and return along the sea,
that would be acceptable."
Shēn Hóu said:
"Good."
Tāo Tú informed him,
and the Marquis of Qí
agreed to it.
Shēn Hóu met (with the Marquis of Qí)
and said:
"The army is old;
if it goes out to the east and encounters the enemy,
I fear it cannot be used.
If it goes between Chén and
Zhèng,
provide them with supplies
and sandals;
that would be acceptable."
The Marquis of Qí was pleased
and gave him Hǔ Láo.
He arrested Yuán Tāo Tú.
B5.4.3 In the autumn,
Punishing Chén
was to punish disloyalty.
B5.4.4 Xǔ Mù Gōng died in the army.
He was buried with the rites of a marquis;
this was proper.
Whenever a feudal lord dies during a court visit
or at a meeting,
his rank is increased by one level;
if he dies in service to the king,
his rank is increased by two levels.
In these cases, he is entombed with a gǔn robe.
B5.4.5 In winter,
Shū Sūn Dài Bó led the army
to join the armies of the feudal lords in invading Chén.
Chén was subdued,
and Yuán Tāo Tú was returned.
B5.4.6 Initially,
Duke Xiàn of Jìn wanted to make Lì Jī his wife.
He divined it with tortoise shells,
but the result was inauspicious.
He divined it with milfoil stalks,
and the result was auspicious.
The duke said,
"I will follow the milfoil stalks."
The diviner said,
"The milfoil stalks are short, the tortoise shells are long;
it is better to follow the long.
Moreover, its divination says:
"To fixate on one's own ideas is to
seize upon the errors of the public.
Mixing sweet wormwood with stinkweed,
even after ten years, the stench still lingers."
This absolutely must not be allowed!"
But he did not listen
and installed him.
Shēng Xīqí (生奚齊) was born,
and his younger sister gave birth to Zhuō Zǐ (卓子).
When he was about to install Xīqí,
having already conspired with the senior officials,
Jī (姬) said to the crown prince,
"The lord dreamed of Qí Jiāng (齊姜),
you must quickly offer sacrifice to her!"
The crown prince offered sacrifice at Qūwò (曲沃),
and brought back the sacrificial meat to the Duke.
The Duke went hunting,
Jī placed the poisoned meat in the palace for six days.
When the Duke returned,
she poisoned it and presented it.
At the place where the Duke made offerings,
the ground swelled up.
It was given to a dog,
and the dog died.
It was given to a minor official,
and the minor official also died.
Jī wept and said,
"The treason is due to the crown prince."
Dàzǐ fled to Xīnchéng.
The duke killed his tutor, Dù Yuánkǎn.
Someone said to the crown prince:
"If you plead your case,
the ruler will surely defend himself."
The crown prince said:
"If the ruler were not of the Jī lineage,
he would be uneasy in his position,
and not eat his fill.
If I plead my case,
Jī will surely be found guilty.
The ruler is old,
and I would not be happy either."
The person said:
"Should you leave then?"
The crown prince said:
"The ruler does not truly understand his guilt;
having this reputation, if I leave,
who would accept me?"
In the twelfth month, on the day wùshēn,
he hanged himself in Xīnchéng.
Jī then slandered the two younger sons,
saying:
"They all knew of it."
Chóng'ěr fled to Pú,
Yíwú fled to Qū.
A5.5 *Xī Gōng's Fifth Year Annals*
A5.5.1 In the fifth year, in spring,
the Marquis of Jìn 晉侯 killed his heir apparent, Shēnshēng 申生.
A5.5.2 The Lady Jī 姬 of the Count of Qǐ 杞 came to court for her son.
A5.5.3 In summer,
Gōngsūn Zī 公孫茲 went to Móu 牟.
A5.5.4 The Duke, along with the Marquis of Qí 齊侯,
the Duke of Sòng 宋公,
the Marquis of Chén 陳侯,
the Marquis of Wèi 衛侯,
the Count of Zhèng 鄭伯,
the Viscount of Xǔ 許男,
and the Count of Cáo 曹伯, met with the King's heir apparent at Shǒuzhǐ 首止.
A5.5.5 In the eighth month, in autumn,
the lords made a covenant at Shǒuzhǐ 首止.
A5.5.6 The Count of Zhèng 鄭伯 fled back without joining the covenant.
A5.5.7 The people of Chǔ 楚 destroyed Xián 弦,
and the Viscount of Xián 弦子 fled to Huáng 黃.
A5.5.8 On the first day of the ninth month, Wùshēn 戊申,
there was a solar eclipse.
A5.5.9 In winter,
The men of Jìn captured the Lord of Yú.
B5.5 *Commentary of the Fifth Year of Duke Xī*
B5.5.1 In the fifth year, spring, the first month of the king, on the day xīn-hài, the first day of the month,
the sun reached its southernmost point.
After the Duke had observed the new moon,
then ascended the viewing terrace to observe,
and record (the event),
as was the proper ritual.
Whenever there was an equinox,
solstice, the beginning (of a season),
or end (of a season),
it was necessary to record the clouds and natural phenomena,
in order to prepare for eventualities.
B5.5.2 The Lord of Jìn sent (someone) to report the reason for killing the Crown Prince Shēnshēng.
Initially,
the Marquis of Jin ordered Shì Wěi
to build Pú and Qū for the two sons of the Duke,
but (he) was not cautious,
and placed firewood there.
Yíwú complained about it.
The Duke sent (someone) to reproach him.
Shì Wěi bowed his head and replied:
"I have heard:
'To grieve without a bereavement,
sorrow will surely seek revenge;
to build a city without war,
"One must certainly protect against enemies."
Protecting against enemies,
what more need be careful about?
Neglecting one's duty to uphold the ruler's command is
disrespect;
stubbornly protecting one's personal enemies is
disloyalty.
Lacking both loyalty and respect,
how can one serve the ruler?
The *Shī Jīng* says:
"Cherishing virtue brings peace,
Supporting the nobles makes the city strong.”
If the ruler cultivates virtue
and strengthens his relatives,
what city could compare to that?
In three years, we will be seeking teachers;
what need is there to be so careful now?"
He withdrew and composed a poem:
"My fox fur is shaggy,
in one state there are three dukes,
whom should I follow?"
When the trouble came,
the Duke sent Sìrén Pī to attack Pú.
Chóng'ěr said:
"The ruler's father's command cannot be questioned."
He then announced:
"Those who question it
are my enemies."
He climbed over the wall and fled.
He slashed and cut his sleeve.
Then he fled to the Dí.
B5.5.3 In the summer,
Gōngsūn Zī went to Móu
to take a wife.
B5.5.4 They met at Shǒuzhǐ,
meeting with Crown Prince Zhèng of the King
to discuss pacifying the Zhōu.
B5.5.5 Chén Yuán Xuānzhòng
resented that Zhèng Shēnhóu had turned against him at Shàolíng,
so he urged him to fortify his bestowed city,
saying,
"Make it a beautiful city;
it will be a great name
that your descendants will not forget.
I will help you request it."
Then he requested it from the various lords
and the city was fortified,
beautifully.
Thereupon, he slandered him to the Earl of Zhèng,
saying,
"Měi is fortifying his bestowed city
with the intention of rebelling."
Shēnhóu consequently fell out of favor.
B5.5.6 In the autumn,
the lords formed an alliance.
The King sent the Duke of Zhōu to summon the Earl of Zhèng,
He said:
"I will appease the daughter by following Chǔ,
and assist her with Jìn,
and she can be a little more at ease."
Zhèng Bó was pleased with the king's command,
but feared that he would not pay homage to Qí,
therefore he fled home without making an alliance.
Kǒng Shū stopped him,
saying:
"The ruler of a state should not be treated lightly,
if treated lightly, one will lose the support of relatives;
if you lose the support of relatives,
misfortune will surely come.
Asking for an alliance when in trouble,
will result in great losses.
You will surely regret it."
He did not listen,
and fled from his army and returned home.
B5.5.7 Chǔ general Dòu Gǔ Yūtú destroyed Xián,
the Viscount of Xián fled to Huáng.
At that time, Jiāng, Huáng, Dào, and Bǎi were all on good terms with Qí,
and were all related to Xián by marriage.
The Viscount of Xián relied on them
and did not serve Chǔ,
nor did he make preparations,
therefore he perished.
B5.5.8 The Marquis of Jìn again borrowed a path from Yú
to attack Guó.
Gōng Zhīqí advised, saying:
"Guó
and Yú are interdependent like the exterior and interior;
if Guó falls,
Yú will inevitably follow.
Jìn should not be provoked,
and enemies should not be trifled with.
Once is already excessive,
how can it happen twice?
The proverb says,
'The carriage cheek-guard relies on the wheel,
if the lips are gone, the teeth are cold,'
refers to
Yú
and Guó."
The Duke said,
"Jìn is
of our lineage,
how could they harm me?"
He replied:
"Tàibó
and Yú Zhòng,
were the brilliant sons of Great King (Dàwáng);
Tàibó did not comply (with the succession),
therefore he did not inherit.
Guó Zhòng
and Guó Shū
were the revered sons of King Jì;
He was a high minister under King Wén (Wén Wáng),
his meritorious service was within the royal house,
and his achievements were preserved in the covenant archives.
If he was going to destroy the state of Guó,
why would he show affection for the state of Yú?
Moreover, could Yú be more closely related to Duke Huán (Huán Gōng) and Duke Zhuāng (Zhuāng Gōng) than we are?
Even if they were to love them,
what crime have the clansmen of Duke Huán and Duke Zhuāng committed
that they should be subjected to slaughter?
Isn't this simply oppression?
To oppress close relatives with favoritism,
and even harm them,
how much more so would they do with a state?"
Duke (of Jìn) said,
"My sacrificial offerings are rich and pure,
the spirits will surely rely on me."
He replied,
"I have heard that
ghosts and spirits are not truly intimate with people,
but only rely on virtue.
Therefore, the *Book of Zhou* says:
'Imperial Heaven has no favorites,
it only assists those with virtue.'
It also says:
'Millet and sorghum are not fragrant,
bright virtue alone is fragrant.'
It also says:
'The people do not easily change their allegiance,
“Only with virtue can one secure possessions."
If it is like this,
then it is not virtue,
the people will not be harmonious,
and the spirits will not accept the offerings.
The spirits rely upon
virtue.
If Jìn takes Yú,
and (Jìn) uses bright virtue
to offer fragrant sacrifices,
would the spirits reject it?"
(Duke Xī of Yú) did not listen,
and permitted the Jìn envoy to pass through.
Gōng Zhīqí took his clan and departed,
saying:
"Yú will not have the là sacrifice this year.
With this passage,
Jìn will not need to attack again."
On the day jiǎwǔ of the eighth month,
The Marquis of Jìn besieged Shàngyáng.
He asked Bǔ Yǎn, saying:
“Will I succeed?”
He replied:
“You will conquer it.”
The duke said:
“When?”
He replied:
“A children's rhyme says:
"On the *bǐng* morning,
the Dragon Tail was in the *chén* position;
their uniforms were all neat,
they seized the banners of Guó.
The *chún* constellation was bright,
the Celestial Whip was ablaze,
the army was formed in the midst of *chún* fire,
Guó Gōng fled."
Was it at the turn of the ninth and
tenth months?
On the *bǐngzǐ* dawn,
the sun was in Tail,
the moon was in Whip,
*Chúnhuǒ* was in the midst,
it must have been at this time."
In the twelfth month of winter, on the *bǐngzǐ*
first day of the month,
Jìn destroyed Guó.
Guó Gōng Chǒu fled to the capital.
The army returned,
lodged in Yú,
and then attacked Yú,
destroying it.
They captured Yú Gōng and his grand officer, Jǐng Bó,
to be a dowry for Qín Mù Jī,
and restored the Yú sacrifices,
and also returned its tribute to the King.
Therefore the history states,
"The Jìn 晉 people captured Gōng 虞公,"
accusing Gōng 虞 of a crime
and also talking about the ease (of the capture).
A5.6 *The Sixth Year of Duke Xī*
A5.6.1 In the sixth year, spring,
the king's first month.
A5.6.2 Summer,
the duke met with the Marquis of Qí 齊侯,
Duke of Sòng 宋公,
Marquis of Chén 陳侯,
Marquis of Wèi 衛侯,
and the Earl of Cáo 曹伯 to attack Zhèng 鄭,
and besieged the New City.
A5.6.3 Autumn,
the Chǔ 楚 people besieged Xǔ 許,
and the various lords then rescued Xǔ 許.
A5.6.4 Winter,
the duke returned from attacking Zhèng 鄭.
B5.6 *The Commentary on the Sixth Year of Duke Xī*
B5.6.1 In the sixth year, spring,
the Marquis of Jìn 晉侯 sent Jiǎ Huá 賈華 to attack Qū 屈.
Yíwú 夷吾 was unable to defend it,
They made an alliance and then acted.
The general was about to flee to the Dí people.
Xì Ruì said,
"To set out later and flee together
is a crime.
It would be better to go to Liáng.
Liáng is near Qín, and we might find favor there."
So they went to Liáng.
B5.6.2 In summer,
the lords attacked Zhèng,
because Zhèng had fled from the alliance at Shǒu Zhǐ.
They besieged Xīn Mì,
which Zhèng had failed to fortify in a timely manner.
B5.6.3 In autumn,
the Viscount of Chǔ besieged Xǔ to relieve Zhèng.
The lords came to the aid of Xǔ,
and so he withdrew.
B5.6.4 In winter,
Marquis Mù of Cài brought Duke Xī of Xǔ
to be presented to the Viscount of Chǔ at Wǔchéng.
The Viscount of Xǔ appeared with his face bound,
holding a jade disc in his mouth,
the officers in mourning robes and sashes,
and the soldiers carrying a coffin.
The Viscount of Chǔ inquired of Féng Bó.
He replied,
"Formerly, when King Wǔ conquered Yīn,
Wēizǐ Qǐ was like this.
Wǔ Wáng himself untied his bonds,
accepted his jade disc and performed an expiation ritual with it,
burned his coffin,
treated him with propriety and gave him orders,
ordering him to return to his position."
The Chǔ ruler followed this.
A5.7 *Xī Gōng* Year 7 *Jīng*
A5.7.1 In the spring of the seventh year,
the people of Qí attacked Zhèng.
A5.7.2 In the summer,
the ruler of Xiǎo Zhū came to court.
A5.7.3 Zhèng killed its grand master, Shēn Hóu.
A5.7.4 In the autumn, seventh month,
the duke met with the Marquis of Qí,
the Duke of Sòng,
the heir apparent Kuǎn of Chén,
and the heir apparent Huá of Zhèng,
and swore an alliance at Níngmǔ.
A5.7.5 Bó Bān of Cáo died.
A5.7.6 Gōngzǐ Yǒu went to Qí.
A5.7.7 In the winter,
The burial of Duke Zhāo of Cáo.
B5.7 "Commentary of the Seventh Year of Duke Xī"
B5.7.1 In the spring of the seventh year,
the people of Qí attacked Zhèng.
Kǒng Shū said to the Count of Zhèng:
"There is a saying:
'If the heart does not strive,
what fear is there of illness?'
Since we cannot be strong,
nor can we be weak,
this is the reason for ruin.
The state is in danger,
please make concessions to Qí to save the state."
The Count said:
"I know where this comes from,
please wait for me a little while."
He replied:
"Morning does not reach evening,
how can we wait for you, my lord?"
B5.7.2 In summer,
Zhèng killed Shēn Hóu to appease Qí,
and also used the slander of Chén Yuán Tāo Tú.
Initially,
Shēn Hóu,
from the Shēn clan,
was favored by King Wén of Chǔ.
When King Wén Wáng was about to die,
he gave him a jade disc,
and told him to leave,
saying:
"Only I understand you.
You are exclusively concerned with profit and are never satisfied,
you give and take, you demand,
and I do not find fault with you.
Those who come after me will demand even more from you,
and you will certainly not escape [their wrath].
After I die,
you must leave quickly,
and do not go to a small state,
as they will not tolerate you."
After the burial,
he fled to Zhèng,
and was once again favored by Duke Lì.
Zǐ Wén heard of his death
and said:
"The ancients had a saying:
'No one knows their ministers better than the ruler,'
and it cannot be changed."
B5.7.3 In the autumn,
they made a covenant at Níngmǔ,
to plan about Zhèng's affairs.
Guǎn Zhòng said to the Marquis of Qí:
"I have heard:
'Attract those nearby with ritual,
Cherish those far away with virtue.
If virtue and propriety are not changed,
there will be no one who does not cherish you."
The Marquis of Qí cultivated propriety among the feudal lords,
and the officials of the feudal lords received local products.
The Count of Zhèng sent Crown Prince Huá
to listen to orders at the assembly,
and said to the Marquis of Qí:
"The Xiè clan,
the Kǒng clan,
and the Zǐrén clan,
truly disobeyed your orders.
If you were to remove them to achieve success,
I would make Zhèng your inner minister,
and you would have no disadvantage."
The Marquis of Qí was about to agree.
Guǎn Zhòng said:
"You unite the feudal lords with propriety and trust,
but end it with treachery;
would that not be wrong?
That fathers and sons do not betray each other is called propriety,
that one keeps one's word and fulfills one's obligations on time is called trust;
to violate these two,
there is no greater treachery."
The Duke said:
"The feudal lords have attacked Zhèng,
but have not yet won;
now if there is a chance
to follow it,
would that not be acceptable?"
He replied:
"If you were to soothe them with virtue,
and add to them instruction,
decline.
and lead the lords to punish Zhèng,
Zhèng will be so pressed for time to avoid destruction,
how could they dare not to fear?
If you were to gather their criminals to confront them,
Zhèng would have a reason to resist,
what is there to fear?
is for promoting virtue.
To expose treachery at the assembly,
how would you set an example for posterity?
In the assemblies of lords,
their virtues,
punishments, rituals,
and righteousness,
are recorded by every state.
To record the positions of traitors,
the lords' alliance will be weakened.
To act but not record it,
is not a display of great virtue.
Your Lordship, please do not agree!
Zhèng will certainly accept the alliance.
Moreover, since Zǐ Huá is already the heir apparent,
And to seek mediation from a great state to weaken their own state,
that also will surely be unavoidable.
Zhèng has Shū Zhān,
Dǔ Shū,
and Shī Shū, three good men in charge of the government,
so they cannot be interfered with."
The Marquis of Qí declined.
Zǐ Huá therefore incurred the displeasure of Zhèng.
B5.7.4 Winter,
The Earl of Zhèng sent to request a covenant from Qí.
B5.7.5 In the intercalary month,
King Huì died.
King Xiāng detested the trouble caused by Dà Shū Dài.
Fearing he would not be established,
he did not announce the mourning,
but reported the trouble to Qí.
A5.8 "The Eighth Year of Duke Xī"
A5.8.1 In the eighth year, spring,
the king's first month,
the duke met with the king's men,
the Marquis of Qí,
the Duke of Sòng,
the Marquis of Wèi,
the Viscount of Xǔ,
the Earl of Cáo,
and the Heir Apparent Kuǎn of Chén,
and formed a covenant at Táo.
Zhèng Bó begged for a covenant.
A5.8.2 In summer,
the Dí attacked Jìn.
A5.8.3 In autumn, the seventh month,
the dì sacrifice was performed at the Great Temple,
to bring the late Lady (back in spirit).
A5.8.4 In winter, the twelfth month, on the day dīngwèi,
the Heavenly King passed away.
B5.8 "Zuǒ Zhuàn, Year 8 of Duke Xī"
B5.8.1 In the spring of the eighth year,
a covenant was made at Táo,
to plan for the royal house.
Zhèng Bó begged for a covenant,
requesting submission.
King Xiāng established his position
and then announced the mourning.
B5.8.2 Lì Kè of Jìn led the army,
Liáng Yóumí was the charioteer,
and Guó Shè was the right-hand man,
to defeat the Dí at Cǎisāng.
Liáng Yóumí said:
"The Dí are shameless,
follow them,
Must greatly overcome."
Lì Kè said:
"We should only fear them,
do not quickly gather the many Dí tribes."
Guó Shè said:
"Within a year, the Dí will certainly arrive;
showing weakness to them."
In summer,
the Dí attacked Jìn,
to retaliate for the mulberry-picking service.
Again, after a full month.
B5.8.3 In autumn,
they performed the *dì* sacrifice
and enshrined Āi Jiāng there;
this was not in accordance with propriety.
Generally, with regard to a *fūrén* (wife of a ruler),
if she does not die in her bedchamber,
is not coffined in the ancestral temple,
does not go to the clan's assembly,
and is not enshrined with the paternal aunt,
then she is not enshrined.
B5.8.4 In winter,
royal messengers came to announce the death;
it was difficult to give a reason,
therefore it was delayed.
B5.8.5 Duke Sòng was ill;
Crown Prince Zīfù earnestly requested,
saying:
"[Mù Yí] is mature and benevolent,
Your Lordship should establish him!"
The Duke ordered Zǐ Yú.
Zǐ Yú declined,
saying:
"To be able to yield the state,
what benevolence is greater than that?
Your servant is not up to it,
moreover, it is also not compliant."
Thereupon, he ran away and withdrew.
A5.9 *The Ninth Year of Duke Xī Chronicle*
A5.9.1 In the ninth year, in spring,
in the third month, on the day *dīngchǒu*,
Duke Yù Shuō of Sòng died.
A5.9.2 In summer,
the Duke met with the Steward Zhōu Gōng,
the Marquis of Qí,
the Viscount of Sòng,
the Marquis of Wèi,
the Count of Zhèng,
the Viscount of Xǔ,
and the Count of Cáo at Kuíqiū.
A5.9.3 In autumn, in the seventh month, on the day *yǐyǒu*,
Bó Jī died.
A5.9.4 In the ninth month, on the day wùchén,
the lords made a covenant at Kuíqiū.
A5.9.5 On the day jiǎzǐ,
the Marquis of Jìn, Guǐzhū, died.
A5.9.6 In winter,
Lì Kè of Jìn killed Xīqí, the son of his lord.
B5.9 *Commentary on the Ninth Year of Duke Xī*
B5.9.1 In the ninth year, in spring,
Duke Huán of Sòng died.
Before he was buried, Duke Xiāng convened the lords,
therefore he is referred to as "
zi (son)".
Generally, during mourning,
the king is called "
xiǎo tóng (little child)",
and dukes and marquises are called "
zi (son)".
B5.9.2 In summer,
they met at Kuíqiū
to renew the covenant
and cultivate good relations,
which is proper etiquette.
The king sent Zǎi Kǒng
to bestow blessed meat upon the Marquis of Qí,
He said:
"The Son of Heaven has affairs related to Wén
and Wǔ,
and sent Kǒng to bestow the sacrificial meat upon your maternal uncle."
The Lord of Qí was about to descend and bow.
Kǒng said:
"There is yet a further command.
The Son of Heaven sent Kǒng, saying:
'Because your maternal uncle is old and advanced in years,
and greatly burdened,
he is granted an additional grade [of honor],
without the need to descend and bow!'"
He replied:
"The majesty of Heaven is never far from one's face, even at a short distance.
Xiǎo Bái,
how dare I covet the Son of Heaven's command
and not descend and bow?
- I fear falling and stumbling below,
and thus bringing shame upon the Son of Heaven.
How dare I not descend and bow?"
He descended,
and bowed;
ascended [the platform],
and received [the sacrificial meat].
B5.9.3 In autumn,
the Lord of Qí convened the feudal lords in a covenant at Kuíqiū,
saying:
"All those who are allied with us,
After the alliance,
they said, "Let's return to being on good terms."
Zǎi Kǒng returned first,
and met the Marquis of Jìn,
saying:
"It is permissible not to attend the meeting.
The Marquis of Qí does not focus on virtue
but is diligent in far-reaching strategies,
therefore he has campaigned north against the Shān Róng,
south against Chǔ,
and now has created this western meeting.
We do not know his eastern strategies,
but the western ones are clear.
He is probably creating chaos!
Your Lordship should focus on pacifying the chaos,
and not be diligent in travel."
The Marquis of Jìn then returned.
B5.9.4 In the ninth month,
the Duke Xiàn of Jìn died.
Lì Kè and Pī Zhèng wanted to install Duke Wén,
and therefore used the followers of the three sons of the Duke to create chaos.
Initially,
Duke Xiàn made Xún Xī the tutor of Xī Qí.
The Duke fell ill,
and summoned him,
saying:
"To entrust these young orphans and disgrace them before the grandees,
what is to be done?"
He bowed his head and replied,
"Your servant will exhaust the strength of his arms and legs,
and add to it loyalty
and integrity.
If it succeeds,
it is due to your Majesty's spirit;
if it fails,
then I will follow it with my death."
The Duke said,
"What is meant by loyalty
and integrity?"
He replied,
"The benefit of the ducal house,
knowing it and doing everything without fail,
is loyalty;
attending to the dead and serving the living,
in pairs without any suspicion,
is integrity."
When Lì Kè was about to kill Xī Qí,
he first told Xún Xī, saying,
"The three resentments are about to arise,
with Qín and Jìn assisting them.
What will you do?"
Xún Xī said,
"I will die for it."
Lì Kè said,
"It will be of no benefit."
Xún Shū said,
"I have already spoken with the late lord,"
"it cannot be changed."
"Does he wish to speak again and yet cherish his own life?
Even though it is of no benefit,
where could he escape to?
Moreover, in the desire for goodness,
who is not like me?
I desire to be unwavering,
and can I say that others have already done so?"
In the tenth month of winter,
Lì Kè killed Xī Qí at the encampment.
The record says
"killed the son of the ruler,"
as he had not yet been buried.
Xún Xī was about to die for it,
and someone said:
"It would be better to install Zhuō Zǐ
and assist him."
Xún Xī installed Gōngzǐ Zhuō
in order to bury (Xī Qí).
In the eleventh month,
Lì Kè killed Gōngzǐ Zhuō at court.
Xún Xī died for it.
The gentleman said:
"The *Poetry* says
'A flaw in white jade
can still be ground away;
but a flaw in these words
"It cannot be done."
Xún Xī 荀息 had them."
B5.9.5 The Marquis of Qí 齊, with the army of the various lords, attacked Jìn 晉,
reaching Gāoliáng 高梁 and then returning,
to punish the disorder in Jìn 晉.
The order did not reach Lǔ 魯,
therefore it was not recorded.
B5.9.6 Xì Ruì 郤芮 of Jìn 晉 sent Yíwú 夷吾 with heavy bribes to Qín 秦
to seek entry,
saying:
"If someone truly possesses a state,
why should I begrudge it?
If he can govern the people upon entry,
what ownership does the land truly hold?"
He followed this advice.
Xí Péng 隰朋 of Qí 齊 led an army to meet the Qín 秦 army
to install Duke Huì of Jìn 晉.
The Earl of Qín 秦 said to Xì Ruì 郤芮:
"Who does the lord rely on?"
He replied:
"I have heard
that a fugitive has no party,
and if he has a party, he must have enemies.
Yíwú 夷吾 is weak and does not like playing around,
his ability to fight is unremarkable,
and he will not change even when he grows up.
I do not know anything else about him."
The Duke said to Gōngsūn Zhī 公孫枝:
"Yí Wú will he be settled?"
He replied:
"Your servant has heard it said:
'Only the principles will settle the state.'
The *Shī* (Book of Odes) says:
'Not knowing, not understanding,
Obeying the principles of the Emperor.'
This refers to King Wén."
"It also says:
'Neither presumptuous nor thieving,
Seldom is one not a principle.'
Having neither likes nor dislikes,
Neither jealous nor conquering is what it means.
Now his words are full of jealousy and conquering,
Difficult indeed!"
The duke said:
"Jealousy begets much resentment,
How can he conquer then?
This is to my advantage."
B5.9.7 Duke Xiāng of Sòng ascended the throne.
Considering Gōngzǐ Mùyí to be benevolent,
he made him Left Preceptor to listen to government affairs.
Thereupon Sòng was well-governed.
Therefore, the Yú lineage served as Left Preceptors for generations.

B5.10 *Commentary on the Tenth Year of Duke Xī*
B5.10.1 Tenth year, spring,
the Dí destroyed Wēn because
Sū Zǐ was untrustworthy.
Sū Zǐ betrayed the King and allied with the Dí,
yet was unable to be loyal to the Dí,
so the Dí people attacked him.
The King did not rescue him,
therefore it was destroyed.
Sū Zǐ fled to Wèi.
B5.10.2 In the fourth month of summer,
Zhōu Gōng Jìfù and

The Marquis of Jìn killed Lǐkè
to appease (the people).
As he was about to kill Lǐkè,
the Duke sent a message to him, saying:
"Without you,
I would not have reached this point.
However,
you killed two rulers and one high official;
for one who is your lord,
isn't that difficult?"
He replied:
"If there were no deposed rulers,
how would the lord rise?
If you want to condemn someone,
is there any need for words?
I have received my fate."
He lay on his sword and died.
Thereupon, Pī Zhèng was sent as an envoy to Qín,
and also apologized for the slow delivery of gifts,
therefore he did not arrive in time.

Encountered the Dàzǐ (太子).

Furthermore, what crime have the people committed?
Loss of penal laws,
lack of sacrifices,
Your Lordship, consider it!"
The lord said:
"Agreed.
I will again make a request.
In seven days,
to the western side of Xīnchéng (新城) there will be a shaman
who will see me."
He agreed to it,
and then did not see him.
When the appointed time arrived,
he went and

I am exhausted by Hán."

"Lǚ Shēng,
Xì Chēng,
and Jì Ruì
it was the king's first month.

A6.1 *The Annals of the First Year of Duke Wén*
A6.1.1 In the first year, in spring,
which was Ān (安).
Chén (陳), and Zhèng (鄭) attacked Xǔ (許),
to punish them for their duplicity towards Chǔ (楚).
B5.33.9 The chief minister Zi Shang (子上) of Chǔ (楚) invaded Chén (陳) and Cài (蔡).
Chén (陳) and Cài (蔡) made peace.

intending to install Gōngzǐ Xiá.

"I have heard that:
'Civilization does not violate submission,
martiality does not oppose the enemy.'
If you want to fight,

you cross over and array your troops,

If not,
relieve me.
To keep the army long is wasteful of resources,
Guǎn Jìngzhòng was a traitor to Duke Huán,
but he truly assisted him in his achievements.
The "Kāng Gào" says:
'If the father is not kind,
the son is not reverent;
if the elder brother is not friendly,
the younger brother is not reverent;
they should not have anything to do with each other."
The *Shī* (詩) says:
"Gathering turnips and radishes,
do not discard the lower parts."
The ruler takes moderation, which can be done."
Duke Wén (文公) appointed him as a senior officer of the lower army.
Returning from Jī (箕),

He removed his helmet and entered the Dí army,

Initially,

they were respectful,

Jiù Jì brought Jì Quē back with him,

"Shùn punished Gǔn for his crimes,

The Duke of Qin, dressed in plain clothes, camped in the suburbs,

Xiān Zhěn (先軫) was angry,

He did not look back and spat.

would that not be acting against our deceased ruler?"

B5.15 *Zuǒ Zhuàn*, Year 15 of Duke Xī
B5.15.1 In the spring of the fifteenth year,
the people of Chǔ attacked Xú,
because Xú had turned to the states of Zhū Xià.
In the third month,
they formed an alliance at Mǔqiū
to reaffirm the alliance of Kuíqiū
and also to rescue Xú.
Mèng Mùbó led the army and the armies of the feudal lords to rescue Xú.
The feudal lords encamped at Kuāng to await them.
B5.15.2 In the summer, in the fifth month,
there was a solar eclipse.
It was not recorded the day of the new moon and the day of the eclipse,
because the officials failed to record it.
B5.15.3 In the autumn,
they attacked Lì,
to rescue Xú.
B5.15.4 When the Lord of Jìn entered (office),
Qín Mù Jī entrusted Jiǎ Jūn to him.
and said,
"Admit all the sons of the lords."
The Marquis of Jìn had illicit relations with the Lord of Jiǎ,
and also did not admit all the sons of the lords,
therefore Mù Jī resented him.
The Marquis of Jìn promised bribes to the senior officials,
but afterwards betrayed them all.
He promised the Duke of Qín five cities outside the Hé River,
reaching as far east as Guólüè,
as far south as Mount Huà,
and extending internally to the city of Jiěliáng,
but afterwards did not give them.
When Jìn was experiencing famine,
Qín transported grain to them;
when Qín was experiencing famine,
Jìn closed the market to them,
therefore the Duke of Qín attacked Jìn.
Bǔ Túfù divined about it,
and the result was auspicious:
"Cross the river,
the lord's chariot will be defeated."
He was questioned about it.
He replied,
"It is indeed very auspicious.
After three defeats,
they will certainly capture the ruler of Jìn.
The hexagram encountered was *Gǔ*
䷑, which says:
'A thousand chariots depart three times,
After the third departure,
one captures their male fox.'
This fox in the *Gǔ* hexagram
must be their ruler.
The constancy of *Gǔ*
is wind;
its regret
is mountain.
The year is already saying it is autumn,
I will cause their fruits to fall,
and take their timber,
that is how we will prevail.
If the fruits fall
and the timber is gone,
if we do not defeat them,
what are we waiting for?"
After three defeats, they reached Hán.
The Marquis of Jìn said to Qìng Zhèng:
"The invaders have penetrated deeply;
what should we do?"
He replied:
"Your Lordship has allowed them to penetrate deeply;
what can be done!"
The Duke said:
"You are not compliant!"
They divined for the right flank,
Qìng Zhèng received a favorable omen.
He was not employed.
Bù Yáng drove the war chariot,
and the family servant became the right-hand man.
They rode in a small team of four horses.
As Zhèng entered the battle,
Qìng Zhèng said,
"In ancient times, for great affairs,
one must ride horses native
to the land and water where they are born,
and know the hearts of the people;
be familiar with their teachings,
and be accustomed to their ways;
only then will things go as planned,
and nothing will be contrary to one's desires.
Now, riding horses from a foreign land
to engage in military affairs,
when fear arises and changes occur,
one will be easily replaced by others.
Turbulent qi and cunning anger,
dark blood surges all around,
the veins swell and burst forth,
appearing strong on the outside but weak on the inside.
To advance or retreat is impossible,
to maneuver is impossible;
Your Lordship will surely regret this."
He did not listen.
In the ninth month,
the Marquis of Jìn 晉侯 met the Qin 秦 army,
and sent Hán Jiǎn 韓簡 to observe the army.
He reported back, saying:
"The army is smaller than ours,
but the combatants are twice as many as ours."
The Duke said,
"Why?"
He replied, saying:
"When they went out, they relied on its resources;
when they entered, they used its favor;
when hungry, they ate its grain.
Three kindnesses given, yet there is no repayment;
therefore they came.
Now, if you strike them again,
we will be weary,
and Qin 秦 will be vigorous;
twice the number would still not be enough."
The Duke said,
"Even one man should not be indulged,
how much more a state?"
Thereupon, he sent someone to request battle, saying:
"The unworthy one,
I am not talented,
Being able to unite his people but not being able to separate them.
"If you, my lord, do not return,
I will have nowhere to escape with my life."
The Earl of Qín sent Gōngsūn Zhī to reply,
saying:
"Before you, my lord, entered,
I was afraid;
after you entered but had not yet settled into ranks,
I was still worried.
If the ranks are settled,
how would I dare not obey the command."
Hán Jiǎn withdrew,
and said:
"I am fortunate to have been captured."
On the rénxū day,
they fought at Hányuán.
The Jìn warhorses became mired in the mud and stopped.
The Duke summoned Qìng Zhèng.
Qìng Zhèng said:
"Rejecting advice,
disobeying divination,
surely seeks defeat,
so where can one escape to?"
Thereupon he left him.
Liáng Yóumí drove for Hán Jiǎn,
Guó Shè was the right-hand protector,
and they approached the Earl of Qín,
intending to stop him.
Zhèng (鄭) mistakenly tried to rescue Duke [Xiāng of Sòng] (襄公),
and consequently lost the favor of the Lord of Qín (秦伯).
Qín captured the Marquis of Jìn (晉侯) and returned home.
The Jìn 大夫 *dàfū* (officials) turned their heads back, uprooted their houses,
followed him.
The Lord of Qín (秦伯) sent someone to speak to them,
saying:
"Why are you gentlemen so distressed!
That I followed your lord westward,
was but to fulfill the ominous dreams of Jìn (晉);
how could I dare to go so far?"
The Jìn (晉) grand officers bowed three times and kowtowed, saying:
"Your Lord treads upon the Later Earth
and bears the August Heaven above;
the August Heaven and Later Earth
have surely heard your words.
We, your ministers, dare to listen from below."
Mù Jī (穆姬) heard that the Marquis of Jìn (晉侯) was about to arrive,
and with the Heir Apparent Yíng (罃),
Hóng (弘), and her daughter Jiǎn Bì (簡璧), ascended the platform
and stood on firewood.
She sent someone dressed in mourning clothes to greet him,
and also announced,
"Heaven has sent down calamity,
causing our two lords not to meet with jade and silk,
but with warfare.
If the Lord of Jìn (晉君) enters in the morning,
then this handmaiden will die in the evening;
In the evening he was brought in,
and by morning he would be dead.
Only you, my lord, can decide!"
Thereupon, he was housed in the Língtái (Spirit Terrace).
The senior officials requested to bring him in (to the palace).
The Duke said,
"Capturing the Marquis of Jìn
was intended for a substantial return;
now to return him dead—
what use is that?
What benefit is there for you, my senior officials?
Moreover, the people of Jìn are consumed by grief and worry
to move me,
and Heaven and Earth are using solemn oaths to bind me.
Not considering the grief of Jìn,
would only deepen their anger;
if I were to eat my words,
I would be betraying Heaven and Earth.
Deep anger
is hard to bear;
betraying Heaven
is inauspicious,
I must return the Marquis of Jìn."
Gōngzǐ Zhí said,
"It would be better to kill him,
and not accumulate evil."
Zǐ Sāng said,
"Return him and hold his heir as hostage,
Surely, great success will be achieved.
Jìn is not ready to be destroyed,
and killing its ruler
will only increase our wickedness.
Moreover, Shǐ Yì has said:
'Do not initiate disaster,
do not rely on chaos,
do not harbor excessive anger.'
Excessive anger
is difficult to control;
humiliating others
is inauspicious."
Consequently, he agreed to peace with Jìn.
The Marquis of Jìn sent Xì Qǐ
to inform Xiá Lǚ Yíshēng
and summon him.
Zǐ Jīn taught him what to say,
saying:
"Address the people of the state
and bestow rewards in the ruler's name.
And tell them:
'Although I, your ruler, have returned,
I have disgraced the altars of the state.
Let us divine whether to use Dài and Yǔ as human sacrifices.'"
The people all wept,
and Jìn thereupon created the Àitián system.
Lǚ Yíshēng said:
"The ruler's loss is not a concern,
And the assembled ministers were worried,
which was the height of kindness.
"What should we do about the ruler?"
The people said,
"What should we do to make it acceptable?"
They replied,
"Levy labor to build and repair
in order to assist the young ruler.
When the feudal lords hear of it,
they will see that though we have lost our ruler, we have another ruler,
and that the ministers are harmonious
and our armor and weapons are increasing.
Those who are friendly to us will be encouraged,
those who hate us will be afraid,
and perhaps there will be some benefit!"
The people were pleased,
and thus Jìn made state troops.
Initially,
when Duke Xiàn of Jìn divined about marrying Bó Jī to Qín,
he encountered Guī Mèi ䷵ changing to Kuí ䷥.
Shǐ Sū interpreted it,
saying,
"It is not auspicious.
Its oracle reads:
'A man slaughters a sheep,
but there is no blood;
a woman carries a basket,
There was also no gift.
The western neighbor demanded words,
which could not be repaid.
*Guī Mèi* changing to *Kuí*
is like not having each other.
*Zhèn* changing to *Lí*,
is also *Lí* changing to *Zhèn*.
"It becomes thunder, it becomes fire,
it becomes Yíng defeating Jī.
The chariot breaks its axle,
fire burns its flag,
it is not advantageous to march troops,
defeated at Zōngqiū.
*Guī Mèi* and *Kuí* are isolated,
the robber draws his bow.
The nephew follows his aunt,
for six years he is a fugitive,
fleeing back to his country,
and abandoning his family,
the next year he dies in the waste of Gāoliáng."
When Duke Huì was in Qín,
he said:
"If the late lord had followed the divination of Shǐ Sū,
I would not have reached this point!"
Hán Jiǎn was in attendance,
and said:
"The tortoise and
elephant are images;
divination and
numbers.
Things are born and then there are images,
after images there is growth,
after growth there are numbers.
The late lord's failed virtue,
how can they be reckoned?
Shǐ Sū is performing divination;
not following him, what benefit is there?
The *Shī* says:
'The calamities of the people below
are not sent down from Heaven.
Crowding together in mutual hatred,
contention arises from men.'"
B5.15.5 An earthquake destroyed the temple of Yí Bó;
it was a punishment for him,
and therefore the Zhǎn clan harbored secret wrongdoings.
B5.15.6 In winter,
the people of Sòng attacked Cáo
to avenge old grievances.
B5.15.7 Chǔ defeated Xú at Lóulín;
Xú relied on aid.
B5.15.8 In the tenth month,
Jìn's Yīn Yíshēng met with the Earl of Qín
and swore an oath at Wángchéng.
The Earl of Qín said,
"Is the state of Jìn harmonious?"
He replied,
"They are not harmonious.
Petty men are ashamed to lose their ruler
and grieve for the loss of their parents.
They do not shrink from military preparations
in order to establish defenses,
saying:
'We must avenge ourselves,
even if it means serving the Róng and Dí barbarians.'
Gentlemen love their ruler
and understand his faults.
They do not shrink from military preparations
in order to await the orders of Qín,
saying:
'We must repay kindness;
we would rather die than be disloyal.'
This is why they are not harmonious."
The Bó of Qín said:
"What do the people say of me?"
He replied:
"Petty men are grieved
and say that you will not be released;
gentlemen are forgiving
and believe that you will surely be returned.
Petty men say:
'We hate Qín;
how could Qín possibly return our ruler?'
Gentlemen say:
'We know we have committed an offense;
Qín will certainly return the lord to you.
If you treat him with duplicity and then detain him,
or if he submits and you then release him,
no virtue could be greater,
and no punishment could be more awe-inspiring.
Those who submit will cherish your virtue,
and those who are duplicitous will fear your punishments.
With this one campaign,
Qín can become hegemon.
To accept him without settling things,
to depose him without establishing a successor,
and to turn kindness into resentment,
Qín would not do such a thing!'"
The Earl of Qín said,
"That is what is in my heart."
He changed the lodging for the Marquis of Jìn
and presented him with seven *láo* offerings.
Ézhé said to Qìng Zhèng,
"Why not flee?"
Qìng Zhèng replied,
"To lead the lord into defeat,
to survive defeat without dying,
and then to cause the loss of punishment is
not what a subject should do.
To be a subject and yet not act as a subject,
where would I go?"
In the eleventh month,
the Marquis of Jìn returned.
On Dīngchǒu,
Qìng Zhèng was killed before entering.
This year,
Jìn was again experiencing famine,
so the Earl of Qín again sent them a gift of grain,
saying:
"I resent their ruler,
but I pity their people.
Moreover, I have heard that when Táng Shū was enfeoffed,
Jī Zi said:
'His descendants will surely be great.'
Can Jìn possibly be hoped for?
Let us for the time being plant virtue there,
in order to await someone capable."
Thereupon, Qín began to tax the area east of the Hé River belonging to Jìn,
establishing officials there.
A5.16 *The Annals of the Sixteenth Year of Duke Xī*
A5.16.1 In the sixteenth year, in spring,
on the first day of the king's first month, Wùshēn, there was a lunar eclipse,
and five meteorites fell in Sòng.
This month,
six yì birds flew backwards,
passing over the capital of Sòng.
A5.16.2 In the third month, on Rénshēn,
Gōngzǐ Jì Yǒu died.
A5.16.3 In the fourth month, on bǐngshēn,
Jì Jī of Zēng died.
A5.16.4 In the autumn, in the seventh month, on jiǎzǐ,
Gōngsūn Zī died.
A5.16.5 In the winter, in the twelfth month,
the Duke met with Marquis of Qí,
Duke of Sòng,
Marquis of Chén,
Marquis of Wèi,
Count of Zhèng,
Viscount of Xǔ,
Marquis of Xíng,
and Count of Cáo at Huái.
B5.16 *Commentary on the Sixteenth Year of Duke Xī*
B5.16.1 In the spring of the sixteenth year,
five stones fell in Sòng,
these were falling stars.
Six yì birds flew backwards,
passing over the capital of Sòng,
this was due to the wind.
Shū Xīng, the Inner Historian of Zhōu, was sent as an envoy to Sòng.
Duke Xiāng of Sòng asked him,
saying:
"What is the significance of this?
"Where does good or bad fortune lie?"
He replied, "
This year, there will be many great funerals in Lǔ,
next year there will be chaos in Qí,
and you, my lord, will gain the allegiance of the feudal lords,
but not to the end."
He withdrew and told people, "
The ruler has missed the point of his question.
These are matters of *yīn* and *yáng*,
not things generated by good or bad fortune.
Good and bad fortune come from people.
I dared not contradict my ruler deliberately."
B5.16.2 In summer,
Qí attacked Lì,
but failed to conquer it,
and returned after rescuing Xú.
B5.16.3 In autumn,
the Dí invaded Jìn,
taking Hú,
Chú, and Shòuduó,
crossing the Fén River,
and reaching Kūndū,
due to Jìn's defeat.
B5.16.4 The king, facing trouble from the Róng, informed Qí.
Qí summoned the feudal lords to garrison Zhōu.
B5.16.5 In the eleventh month, on the day *yǐmǎo*,
Zhèng killed Zǐ Huá.
B5.16.6 In the twelfth month,
They met at the Huái River
to plan against Zēng
and to make eastern raids.
They built a city at Zēng.
The laborers were weary.
One night, someone climbed a hill and shouted:
"There is turmoil in Qí!"
They did not complete the city and returned.
A5.17 *Xīgōng* Year 17 Chronicle
A5.17.1 In the spring of the seventeenth year,
the people of Qí
and the people of Xú attacked the Yīng clan.
A5.17.2 In the summer,
they extinguished Xiàng.
A5.17.3 In the autumn,
Lady Jiāng met with Marquis of Qí at Biàn.
A5.17.4 In the ninth month,
the Duke returned from the meeting.
A5.17.5 In the winter, in the twelfth month, on the day yǐ-hài,
Marquis Xiǎo Bái of Qí passed away.
B5.17 *Xīgōng* Year 17 Commentary
B5.17.1 In the spring of the seventeenth year,
the people of Qí attacked the Yīng clan for Xú,
to avenge the battle of Lóulín.
B5.17.2 In the summer,
Crown Prince Yǔ of Jìn was sent to Qín as a hostage.
Qín returned the land east of the Hé River
and gave him a wife.
When Duke Huì was in Liáng,
the wife of the Earl of Liáng married him.
Yíng of Liáng became pregnant
and was overdue.
Diviner Zhāo Fù and his son divined for her.
His son said:
"She will give birth to one boy and one girl."
Zhāo said:
"Yes.
The boy will be a subject,
and the girl will be a concubine."
Therefore, the boy was named Yǔ
and the girl was named Qiè.
When Zǐ Yǔ went west as a hostage,
Qiè became a female palace servant there.
B5.17.3 The army destroyed Xiàng.
At the meeting on the Huái River,
the Duke had affairs with the various lords
and did not return,
but took Xiàng.
and detained the Duke.

B5.17.4 In the autumn,

In the ninth month,
the Duke arrived.
The text states

Marquis Qí was fond of women

Yōng Wū was favored by Wèi Gòng Jī,
and therefore the eunuch Diāo
the royal first month,
