A6.1.2 In the second month, on guǐhài,
there was a solar eclipse.
A6.1.3 The Heavenly King sent Shū Fú to attend the funeral.
A6.1.4 In summer, the fourth month, on dīngsì,
we buried our lord, Duke Xī.
A6.1.5 The Heavenly King sent Máo Bó to bestow orders upon the Duke.
A6.1.6 The Marquis of Jìn attacked Wèi.
A6.1.7 Shūsūn Déchén went to the capital.
A6.1.8 The people of Wèi attacked Jìn.
A6.1.9 In autumn,
Gōngsūn Áo met the Marquis of Jìn in Qī.
A6.1.10 In winter, the tenth month, on dīngwèi,
The Chǔ heir apparent, Shāngchén, murdered his lord, Yūn.
A6.1.11 Gōngsūn Áo went to Qí.
B6.1 "Commentary of the First Year of Duke Wén"
B6.1.1 In the first year, spring,
the King sent the palace official Shūfú to attend the funeral.
Gōngsūn Áo, hearing of his ability to judge people's character,
showed him his two sons.
Shūfú said:
"Gǔ will feed you,
Nán will take you in.
Gǔ's lower body is full,
he will certainly have descendants in the state of Lǔ."
B6.1.2 Thereupon, in the intercalary third month,
which was against ritual.
The former kings regulated the seasons by
beginning at the start,
adjusting in the middle,
and returning the remainder to the end.
Beginning at the start,
the sequence would not be incorrect;
adjusting in the middle,
the people would not be confused;
returning the remainder to the end,
affairs would not be contrary.
B6.1.3 In summer, the fourth month, on dīngsì day,
Duke Xī was buried.
B6.1.4 The King sent Máo Bó Wèi to bestow a command on the Duke.
Shūsūn Déchén went to Zhōu to pay respects.
B6.1.5 In the later years of Duke Wén of Jìn,
the lords paid court to Jìn,
but Duke Chéng of Wèi did not pay court,
and sent Kǒng Dá to invade Zhèng,
attacking Mián, Zī, and Kuāng.
After the mourning period for Duke Xiāng of Jìn was over,
he sent a message to the various lords and attacked Wèi,
reaching Nányáng.
Xiān Qiějū said:
"Following a bad example
is a disaster.
I request that you, my lord, attend court to the King,
and I, your subject, will lead the army."
The Marquis of Jìn attended court to the King at Wēn.
Xiān Qiějū and Xū Chén attacked Wèi.
On the first day of the fifth month, Xīnyǒu,
the Jìn army besieged Qī.
On the day of Wùxū in the sixth month,
they took it,
capturing Sūn Zhāozi.
The people of Wèi sent a message to Chén.
Duke Gòng of Chén said:
"Attack it again,
and I will excuse it."
Wèi's Kǒng Dá led an army to attack Jìn.
Gentlemen consider this ancient.
The ancient way
was to plan beyond one's own state.
B6.1.6 In the autumn,
the Marquis of Jìn surveyed the fields of Qī,
therefore Gōngsūn Áo attended a meeting concerning it.
B6.1.7 Initially,
the Viscount of Chǔ (楚子) was going to make Shāng Chén (商臣) his heir apparent,
and consulted the Prime Minister Zǐshàng (子上) about it.
Zǐshàng said:
"Your Majesty's age is not yet advanced,
and you have many favorites,
deposing him will lead to disorder.
The selection of heirs in the state of Chǔ (楚國),
has always favored the younger ones.
Moreover, this man,
has eyes like a wasp and a voice like a jackal,
he is a cruel man,
he cannot be established."
He did not listen.
Afterwards,
he wanted to establish Prince Zhí (王子職),
and depose the heir apparent Shāng Chén.
Shāng Chén heard of this but was not certain,
and said to his tutor Pān Chóng (潘崇):
"How can I be certain of it?"
Pān Chóng said:
"Feast Jiāng Mǐ (江羋)
and do not respect him."
He followed this advice.
Jiāng Mǐ was furious and said:
"Ah!
Menial!
It is fitting that the king wants to depose you and establish Zhí."
He told Pān Chóng, saying:
"It is true."
Pān Chóng said:
"Can you serve in various matters?"
He said:
"I cannot."
"Can you act?"
He said:
"I cannot."
"Can you carry out great affairs?"
He said:
"I can."
In the tenth month of winter,
he used the palace guards to surround King Chéng.
The King asked to eat bear paws and die.
They did not listen.
On the day dingwei,
the King hanged himself.
The posthumous name they gave him was
"Líng,"
but he did not close his eyes;
they called him
"Chéng,"
and then he closed his eyes.
King Mù was enthroned.
He gave his residence as heir apparent to Pān Chóng,
making him Grand Tutor,
and also put him in charge of the Yin of Huán Liè.
B6.1.8 Mù Bó went to Qí
to initiate the betrothal,
as was proper.
Whenever a ruler ascends the throne,
his ministers go out on simultaneous missions of betrothal,
to renew old alliances,
to seek external aid,
to befriend neighboring states,
in order to protect the state,
which is the way of loyalty, trust, humility, and deference.
Loyalty
is the correctness of virtue,
trust
is the firmness of virtue,
and humility and deference
are the foundation of virtue.
B6.1.9 After the Battle of Yáo,
the Jìn people had already returned the Qin commander,
the Qin grandees and attendants all spoke to the Duke of Qin, saying:
"This defeat
is the fault of Mèng Míng,
he must be killed."
The Duke of Qin said:
"This is my fault.
The poem of Ruì Liángfū of Zhou says:
'The great wind has tunnels,
greedy men ruin their kind.
Listening to words, then answering,'
Reciting words as if drunk.
Not using their good men,
On the contrary, they cause me to be confused.'
This is because of greed;
it speaks of me.
It was truly my greed that brought disaster upon you, sir;
what fault is there in you, sir?"
He restored him to his position of authority.
A6.2 *Annals of the Second Year of Duke Wén*
A6.2.1 In the spring of the second year,
in the second month of the King, on the day jiǎzǐ,
the Marquis of Jìn and the Qín army fought at Péngyá,
and the Qín army suffered a crushing defeat.
A6.2.2 On the day dīngchǒu,
they began building the palace of Princess Xī.
A6.2.3 In the third month, on the day yǐsì,
they made a covenant with Chǔ Fù of Jìn.
A6.2.4 In the sixth month of summer,
Gōngsūn Áo met with the Duke of Sòng,
the Marquis of Chén,
the Earl of Zhèng,
and Shì Hú of Jìn at Chuílǒng to form a covenant.
A6.2.5 From the twelfth month onward, there was no rain.
until the seventh month of autumn.
A6.2.6 On the day dīngmǎo of the eighth month,
a great ceremony was held at the Grand Temple,
and Duke Xī was ascended (to the ancestral tablets).
A6.2.7 In winter,
the people of Jìn,
the people of Sòng,
the people of Chén,
and the people of Zhèng attacked Qín.
A6.2.8 Gōngzǐ Suì went to Qí to present betrothal gifts.
B6.2 *Commentary on the Second Year of Duke Wén*
B6.2.1 In the spring of the second year,
Mèngmíng Shì of Qín led an army to attack Jìn,
to avenge the Battle of Yáo.
In the second month,
the Marquis of Jìn resisted them,
Xiān Qiějū commanded the central army,
Zhào Shuāi 趙衰 assisted him.
Wángguān Wúdì 王官無地 served as chariot driver,
and Hú Jújū 狐鞫居 was the charioteer's assistant.
On the day jiǎzǐ 甲子,
they engaged the Qin army in battle at Péngyá 彭衙,
and the Qin army was utterly defeated.
The people of Jin referred to the Qin
as the "army that came to bestow gifts."
In the battle at Yáo 殽,
Jìn Liáng Hóng 晉梁弘 drove the chariot,
and Lái Jū 萊駒 was the charioteer's assistant.
The day after the battle,
Duke Xiāng of Jìn 晉襄公 bound the Qin prisoners,
and ordered Lái Jū 萊駒 to execute them with a halberd.
The prisoner cried out,
Lái Jū 萊駒 dropped the halberd.
Láng Shěn 狼瞫 seized the halberd and executed the prisoner,
capturing him to ride with the Duke.
Consequently, he was made the charioteer's assistant.
During the campaign at Jī 箕,
Xiān Zhěn 先軫 demoted him,
and appointed Xù Jiǎnbó 續簡伯.
Láng Shěn 狼瞫 was furious.
His friend said,
"Why not die for it?"
Shěn 瞫 said,
"I have not yet found a suitable place to die."
His friend said,
"I will create difficulties for you."
Shěn 瞫 said,
"The *Zhōu Zhì* 周志 says:
'If one is brave, one will harm his superior,
and will not ascend to the Bright Hall.'
To die without righteousness,
is not bravery.
Working together is what is called bravery.
I used bravery to seek the position on the right,
and if I am dismissed because I lack bravery,
that is also what I should expect.
To say that the ruler does not know me,
and to be dismissed is appropriate,
then he knows me.
You should wait for it."
When they reached Péngyá 彭衙,
after they had arrayed
he charged the Qin 秦 army with his followers
and died there.
The Jin 晉 army followed them,
greatly defeating the Qin army.
The gentleman said,
"Láng Shěn 狼瞫 is therefore a gentleman.
The *Shī*
says: 'When the gentleman is like he is angry,
the chaos of the multitude will quickly be stopped.'
It also says:
'The king was exceedingly angry,
"Then he prepared his army."
To be angry and not cause chaos,
but instead to follow the army,
he can be called a *jūnzǐ*."
The Earl of Qín still employed Mèng Míng.
Mèng Míng further improved the governance of the state,
and heavily favored the people.
Zhào Chéngzǐ said to the various ministers,
"The Qín army has arrived again,
and we will surely avoid them.
To fear and increase virtue,
is something that cannot be confronted.
The *Shī* says:
'Do not forget your ancestors,
but cultivate their virtue.'
Mèng Míng has remembered this.
To not be remiss in remembering virtue,
how can he be opposed?"
B6.2.2 On *dīngchǒu* day,
the Xī princess was made.
The *shū*
was not timely.
B6.2.3 The people of Jìn, because the duke did not attend court,
came to punish him.
The duke went to Jìn.
In the fourth month, on *jǐsì* day,
the people of Jìn had Yáng Chùfǔ make a covenant with the duke
in order to humiliate him.
The *Book of Documents* says:
"When Jìn and Chǔ Fù made an alliance,"
in order to appease them.
Not recording the visit to Jìn
was to avoid mentioning it.
B6.2.4 Before the Duke arrived,
in the sixth month,
Mù Bó convened the lords
and the Sīkōng Shì Hú of Jìn made an alliance at Chuí Lǒng,
because Jìn was punishing Wèi for past offenses.
The text records
"Shì Hú,"
because he was capable of handling the matter.
The Marquis of Chén interceded with Jìn on behalf of Wèi, seeking peace,
and held Kǒng Dá to persuade them.
B6.2.5 In the autumn, the eighth month, on the day Dingmǎo,
a great ceremony was held at the Great Temple,
elevating Duke Xī,
which was a backward sacrifice.
Thereupon, Xiàfǔ Fú Jì, serving as Zōngbó,
honored Duke Xī,
and clearly stated,
"I see the new ghost as great,
so the old ghosts are small.
Prioritizing the great over the small
is proper.
Elevating the sages and worthies
is enlightened.
Brightness, obedience,
this is ritual propriety."
The gentleman considered this a breach of propriety:
"Ritual propriety is always about obedience.
Sacrifices
are great events of the state,
yet to go against them,
can this be called ritual propriety?
Even if you are perfectly sage,
you cannot eat before your father for long.
Therefore, Yǔ did not precede Gǔn,
Tāng did not precede Qiè,
Wén and Wǔ did not precede Bù Zhú.
The ancestor of Sòng was Dì Yǐ,
the ancestor of Zhèng was Lì Wáng,
these were still superior ancestors.
Therefore, the "Odes of Lǔ" says:
'In spring and autumn without fail,
the offerings and sacrifices are without error,
bright and grand is Sovereign Dì,
grand ancestor is Hòu Jì.'
The gentleman says,
'ritual propriety',
means that Hòu Jì is intimate
and precedes Dì.
The "Book of Odes" says:
'I ask my various aunts,
and then reach my elder sisters.'
The gentleman says
'ritual propriety',
means that the elder sister is intimate
and precedes the aunt."
Zhòng Ní said:
"Zāng Wénzhòng,
had three instances of being unbenevolent,
and three instances of being unknowing.
Demoting Zhǎn Qín (展禽),
abolishing the six border passes,
and having concubines weave cattails,
these are the three instances of unbenevolence.
Making empty vessels,
indulging in improper sacrifices,
and sacrificing to Yuán Jū (爰居),
these are the three instances of unknowing."
B6.2.6 In winter,
Xiān Qiějū (先且居) of Jìn (晉), Gōngzǐ Chéng (公子成) of Sòng (宋), Yuán Xuǎn (轅選) of Chén (陳), and Gōngzǐ Guīshēng (公子歸生) of Zhèng (鄭) attacked Qín (秦),
capturing Wāng (汪) and Péngyá (彭衙) and then returning,
to avenge the campaign of Péngyá.
The chronicle does not record the ministers,
because of Duke Mù (穆公),
showing respect to Qín,
and is called honoring virtue.
B6.2.7 Xiāng Zhòng (襄仲) went to Qí (齊) to deliver betrothal gifts;
this was proper ritual.
Whenever a ruler ascends the throne,
he fosters good relations with his maternal uncle and nephew,
To cultivate marriage,
to marry the principal wife in order to provide the sacrificial grains,
is filial piety.
Filial piety is the beginning of ritual.
A6.3 *The Annals of Duke Wén, Year 3*
A6.3.1 In the spring of the third year,
in the first month of the king,
Shūsūn Déchén 叔孫得臣 met with the men of Jìn 晉,
Sòng 宋,
Chén 陳,
Wèi 衛,
and Zhèng 鄭 to attack Shěn 沈.
Shěn collapsed.
A6.3.2 In the summer, in the fifth month,
Wángzǐ Hǔ 王子虎 died.
A6.3.3 The men of Qín 秦 attacked Jìn 晉.
A6.3.4 In the autumn,
the men of Chǔ 楚 besieged Jiāng 江.
A6.3.5 Locusts rained down on Sòng 宋.
A6.3.6 In the winter,
the duke went to Jìn 晉.
In the twelfth month, on the day jǐsì 己巳,
the duke and the lord of Jìn 晉 made a covenant.
A6.3.7 Yángchù Fù 陽處父 led an army to attack Chǔ 楚 in order to rescue Jiāng 江.
B6.3 *The Commentary on the Annals of Duke Wén, Year 3*
B6.3.1 In the spring of the third year,
Zhuāng Shū assembled the armies of the various lords to attack Shěn,
because it submitted to Chǔ.
Shěn collapsed.
When the common people flee from their superiors, it is called "collapse";
when superiors flee, it is called "escape."
B6.3.2 The Marquis of Wèi went to Chén
to pay homage for the success of Jìn.
B6.3.3 In the fourth month, yǐ hài,
Wáng Shū Wén Gōng died,
and an envoy came to report the event.
Condolences were offered as to an ally,
according to propriety.
B6.3.4 The Earl of Qín attacked Jìn,
crossing the river and burning the boats,
taking Wáng Guān and the suburbs.
The people of Jìn did not come out to fight.
He then crossed from Máo Jīn,
buried the corpses at Xiáo and returned.
He then became the hegemon of the Western Rong,
through the use of Mèng Míng.
Therefore, gentlemen know
"When Qín Mù Gōng 秦穆公 was ruler,
he selected men comprehensively,
and he was unified with the people.
When Mèng Míng 孟明 was a minister,
when he did not understand,
he was able to fear and ponder.
When Zǐ Sāng 子桑 was loyal,
when he knew men,
he was able to promote the good.
The *Shī* (Book of Poetry) says,
'Where do they gather the fán (white artemisia)?
At the swamp and on the small island.
Where do they use it?
For the affairs of the dukes and lords.'
Qín Mù 秦穆 had this.
'Not relaxing early and late,
to serve one man,'
Mèng Míng 孟明 had this.
'Planning for his descendants,
to shelter his sons like wings,'
Zǐ Sāng 子桑 had this."
B6.3.5 In autumn,
grasshoppers rained down on Sòng 宋,
falling in heaps and dying.
B6.3.6 The Chǔ 楚 army besieged Jiāng 江;
Xiān Pú 先僕 of Jìn 晉 attacked Chǔ 楚 to rescue Jiāng 江.
In winter,
Jìn 晉, on account of Jiāng 江, informed the Zhōu 周 court.
Wáng Shū Huán Gōng 王叔桓公
and Yáng Chù Fù 陽處父 of Jìn 晉 attacked Chǔ 楚 to rescue Jiāng 江,
going as far as the gates of Fāngchéng 方城,
encountered Zhū 朱, the son of the lord of Xī 息, and then returned.
B6.3.7 The people of Jìn 晉, fearing that he would be disrespectful to the duke,
requested to revise the alliance.
The duke [of Lǔ] went to Jìn
and allied with the Marquis of Jìn.
The Marquis of Jìn hosted the duke [of Lǔ] with a feast
and recited the poem "Jīng Jīng Zhě É" (Luxuriant is the Artemisia) [from the *Book of Poetry*].
Zhuāng Shū had the duke descend [from the dais]
and bow.
He said,
"Small states receive orders from large states;
how dare we not be careful with rituals?
You, my lord, bestow upon us great courtesy;
what joy could be greater than this?
Moreover, the joy of a small state
is the benevolence of a large state."
The Marquis of Jìn descended [from the dais],
declined [the honor],
ascended [again],
and completed the bow.
The duke [of Lǔ] recited the poem "Jiā Lè" (Great Joy) [from the *Book of Poetry*].
A6.4 [*Chunqiu*] Duke Wén, Year 4 [Chronicle]
A6.4.1 In the fourth year, spring,
the duke returned from Jìn.
A6.4.2 In summer, Nì Fù Jiāng was brought back from Qí.
A6.4.3 The Dí invaded Qí.
A6.4.4 In autumn, the Chǔ people destroyed Jiāng.
A6.4.6 The Marquis of Wèi sent Níng Yú to come and pay a formal visit.
A6.4.7 In winter, on the rén yín day of the eleventh month, Fū Rén Fēng Shì died.
B6.4 *Commentary on the Fourth Year of Duke Wén*
B6.4.1 In the spring of the fourth year, the Jìn people returned Kǒng Dá to Wèi, considering him to be good for Wèi, and therefore released him.
B6.4.2 In summer, the Marquis of Wèi went to Jìn to pay respects.
B6.4.3 The Earl of Cáo went to Jìn for an assembly.
B6.4.4 Nì Fù Jiāng was brought back from Qí.
If a high minister does not go, it is against propriety.
Therefore, the superior man knows that Chū Jiāng was not pleased in Lǔ, saying:
He said:
Therefore, a superior man knew that Chū Jiāng (出姜) would not be accepted in Lǔ (魯).
"To value her betrothal but slight her welcome,
To treat her as a ruler but demean her,
To establish her but then depose her,
To abandon trust
and undermine her lord,
in the state, there will surely be chaos;
in the family, there will surely be ruin.
It is fitting that she is not accepted!
The *Shī* [Book of Odes] says:
'Fearing the majesty of Heaven,
At all times preserve it,'
This speaks of respecting one's lord."
The Marquis of Jìn (晉) attacked Qín (秦),
besieging Yuán (邧)
and Xīnchéng (新城),
to avenge the campaign of Wáng Guān (王官).
B6.4.6 The Chǔ (楚) people destroyed Jiāng (江).
The Earl of Qín (秦伯) wore mourning clothes for it,
and went out to reside in a side chamber,
not holding court,
and going past the prescribed number of days for mourning.
The high officials remonstrated.
The Earl said:
"When an ally is destroyed,
even if I cannot save them,
How dare I not be cautious?
I myself am fearful."
The *jūnzǐ* said:
"The *Shī* says,
'Those two states,
their governance was not successful;
These four states,
they were thoroughly examined and measured,'
it speaks of Qín Mù Gōng."
B6.4.7 Wèi Níng Wǔzǐ came to visit.
The duke feasted with him,
and recited the poems "Zhàn Lù" (湛露) and "Tóng Gōng" (彤弓).
He did not decline [the honor],
nor did he respond with a poem.
The duke sent an officer to ask him privately.
He replied:
"Your servant believes that this is for practice
and that it applies to this situation.
In the past, when the lords paid homage to the king on the first day of the year,
the king feasted and entertained them.
At that time, he would recite 'Zhàn Lù' (湛露),
indicating that the Son of Heaven was in the light [of good fortune],
and the lords were at his command.
When the lords resisted what the king hated [enemies],
and presented their accomplishments,
the king would then bestow upon them one red bow,
one hundred red arrows,
and one thousand black bows and arrows,
to acknowledge and reward the feast.
Now, as an accompanying minister, I have come to continue the old friendship.
You, my lord, have condescended to favor me.
How dare I presume upon such a great ceremony to bring about offense?"
B6.4.8 In winter,
Chéng Fēng passed away.
A6.5 *The Annals of Duke Wén, Year Five*
A6.5.1 In the fifth year, in spring,
in the first month of the king,
the king sent Róng Shū to bring the burial shroud,
and also funeral gifts.
A6.5.2 In the third month, on the day xinhai,
we buried our minor consort, Chéng Fēng.
A6.5.3 The king sent Zhào Bó to attend the funeral.
A6.5.4 In summer,
Gōngsūn Áo went to Jìn.
A6.5.5 The people of Qín entered Ruò.
A6.5.6 In autumn,
the people of Chǔ destroyed Lù.
A6.5.7 In winter, in the tenth month, on the day jiǎshēn,
the Viscount of Xǔ, Yè, died.
B6.5 *The Commentary on Duke Wén, Year Five*
B6.5.1 In the fifth year, in spring,
the king sent Róng Shū to bring the burial shroud and funeral gifts, and
summoned Zhào Zhāo Gōng to attend the funeral.
This was proper etiquette.
B6.5.2 Initially,
Ruò rebelled against Chǔ and sided with Qín,
but then wavered again towards Chǔ.
In the summer,
the people of Qín entered Ruò.
B6.5.3 The Six clans rebelled against Chǔ and sided with the Eastern Yí.
In the autumn,
Chǔ's Chéng Dàxīn and
Zhòng Guī led troops to extinguish the Six.
B6.5.4 In the winter,
Chǔ's Gōngzǐ Xiè extinguished Liǎo.
Zāng Wénzhòng, hearing of the destruction of the Six and Liǎo,
said,
"Gāo Yáo and
Tíng Jiān are no longer venerated!
If virtue is not established,
and the people have no support,
how sad!"
B6.5.5 Jìn's Yáng Chǔfǔ was sent on a diplomatic mission to Wèi.
On his return, he passed by Níng.
Níng Yíng accompanied him.
He went as far as Wēn and then returned.
His wife asked him about it.
Yíng said:
"It was based on rigidity.
The *Shang Shu* says:
'The deeply entrenched gradually succumb to rigidity;
the lofty and insightful succumb to gentleness.'
If the master only relies on one,
will he not be submerged?
Heaven possesses the virtue of rigidity,
yet it does not interfere with the seasons.
How much less should a person?
Moreover, to be flowery but without substance
is where resentment gathers.
To offend and gather resentment
is not a way to establish oneself firmly.
I fear that I would not gain any benefit but would instead encounter difficulty,
and that is why I left."
The Jìn officials Zhào Chéngzǐ, Luán Zhēnzǐ, Huò Bó, and Jiù Jì all died.
A6.6 *The Sixth Year of Duke Wén Chronicle*
A6.6.1 In the spring of the sixth year,
the Xǔ Xīgōng was buried.
A6.6.2 In the summer,
Jìsūn Hángfǔ went to Chén.
A6.6.3 In the autumn,
Jìsūn Hángfǔ went to Jìn.
A6.6.4 In the eighth month, on the day yǐhài,
the Jìn ruler Huān died.
A6.6.5 In the tenth month of winter,
Gōngzǐ Suì went to Jìn.
A6.6.6 The funeral of Duke Xiāng of Jìn was held.
A6.6.7 Jìn killed its grand master, Yáng Chùfǔ.
A6.6.8 Hú Shègū of Jìn fled to the Dí people.
A6.6.9 In the intercalary month, the new moon was not announced,
yet the court still paid homage at the temple.
B6.6 "Biography of the Sixth Year of Duke Wén"
B6.6.1 In the spring of the sixth year,
Jìn conducted a military review at Yí,
and dismissed two armies.
He made Hú Shègū commander of the central army,
with Zhào Dùn assisting him.
Yáng Chùfǔ arrived from Wēn,
and the review was changed to Dǒng,
replacing the central army.
Master Yáng,
He belonged to the faction of Chéng Jì
, therefore he sided with the Zhào clan
, and furthermore said that Zhào Dùn was capable
, saying
: "If he is capable
, it is beneficial to the state."
Therefore, he promoted him.
Xuān Zǐ from this point onward began to manage the state affairs
, establishing rules and regulations
, correcting legal punishments
, investigating legal cases and executions
, overseeing fugitives
, proceeding according to the evidence and important points
, clearing up old grievances
, basing actions on proper etiquette
, continuing regular duties
, and releasing those detained for too long
. After completion
, he gave these to the Grand Tutor Yáng Zǐ and the Grand Master Jiǎ Tuó
, to implement them in the state of Jìn
, as standing laws.
B6.6.2 Zāng Wénzhòng, because of the harmony between Chén and Wèi
, wished to seek amity with Chén.
In summer
, Jì Wénzǐ
went to Chén as an envoy
, and also took a wife there.
B6.6.3 Duke Mù of Qín, Rèn Hǎo, died
He took the three sons of the Zǐchē clan, Yǎn Xī, Zhòng Háng, and Zhēn Hǔ, to be buried alive with him;
all of them were excellent men of Qín.
The people of the state grieved for them
and composed the "Yellow Bird" poem.
The junzi said:
"It is fitting that Duke Mù of Qín was not a leader of the alliance!
He died and abandoned the people.
When former kings passed away,
they still bequeathed laws to them,
how much more so should they not have deprived them of good men?
The *Shī* says:
'When that man is gone,
the state is utterly exhausted.'
This means having no good men.
How could he deprive them of such men?
The ancient kings knew that their lives were not long,
therefore they simultaneously established sages and wise men,
established their reputation,
divided their income,
recorded their sayings,
made laws and standards for them,
displayed the extremes of their skills,
promoted their exemplary behavior,
gave them legal systems,
announced their teachings,
taught them how to prevent harm,
entrusted them with regular positions,
guided them with ritual principles,
so that they would not lose the appropriateness of their land,
and the multitudes relied on them;
and then they accepted their fate.
The sage kings acted in the same way.
Now, he abandons the law
to bequeath to future generations.
He is fond of goodness and is senior [in age],
the late lord loved him,
and he is also close to Qín.
Qín
and we have an old friendship.
Installing Shàn would be secure,
serving the senior would be compliant,
establishing one beloved would be filial,
and renewing the old alliance would be peaceful.
Because there are difficulties,
therefore, I want to establish the senior lord.
If one possesses these four virtues,
the difficulties will surely be resolved."
Jiǎ Jì said:
"It would be better to install Gōngzǐ Yuè.
Chén Yíng was favored by two lords,
if we install her son,
the people will surely be at peace with it."
Zhào Mèng said:
"Chén Yíng is of low status,
ranking among the nine concubines,
how can her son have any power to awe [the people]?
Moreover, being favored by two lords
is licentious.
As the son of the former lord,
he was unable to seek greatness
and instead resided in a small state,
which is evasive.
When the mother is licentious and the son is evasive,
there is no authority.
When the state of Chén 陳 is small and distant,
there is no support.
Where can the ruler find peace?
Dù Qí 杜祁, for the sake of the ruler,
yielded to Bī Jí 偪姞 and placed her above himself.
For the sake of the Dí 狄 people,
he yielded to Jì Wěi 季隗 and placed himself next to her.
Therefore, his position was fourth.
The late ruler therefore loved his son
and had him serve in Qín 秦,
making him a vice-minister there.
Qín 秦 is large and nearby,
sufficient to be a source of support.
The mother is righteous, and the son is loved;
sufficient to command respect from the people.
Establishing him,
would that not be acceptable?"
He sent Xiān Miè 先蔑 and Shì Huì 士會 to Qín 秦 to bring back Gongzi Yōng 公子雍.
Jiǎ Jì 賈季 also sent someone to summon Gongzi Lè 公子樂 from Chén 陳.
Zhào Mèng 趙孟 had him killed in Pí 郫.
B6.6.6 Jiǎ Jì 賈季 resented Yáng Chùfǔ 陽處父 for usurping his position,
and knowing that he had no support in Jìn 晉,
in the ninth month,
Jiǎ Jì 賈季 had Xù Jūjū 續鞫居 kill Yáng Chùfǔ 陽處父.
The chronicle states:
"Jìn 晉 killed its grand master,"
encroaching upon the office.
B6.6.7 In the tenth month of winter,
Xiāng Zhòng 襄仲 went to Jìn 晉 to attend the funeral of Duke Xiāng 襄公.
B6.6.8 On the day bǐngyín 丙寅 of the eleventh month,
Jìn 晉 killed Xù Jiǎnbó 續簡伯.
Jiǎ Jì 賈季 fled to the Dí 狄.
Xuān Zǐ (宣子) sent Yú Pián (臾駢) to escort his family and possessions.
At the hunt of Yí (夷),
Jiǎ Jì (賈季) executed Yú Pián (臾駢).
Yú Pián's (臾駢) people wanted to kill all of the Jiǎ (賈) clan to avenge him.
Yú Pián (臾駢) said:
"No.
I have heard it said in past records:
'Requite kindness with kindness,
and resentment with resentment,
but not on future generations;
this is the way of loyalty.'
Our master treated Jiǎ Jì (賈季) with courtesy,
and if I were to use that favor to repay personal resentment,
would that not be improper?
To make use of another's favor
is not courage.
To diminish resentment
and increase enmity
is not wisdom.
To harm the public for private gain
is not loyalty.
If I abandon these three principles, how can I serve our master?"
They fully prepared his family, their utensils, and their wealth,
personally leading and protecting them,
and escorted them to the border.
B6.6.9 In the intercalary month, not announcing the first day of the month
was contrary to ritual.
Intercalary months are used to correct the seasons,
the seasons are used to conduct affairs,
and affairs are used to enrich the people's livelihood.
The way to sustain the people lies in this.
Not announcing the beginning of the lunar month in a leap month
is abandoning timely governance.
How can this serve the people?
A6.7 *Wén Gōng* (Duke Wen), Seventh Year, *Jīng* (Classic)
A6.7.1 Seventh year, spring,
the Duke attacked *Zhū*.
A6.7.2 In the third month, *jiǎxū* day,
he captured *Xūjù*.
A6.7.3 And then fortified *Wū*.
A6.7.4 In the summer, fourth month,
*Sòng Gōng* (Duke of Song), *Wáng Chén*, died.
A6.7.5 The people of *Sòng* killed their high official.
A6.7.6 On *wùzǐ* day,
The people of Jìn and the people of Qín fought at Lìnghú.
Xiān Miè of Jìn fled to Qín.
A6.7.7 The Dí invaded our western borders.
A6.7.8 In the autumn, the eighth month,
the duke met with the various lords,
and the grand masters of Jìn formed an alliance at Hù.
A6.7.9 In the winter,
Xú attacked Jǔ.
A6.7.10 Gōngsūn Áo went to Jǔ to oversee the alliance.
B6.7 *Zuǒ Zhuàn*, Year 7 of Duke Wén
B6.7.1 In the spring of the seventh year,
the duke attacked Zhū,
taking advantage of the difficulties in Jìn.
B6.7.2 In the third month, on the day jiǎxū,
he captured Xūgōu,
placing a son of Duke Wén there,
which was not in accordance with ritual.
B6.7.3 In the summer, the fourth month,
Duke Chéng of Sòng died.
Thereupon, Gōngzǐ Chéng became the Right Preceptor,
Gōngsūn Yǒu became the Left Preceptor,
Yuè Yù became the Minister of War,
Lín Guàn served as the Minister of Instruction (司徒, Sītú),
Gōngzǐ Dàng served as the Minister of the City (司城, Sīchéng),
and Huá Yùshì served as the Minister of Crime (司寇, Sīkòu).
Duke Zhāo was planning to remove the group of 公子 (gōngzǐ, sons of the ruler),
and Yuè Yù said,
"It is not permissible.
The 公族 (gōngzú, members of the ducal clan)
are the branches and leaves of the ducal house.
If you remove them,
then the roots will have no place to find shelter.
Even vines are able to shelter their roots,
therefore the wise man uses this as an analogy.
How much more so should a ruler of a state?
This is what the proverb means when it says,
'Providing shelter
and then allowing axes to be used to seek them out.'
It absolutely must not be done.
You must consider this!
Treat them kindly with virtue,
and they will all be your arms and legs.
Who would dare to harbor disloyalty?
Why would you remove them?"
He did not listen.
The lineages of Duke Mù and Duke Xiāng
led the people of the state to attack the duke,
killing Gōngsūn Gù and Gōngsūn Zhèng in the ducal palace.
The six ministers reconciled with the ducal house,
Yuè Yù relinquished the position of Sīmǎ
to give way to Gōngzǐ Áng.
Zhāo Gōng ascended the throne and held the funeral.
The *Spring and Autumn Annals* records: “The people of Sòng killed their Grand Master,”
without stating his name,
because it was a collective action,
and also implying he was not guilty.
B6.7.4 Qín Kāng Gōng sent Gōngzǐ Yōng to Jìn,
saying:
“When Duke Wén entered [Jìn],
he had no guards,
hence the difficulties with Lǚ and Xì.”
Therefore, he provided him with many followers as guards.
Mù Yíng daily held the heir apparent
and wept at court,
saying:
“What crime did the late ruler commit?
What crime has his heir committed?
Abandoning the rightful heir and not establishing him,
but seeking a ruler from outside,
where will you place this child?”
After leaving the court,
she would take him to the Zhào clan,
bowing her head to Xuān Zǐ,
saying:
“The late ruler entrusted this child to you,
saying:
‘If this child is talented,
"I received your favor;
being untalented,
I only inspire resentment in you."
Now, although our lord has passed away,
his words are still ringing in my ears,
and you abandon them,
how can you do this?"
Xuān Zǐ and the other senior officials were all troubled by Mù Yíng,
and also feared her pressure,
so they went against Xiān Miè
and installed Líng Gōng,
in order to resist the Qín army.
Jī Zhèng remained to guard the capital.
Zhào Dùn commanded the central army,
with Xiān Kè assisting him;
Xún Línfù assisted the upper army;
Xiān Miè commanded the lower army,
with Xiān Dū assisting him.
Bù Zhāo was the charioteer,
and Róng Jīn was the right-hand man.
When they arrived at Jǐn Yīn,
Xuān Zǐ said:
"If we accept Qin,
Qin will be our guest;
if we do not accept them,
they will be our enemy.
Since we have already refused them,
and then delay our army,
The general of Qín (秦), Shēng Xīn (生心), harbored ambition.
"Our ancestors had the will to seize from others;
This is the skillful planning of an army.
Chasing the enemy like pursuing fugitives;
This is the excellent administration of an army."
Training the soldiers,
Sharpening the weapons,
Feeding the horses,
Preparing early meals,
Secretly mobilizing the army at night.
On the day *wùzǐ* (戊子),
They defeated the Qín (秦) army at Lìnghú (令狐),
Reaching Kūshǒu (刳首).
On the day *jǐchǒu* (己丑),
Xiān Miè (先蔑) fled to Qín (秦),
Shì Huì (士會) followed him.
When Xiān Miè (先蔑) was about to set out,
Xún Línfù (荀林父) stopped him,
Saying:
"The Lady and the Heir Apparent are still here,
Yet you seek a ruler from outside;
This will surely not succeed.
Why not decline with illness?
What do you think?
If not,
Calamity will befall you.
Appointing another minister to go instead,
Is acceptable,
Why must it be you?
Those in the same office are colleagues,
We were once colleagues,
How could I not do my best?"
He did not listen.
He composed three stanzas of the Ode *Bǎn* (板) for him,
and he did not listen.
When he fled,
Xún Bó completely sent his wealth and his utensils and property to Qín,
saying:
"It is because we were colleagues."
Shì Huì stayed in Qín for three years
without seeing Shì Bó.
Someone said:
"He was able to cause a man to flee the state,
but cannot be seen here,
what use is he?"
Shì Jì said:
"I share the same guilt with him.
It is not righteous of me to see him.
How can I see him?"
When he returned,
he finally did not see him.
B6.7.5 The Dí invaded our western borders.
The Duke sent word to Jìn.
Zhào Xuānzǐ had Jiǎ Jì ask Fēng Shū and
moreover reproach him.
Fēng Shū asked Jiǎ Jì, saying:
"Zhào Shuāi and Zhào Dùn, who is more virtuous?"
The answer was:
"Zhào Shuāi is like the sun in winter;
Zhào Dùn is like the sun in summer."
Zhào Dùn
is like the sun in summer."

B6.7.6 In the eighth month of autumn, the Marquis of Qí, Duke of Sòng, Marquis of Wèi, Marquis of Chén, Earl of Zhèng, Viscount of Xǔ, and Earl of Cáo met with Zhào Dùn of Jìn at Hù and formed an alliance.
The Marquis of Jìn established the former order.
The Duke arrived late,
therefore, the location of the meeting was not recorded.
Generally, when meeting with the feudal lords,
if the location of the meeting is not recorded,
it is because of lateness.
Arriving late,
not recording the state involved
avoids mentioning their tardiness.
B6.7.7 Mù Bó took a wife from Jǔ,
named Dài Jǐ,
who gave birth to Wén Bó.
Her younger sister, Shēng Jǐ, gave birth to Huì Shū.
After Dài Jǐ died,
he again sought a wife from Jǔ.
The people of Jǔ declined, using Shēng Jǐ as the reason.
Then, he arranged for Xiāng Zhòng to betroth her.
In winter,
Xú attacked Jǔ.
The people of Jǔ came to request an alliance.
Mù Bó went to Jǔ to oversee the alliance,
Moreover, he took Zhòng Nì (仲逆).
When they arrived at Yānlíng (鄢陵),
he ascended the city wall and saw her.
She was beautiful,
so he took her for himself as a wife.
Zhòng (仲) requested to attack him.
The Duke was about to permit it,
but Shūzhòng Huìbó (叔仲惠伯) remonstrated,
saying:
"I have heard it said:
'If warfare arises internally, it is called rebellion;
if it arises externally, it is called invasion.'
Invasion may still affect others,
but rebellion affects oneself.'
Now, if your subject rebels and you, my lord, do not prohibit it,
thereby inciting hostility,
what will become of us?"
The Duke stopped it.
Huìbó (惠伯) reconciled them,
causing Zhòng (仲) to abandon the feud.
Gōngsūn Áo (公孫敖) reversed this decision,
and they became brothers again as before.
He followed his advice.
[B6.7.8] Jìn (晉) Xì Quē (郤缺) said to Zhào Xuānzǐ (趙宣子):
"In the past, Wèi (衛) was not harmonious,
therefore we took their territory.
Now they are harmonious,
so we can return it to them.
To rebel and not punish,
how can you display your power?
To submit but not be gentle,
how can you display your benevolence?
If you are neither powerful nor benevolent,
how can you display your virtue?
Without virtue,
how can you lead the alliance?
You, sir, as a senior minister,
to preside over the feudal lords,
but you do not focus on virtue,
what will you do?
The *Xià Shū* says:
“Warn them to use rest,
control them with authority,
encourage them with the 'Nine Songs,'
do not let them go bad.”
The virtues of the Nine Accomplishments are all worthy of song,
hence they are called the "Nine Songs."
The Six Treasuries and Three Affairs
are called the Nine Accomplishments.
Water, fire, metal, wood, earth, and grain
are called the Six Treasuries;
rectifying virtue, promoting utility, and enriching life
are called the Three Affairs.
To act justly and implement it
is called virtue and ritual.
Without ritual, there is no joy,
the reason for rebellion.
With your virtue, my son,
there is nothing to sing about;
who would come to you?
Why not have those who are friendly sing about you?"
Xuān Zǐ was pleased by this.
A6.8 *The Annals of the Eighth Year of Duke Wén*
A6.8.1 In the eighth year, spring,
the king's first month.
A6.8.2 Summer, fourth month.
A6.8.3 Autumn, eighth month, wùshēn,
the Heavenly King died.
A6.8.4 Winter, tenth month, rénwǔ,
Gōngzǐ Suì met with Zhào Dùn of Jìn,
and they swore an alliance at Héngyōng.
A6.8.5 yǐyǒu,
Gōngzǐ Suì met with the Luò Róng,
and they swore an alliance at Bào.
A6.8.6 Gōngsūn Áo went to the capital,
but did not arrive and returned. On bǐngxū,
he fled to Jǔ.
A6.8.7 Locusts.
A6.8.8 A man of Sòng killed his grand master, Sīmǎ.
The Sòng minister of works came to seek refuge.
B6.8 *Commentary on the Eighth Year of Duke Wén*
B6.8.1 In the spring of the eighth year,
the Marquis of Jìn sent Xiè Yáng to return the fields of Kuāng and Qī to Wèi,
and also restored the fief of Chí, the duke's son-in-law,
from Shēn to the border of Hǔláo.
B6.8.2 In the summer,
the people of Qín attacked Jìn,
taking Wǔchéng,
to avenge the campaign of Lìnghú.
B6.8.3 In the autumn,
King Xiāng died.
B6.8.4 The people of Jìn used the covenant of Hù to come and punish.
In winter,
Xiāng Zhòng met with Zhào Mèng of Jìn
to make a covenant at Héngyōng,
to retaliate against the covenant of Hù.
Thereupon, he met with the Róng people of Yī and Luò.
The text says "Gōngzǐ Suì",
valuing him.
B6.8.5 Mù Bó went to Zhōu to express condolences,
Did not arrive,
and fled to Jǔ with gifts,
following the Jǐ clan there.
B6.8.6 Sòng Xiāng Fūrén,
was the elder sister of King Xiāng,
but Duke Zhāo did not treat her with respect.
The Fūrén, relying on the Dài clan,
then killed Kǒng Shū, grandson of Duke Xiāng, Gōngsūn Zhōnglí, and Grand Sīmǎ, Gōngzǐ Áng,
all of whom were of Duke Zhāo's faction.
The Sīmǎ, Wò, maintained his integrity and died,
so it is written with his official title.
Sīchéng Dàng Yìzhū came to defect,
showing his loyalty to the people of the palace and escaping.
The Duke used his official title to welcome him,
and restored them all to their positions.
It is also written with their official titles,
to show that they were all esteemed.
B6.8.7 At the hunt in Yí,
the Marquis of Jìn was about to appoint Jī Zhèngfǔ and Xiān Dū to the central army,
and send Shì Hú and Liáng Yì'ěr to lead the central army.
Xiān Kè said:
"The merits of Hú and Zhào
cannot be abandoned."
They followed his advice.
Xiān Kè seized Kuǎi Dé's fields in Jǐnyīn.
Therefore, Jī Zhèngfǔ, Xiān Dū, Shì Hú, Liáng Yì'ěr, and Kuǎi Dé caused a rebellion.
A6.9 *The Ninth Year of Duke Wén [Chronicle]*
A6.9.1 In the spring of the ninth year,
the Earl of Máo came to request metal.
A6.9.2 The Fūrén, Jiāng Shì, went to Qí.
A6.9.3 In the second month,
Shūsūn Déchén went to the capital.
On the day xīncǒu,
Xiāng Wáng was buried.
A6.9.4 The people of Jìn killed their grand master, Xiān Dū.
A6.9.5 In the third month,
Fūrén Jiāng Shì arrived from Qí.
A6.9.6 The people of Jìn killed their grand masters Shì Hú and Jī Zhèngfù.
A6.9.7 The people of Chǔ attacked Zhèng.
A6.9.8 Gōngzǐ Suì met with the people of Jìn,
the people of Sòng,
the people of Wèi,
and the people of Xǔ to rescue Zhèng.
A6.9.9 In the summer,
the Dí invaded Qí.
A6.9.10 In the eighth month of autumn,
Cáo Bó Xiāng died.
A6.9.11 In the ninth month, on the day guǐyǒu,
there was an earthquake.
A6.9.12 In winter,
the Viscount of Chǔ sent Jiāo to come for a formal visit.
A6.9.13 The people of Qín came to return the burial clothes of Duke Xī and
Chéng Fēng.
A6.9.14 The funeral of Duke Gòng of Cáo was held.
B6.9 *Zuǒ Zhuàn*, Ninth Year of Duke Wén.
B6.9.1 In the ninth year, in spring,
in the first month of the king, on the day jǐyǒu,
someone was sent to assassinate Xiān Kè.
On yǐchǒu,
the people of Jìn killed Xiān Dū and Liáng Yì'ěr.
B6.9.2 Máo Bó Wèi came to seek gold,
which was not in accordance with propriety.
The king's command was not recorded,
because the king had not yet been buried.
B6.9.3 In the second month,
Zhuāng Shū went to Zhōu
to bury King Xiāng.
B6.9.4 In the third month, on the day jiǎxū,
The people of Jìn killed Jī Zhèngfǔ,
Shì Hú,
and Kuǎi Dé.
Fàn Shān said to the ruler of Chǔ:
"The ruler of Jìn is young
and not respected among the lords.
The northern regions can be taken."
The ruler of Chǔ stationed his army at Lángyuān to attack Zhèng.
He captured Gōngzǐ Jiān, Gōngzǐ Máng, and Yuè Ěr.
Zhèng then made peace with Chǔ.
Gōngzǐ Suì met with Zhào Dùn of Jìn, Huá Ǒu of Sòng, Kǒng Dá of Wèi, and a grandee of Xǔ to rescue Zhèng,
but they did not reach the Chǔ army in time.
It is not recorded as a mission of a high minister,
as it was slow
in order to punish the disrespect.
In summer,
Chǔ invaded Chén
and captured Húqiū,
because it had submitted to Jìn.
In autumn,
Gōngzǐ Zhū of Chǔ attacked Chén from the eastern Yí tribes.
The people of Chén defeated him
and captured Gōngzǐ Fèi.
Chén was afraid
and subsequently made peace with Chǔ.
In winter,
Yuè Jiāo, a noble of Chǔ, came to visit,
and held the gifts with arrogance.
Shūzhòng Huìbó said:
"This will certainly lead to the destruction of the Ruò'áo clan.
They were arrogant towards their former lord,
and the spirits will not bless them."
B6.9.10 The people of Qín came to return the burial clothes of Xīgōng and
Chéngfēng,
which was proper.
When feudal lords visited each other to offer condolences or congratulations,
even if it was not their immediate concern,
as long as they followed proper etiquette,
it was recorded,
so as not to forget old friendships.
A6.10 *Annals, Year 10 of Duke Wén*
A6.10.1 In the tenth year, in spring,
in the third month of the king, on the day xinmao,
Zāngsūn Chén died.
A6.10.2 In summer,
Qín attacked Jìn.
A6.10.3 Chǔ killed its grand master Yí Shēn.
A6.10.4 From the first month, there was no rain,
until the seventh month of autumn.
A6.10.5 Then Sūzǐ made a covenant at Nǚlì.
A6.10.6 In winter,
the Dí invaded Sòng.
A6.10.7 The Viscount of Chǔ and
the Marquis of Cài were stationed at Juéhé.
B6.10 *Zuǒ Zhuàn*, Year 10 of Duke Wén (文公十年傳)
B6.10.1 In the spring of the tenth year, the people of Jìn (晉) attacked Qín (秦) and
took Shào Liáng (少梁).
B6.10.2 In the summer,
the Count of Qín (秦伯) attacked Jìn (晉) and
took Běi Zhēng (北徵).
B6.10.3 Initially,
the Chǔ (楚) diviner Fàn Wū Yù Sì (范巫矞似) told King Chéng (成王), Zǐ Yù (子玉), and
Zǐ Xī (子西), saying:
"The three lords will all die violent deaths."
During the Battle of Chéngpú (城濮之役),
the King thought of this,
so he sent someone to stop Zǐ Yù (子玉), saying:
"Do not die."
It was too late.
He tried to stop Zǐ Xī (子西).
Zǐ Xī (子西) hanged himself, but the rope broke.
The King's envoy arrived just in time,
and stopped him,
making him the Duke of Shāng (商公).
Following the Hàn River and going up the Jiāng River,
they were about to enter Yǐng.
The king was at Zhǔ Palace,
descended,
and met with him.
He was fearful
and excused himself, saying:
"I was spared from death,
but there are slanderous words again,
saying that I was going to flee.
I would rather return and die at the hands of the Sībài (司敗)."
The king appointed him as Gōngyǐn (工尹),
and later he conspired with Zǐ Jiā (子家) to assassinate King Mù (穆王).
King Mù (穆王) heard of it,
and in the fifth month,
killed Dòu Yíshēn (鬭宜申) and Zhòng Guī (仲歸).
B6.10.4 In the seventh month of autumn,
he allied with Sū Zǐ (蘇子) at Nǚlì (女栗),
because King Qǐng (頃王) was established.
B6.10.5 The Marquis of Chén (陳侯) and the Count of Zhèng (鄭伯) met with the Viscount of Chǔ (楚子) at Xī (息).
In winter,
they then encamped with the Marquis of Cài (蔡侯) at Juéhé (厥貉),
intending to attack Sòng (宋).
Huá Yùshì (華御事) of Sòng (宋) said:
"Chǔ (楚) wants to weaken us;
should we weaken ourselves first?
Why must they entice us?
If we are indeed incapable,
"What crime have the people committed?"
He then opposed the ruler of Chǔ.
The people were weary but obedient.
Thereupon, a path was cleared to allow hunting at Mèng Zhū.
The Duke of Sòng was the right-hand attendant,
and the Earl of Zhèng was the left-hand attendant.
Qísī Gōng, Fù Suì, was once again made Right Sīmǎ,
Zǐ Zhū and Wén Zhī’s Wúwèi were appointed as the left-hand Sīmǎ.
He ordered an early departure carrying the fire-lighting equipment.
The Duke of Sòng disobeyed the order.
Wúwèi flogged his servant as a warning.
Someone said to Zǐ Zhōu:
"A ruler of a state cannot be punished!"
Zǐ Zhōu said:
"When one is in office, one must act accordingly.
What constraint is there?
The *Shī* says:
'When hard, he does not reject;
when soft, he does not swallow.'
'Do not indulge in deceitful compliance,
so as to carefully avoid limitless trouble.'
This is not like avoiding force.
How dare I love life and disrupt official duties?"
B6.10.6 At the gathering at Jue (厥), the Rong (貉) tribes
The chief of Jūn (麇) fled back.
A6.11 *The Annals of the Eleventh Year of Duke Wén*
A6.11.1 In the spring of the eleventh year,
the ruler of Chǔ attacked Jūn.
A6.11.2 In summer,
Shū Péngshēng met with Xì Quē of Jìn at Chéngkuāng.
A6.11.3 In autumn,
the Count of Cáo came to court.
A6.11.4 Gōngzǐ Suì went to Sòng.
A6.11.5 The Dí invaded Qí.
A6.11.6 In winter, the tenth month, on the day jiǎ-wǔ,
Shūsūn Déchén defeated the Dí at Xián.
B6.11 *Commentary on the Eleventh Year of Duke Wén*
B6.11.1 In the eleventh year, in spring,
the Chǔ ruler attacked Jūn.
Chéng Dàxīn
defeated the Jūn army at Fángzhǔ.
Pān Chóng again attacked Jūn,
reaching Xíxué.
B6.11.2 In summer,
Shūzhòng Huìbó met with Xì Quē of Jìn at Chéngkuāng,
to deliberate about the feudal lords who were following Chǔ.
B6.11.3 In autumn,
Duke Wén of Cáo came to court,
[He] ascended the throne
and came to pay a visit.
B6.11.4 Xiāng Zhòng was sent as envoy to Sòng,
and also spoke about reinstating the Sīchéng Dàng Yì Zhū.
[He] took the opportunity to congratulate on the Chǔ army not causing harm.
B6.11.5 The *Sōumán* invaded Qí,
and then attacked us.
The Duke divined to send Shū Sūn Déchén to pursue them,
and it was auspicious.
Hóu Shū Xià drove for Zhuāng Shū,
Mián Fáng Shēng was the right-hand man,
and Fù Fù Zhōng Shēng was the chariot driver.
In the winter, on the *jiǎwǔ* day of the tenth month,
they defeated the Dí at Xián,
and captured the Long Dí Qiáo Rú.
Fù Fù Zhōng Shēng pierced his throat with a *gē*,
killing him.
[They] buried his head at the Zǐ Jū Gate.
[They] reported this to Xuān Bó.
Initially,
during the reign of Duke Wǔ of Sòng,
the *Sōumán* attacked Sòng.
The Sītú Huáng Fǔ led the army to resist them.
Ér Bān drove for Huáng Fǔ Chōngshí,
Gōngzǐ Gǔshēng was the right-hand man,
and the Sīkòu Niú Fù was the chariot driver,
and defeated the Dí at Chángqiū,
capturing the Long Dí Yuán Sī.
The two sons of Huáng Fǔ died there.
so the Duke of Sòng rewarded Ér Bān with a gate,
allowing him to levy taxes there,
calling it the Ér Gate.
When Jìn destroyed Lù,
they captured Fén Rú, the younger brother of Qiáo Rú.
In the second year of Duke Huì of Qí,
the Sōumán attacked Qí.
Prince Chéng Fù of Qí captured his younger brother, Róng Rú.
They buried his head north of the north gate of Zhōu Shǒu.
The people of Wèi captured his youngest brother, Jiǎn Rú.
The Sōumán thereupon perished.
B6.11.6 The Crown Prince Zhū Rú of Chéng secured himself at Fū Zhōng;
the people of the state did not follow him.
A6.12 *Annals, Year 12 of Duke Wén*
A6.12.1 In the spring of the twelfth year,
in the first month of the king,
the Count of Chéng came to seek refuge.
A6.12.2 The Count of Qǐ came to court.
A6.12.3 In the second month, on the day Gēngzǐ,
Zǐ Shū Jī died.
A6.12.4 In the summer,
the people of Chǔ besieged Cháo.
A6.12.5 In the autumn,
the Viscount of Téng came to court.
A6.12.6 The Earl of Qín sent Shù to come on a diplomatic visit.
A6.12.7 In the twelfth month, on the day Wùwǔ,
the Jìn people and
the Qín people fought at the bend of the Hé River.
A6.12.8 Jìsūn Hángfǔ led the army to build the cities of Zhū and Yùn.
B6.12 *Zuǒ Zhuàn*, Twelfth Year of Duke Wén
B6.12.1 In the spring of the twelfth year,
the Earl of Chéng died,
and the people of Chéng established a ruler.
The Heir Apparent brought the fū bell and the Chéng guī jade to seek refuge.
The Duke met him with the etiquette due to a feudal lord,
which was improper,
so the text records,
"The Earl of Chéng came to seek refuge."
The place is not recorded,
to show respect for the feudal lords.
B6.12.2 The Duke Huán of Qǐ came to court,
it was the first time he came to court to the Duke.
Furthermore, he requested to sever ties with Shū Jī
but not to break off the marriage relationship,
and the Duke approved it.
In the second month,
Shū Jī died.
It is not written "Qǐ,"
because the connection was severed.
It is written "Shū Jī,"
indicating she was not a daughter.
B6.12.3 The Chǔ Chancellor Dàsūn Bó died,
and Chéng Jiā became Chancellor.
The various Shū states rebelled against Chǔ.
In the summer,
Zǐ Kǒng captured Shū Zǐ Píng and his clan leaders,
and then besieged Cháo.
B6.12.4 In the autumn,
Duke Zhāo of Téng came to court,
and this was the first time he came to court to see the Duke.
B6.12.5 The Earl of Qín sent Xī Qǐ Shù as an envoy to visit,
and also to announce the intention to attack Jìn.
Xiāng Zhòng declined the jade,
saying:
"Our lord does not forget the friendship of your late lord,
illuminates and watches over the state of Lǔ,
pacifies and protects its altars of soil and grain,
and adds to it with great treasures.
How dare our lord decline the jade."
The envoy replied,
"These are but paltry, worn-out items,
not worth declining."
The host declined three times.
Bīn replied, saying:
"Our ruler wishes to seek blessings from the Duke of Zhou and the Duke of Lu to serve you.
These are humble relics of our late ruler.
I, your subject, am sent to present them to the officers,
as tokens of auspiciousness,
to establish a good alliance,
thereby relying on our ruler's command,
to forge amity between the two states,
and thus I dare to present them."
Xiāng Zhòng said:
"Without gentlemen,
how could there be a state?
Our state is not ignorant."
He richly rewarded him.
B6.12.6 Because of the campaign against Línghú by Qín,
in winter,
the Earl of Qín attacked Jìn,
and seized the tethered horses.
The people of Jìn resisted them.
Zhào Dùn commanded the central army,
assisted by Xún Línfù.
Xì Quē commanded the upper army,
assisted by Yú Pián.
Luán Dùn commanded the lower army,
assisted by Xū Jiǎ.
Fàn Wúxù served as charioteer,
to follow the Qín army at the bend of the Yellow River.
Yú Pián said:
"Qín cannot last long,
please build deep ramparts and strengthen our army
to wait for them."
They followed his advice.
The Qín people wanted to fight.
The Lord of Qín said to Shì Huì:
"How should we fight?"
He replied:
"The Zhào clan has newly produced a subordinate named Yú Pián,
he must be responsible for this plan,
intending to exhaust our troops.
Zhào has a member of a secondary lineage named Chuān,
the son-in-law of the Lord of Jìn,
favored but weak,
not involved in military affairs;
fond of bravery and reckless,
and hates that Yú Pián assists the upper army.
If we allow a rash person to act freely,
it will be feasible."
The Lord of Qín used jade to pray to the river for battle.
On the day wùwǔ of the twelfth month,
the Qín army ambushed the Jìn's upper army.
Zhào Chuān pursued them,
but did not catch up.
Returning,
he angrily said:
"We carry rations and wear armor,
To deliberately seek out the enemy.
If the enemy arrives and you do not attack,
what are the generals waiting for?"
The military officer said:
"The general has something to wait for."
Zhuān said:
"I do not understand strategy,
the general is acting on his own."
Thereupon, he led his subordinates out.
Xuānzǐ said:
"If Qín captures Zhuān,
they will have captured a high minister.
If Qín returns in victory,
how will we retaliate?"
Thereupon, they all went out to battle,
engaging in a brief skirmish.
The Qín envoy warned the Jìn army at night, saying:
"The soldiers of both lords are not yet content,
tomorrow, we request to meet."
Yú Pián said:
"The envoy's eyes move and his speech is unrestrained,
he is afraid of us,
he is about to flee.
Press them to the river,
and we will surely defeat them."
Xū Jiǎ and
Zhào Zhuān stood at the military gate and shouted:
"To abandon the dead and wounded without collecting them,
This is not benevolent.
To press people into danger without waiting for the appointed time
is not courageous."
Therefore, they stopped.
The Qin army retreated at night.
They invaded Jìn again,
entering Xiá.
Recording the construction of Chéng Zhū and Yùn
was timely.
*The Annals of Duke Wén, Year Thirteen*
In summer, the fifth month, on the day rénwǔ,
Marquis Shuò of Chén died.
Zū Zǐ Qúchú of Zhū died.
From the first month, there was no rain,
until the seventh month of autumn.
The roof of the great hall collapsed.
In winter,
the duke went to Jìn.
The Marquis of Wèi met with Duke Xiāng of Jìn at Dá.
A6.13.7 The Dí invaded Wèi.
A6.13.8 In the twelfth month, on the day jǐchǒu, Duke Xiāng of Jìn and Duke Xiāng of Lǔ formed an alliance.
Duke Xiāng of Lǔ and Duke Xiāng of Jìn formed an alliance.
A6.13.9 Duke Xiāng of Lǔ returned from Jìn,
Zhèng Bó met with Duke Xiāng of Lǔ at Fěi.
B6.13 *Commentary on the Thirteenth Year of Duke Wén*
B6.13.1 In the spring of the thirteenth year,
Duke Xiāng of Jìn sent Zhān Jiā to reside at Xiá,
in order to guard the fortress of Táolín.
B6.13.2 The people of Jìn were worried about Qín's employment of Shì Huì.
In summer,
the six ministers met each other at Zhūfú.
Zhào Xuānzǐ said:
"Suí Huì is in Qín,
Jiǎ Jì is among the Dí.
Difficulties will arrive daily.
What should we do?"
Zhōngháng Huánzǐ said:
"Please reinstate Jiǎ Jì.
He is capable in foreign affairs,
and it is due to his former merits."
Xì Chéngzǐ said:
"Jiǎ Jì is in turmoil,
and his crimes are great.
He is not as good as Suí Huì.
He is capable of being humble and having shame,
gentle and not offensive;
his knowledge is sufficient for him to be employed.
Moreover, he is innocent."
So, he sent Wèi Shòuyú to feign
being a defector from Wèi,
in order to entice Shì Huì.
He held his family hostage in Jìn
and let him escape at night.
He requested to return to Qín of his own accord,
and the Duke of Qín permitted it.
He (Shì Huì) trod the Duke of Qín’s feet at court.
The Duke of Qín stationed troops west of the river.
The people of Wèi were in the east.
Shòuyú said:
"Let the eastern people who are capable of speaking with those few officials
let me be the first to speak with them."
He sent Shì Huì.
Shì Huì declined,
saying:
"The people of Jìn
are like tigers and wolves.
If I betray their words,
I will die,
and my wife and children will be slaughtered,
It will not benefit you,
and you cannot regret it."
The Count of Qín 秦 said:
"If I break my word,
may I not return your belongings,
as sure as the Hé 河 (Yellow River) flows!"
Thereupon they departed.
Rào Cháo 繞朝 presented him with a riding whip,
saying:
"Do not say that Qín 秦 has no men;
it is only that my plans are not being used."
Having crossed the river,
the people of Wèi 魏 clamored and returned.
The people of Qín 秦 returned their belongings.
Those who remained there became the Liú 劉 clan.
B6.13.3 The Wén Gōng 文公 of Zhū 邾
divined about moving to Yì 繹.
The historian said:
"It will benefit the people but not the ruler."
The Zhū Zǐ 邾子 (Ruler of Zhū) said:
"If it benefits the people,
it also benefits me.
Heaven creates people and establishes a ruler over them
in order to benefit them.
Now that the people are benefited,
I must share in it."
Those around him said:
"Life can be lengthened;
"Why doesn't Your Lordship do it?"
The ruler of Zhū said,
"My duty lies in nurturing the people.
The length of life and death
is a matter of timing.
If the people benefit,
even moving the capital
could not be more auspicious!"
Thereupon, they moved to Yì.
In the fifth month,
Zhū Wén Gōng died.
The gentleman said,
"He understood destiny."
B6.13.4 In the seventh month of autumn,
the roof of the great chamber collapsed,
and the chronicles
were not properly maintained.
B6.13.5 In winter,
the Duke went to Jìn
for an audience
and to renew the alliance.
The Marquis of Wèi met the Duke at Tà,
requesting peace with Jìn.
The Duke returned.
The Count of Zhèng met the Duke at Fěi,
also requesting peace with Jìn.
The Duke agreed to both.
The Count of Zhèng feasted the Duke at Fěi.
Zǐ Jiā recited the "Wild Geese" ode.
Jì Wénzǐ said,
"Our ruler is not free from such [behavior]."
Wénzǐ recited the "Fourth Month" ode.
Zǐ Jiā recited the fourth stanza of "Loaded Chariot."
Wénzǐ recited the fourth stanza of "Gathering Ferns."
The Count of Zhèng bowed.
The Duke returned the bow.
A6.14 *Annals of Duke Wén, Year 14*
A6.14.1 In the spring of the fourteenth year,
in the first month of the royal calendar,
the Duke arrived from Jìn.
A6.14.2 The people of Zhū attacked our southern borders.
Shū Péngshēng led troops to attack Zhū.
A6.14.3 In the fifth month, on the day yǐ-hài,
Lord Pān of Qí died.
A6.14.4 In the sixth month,
the Duke met with Duke of Sòng,
Marquis of Chén,
Marquis of Wèi,
Count of Zhèng,
Viscount of Xǔ,
Count of Cáo,
and Zhào Dùn of Jìn.
Guǐyǒu.
An alliance was formed at Xīnchéng.
A6.14.5 In the seventh month of autumn,
a comet entered the Northern Dipper.
A6.14.6 The Duke returned from the assembly.
A6.14.7 The Jìn people tried to deliver Jié Zī to Zhū,
but were unable to deliver him.
A6.14.8 On the day jiǎshēn of the ninth month,
Gōngsūn Áo died in Qí.
A6.14.9 The Qí prince, Shāngrén, assassinated his lord, Shě.
A6.14.10 Sòng Zǐ Āi came to seek refuge.
A6.14.11 In winter,
Dān Bó went to Qí.
A6.14.12 The people of Qí arrested Dān Bó.
A6.14.13 The people of Qí arrested Zǐ Shū Jī.
B6.14 *Zuǒ Zhuàn*, Fourteenth Year of Duke Wén
B6.14.1 In the spring of the fourteenth year,
King Qǐng died.
Zhōu Gōng Yuè and Wángsūn Sū contended for power,
therefore he did not attend [the funeral].
Whenever there is a death of a king (崩, *bēng*)
or a feudal lord (薨, *hōng*),
and one does not attend,
then it was not recorded.
Calamities or blessings,
if they were not reported,
were also not recorded.
This was to punish disrespect.
B6.14.2 When Duke Wén of Zhū died,
the duke sent someone to offer condolences,
but they were disrespectful.
The people of Zhū came to retaliate,
attacking our southern borders,
therefore, Huì Bó attacked Zhū.
B6.14.3 Zǐ Shū Jī was the concubine of Duke Zhāo of Qí,
and gave birth to Shě.
Shū Jī had no favor,
and Shě had no authority.
Gōngzǐ Shāngrén frequently bestowed favors in the state
and gathered many retainers,
exhausting his family's wealth,
and borrowing from the public officials to continue.
In the fifth month of summer,
Duke Zhāo died,
and Shě ascended the throne.
B6.14.4 The primary consort of Duke Wén of Zhū, Qí Jiāng,
gave birth to Duke Dìng;
the second consort was Jìn Jī,
who gave birth to Jié Zī.
When Duke Wén died,
the people of Zhū installed Duke Dìng.
Jié Zī fled to Jìn.
B6.14.5 In the sixth month,
they formed an alliance at Xīnchéng,
those who followed Chǔ submitted,
and they plotted against Zhū.
B6.14.6 In the seventh month, on the day yǐ-mǎo in autumn,
at night,
a Qí merchant named Shè assassinated Yuán,
and blamed it on Yuán.
Yuán said:
"You have sought this for a long time.
If I can serve you,
you must not allow much resentment to accumulate,
will you spare me?
Do it!"
B6.14.7 A comet entered the Big Dipper.
Shū Fú, the Inner Historian of the Zhōu Dynasty, said:
"Within seven years,
the rulers of Sòng, Qí, and Jìn will all die in turmoil."
B6.14.8 Zhào Dùn of Jìn, with eight hundred chariots from the armies of the feudal lords, escorted Jié Zī into Zhū.
The people of Zhū declined, saying:
"Qí has sent out Jue, and he is older."
Xuān Zǐ said:
"Words are compliant,
but not followed,
is inauspicious."
Thereupon he returned.
B6.14.9 Zhōu Gōng was about to litigate with Wángsūn Sū in Jìn,
the King betrayed Wángsūn Sū,
and sent Yǐn Shì and Dān Qǐ to litigate against Zhōu Gōng in Jìn.
Zhào Xuānzǐ pacified the royal house
and restored it.
B6.14.10 When Chǔ Zhuāng Wáng ascended the throne,
Zǐ Kǒng and Pān Chóng were about to attack the various Shū states,
and sent Gōngzǐ Xiè and Zǐ Yí to guard [the capital],
and then attacked Shū Liǎo.
The two men rebelled.
They fortified Yǐng,
and sent an assassin to kill Zǐ Kǒng,
but failed and returned.
In the eighth month,
the two men took the Chǔ ruler out [of the city].
They were about to go to Shāngmì,
when Lú Jílí and Shū Jūn lured them,
and then killed Dòu Kè and Gōngzǐ Xiè.
Initially,
Dòu Kè was imprisoned in Qín,
after Qín suffered defeat at Háo,
they sent him back to seek a settlement.
Having reached a settlement but not getting his way,
Gōngzǐ Xiè sought to be appointed Prime Minister (令尹 lìngyǐn) but was unsuccessful,
therefore the two sons caused a rebellion.
the people of Lǔ established Wén Bó.
Mù Bó had two sons in Jǔ,
and sought to return.
Wén Bó interceded on his behalf.
Xiāng Zhòng ordered him not to attend court
to await orders.
He returned but did not leave [Jǔ].
After three years, he moved his entire household to Jǔ.
Wén Bó fell ill,
and requested, saying:
"The son of Gǔ is weak,
I request that Nàn be established."
It was permitted.
Wén Bó died,
and Huì Shū was established.
Mù Bó requested heavy bribes to seek return.
Huì Shū interceded on his behalf,
and it was permitted.
He was about to come,
[but in] the ninth month,
he died in Qí.
[They] reported the mourning,
and requested burial,
[but it was] not permitted.
B6.14.12 Sòng Gāo Āi was the border official of Xiāo,
[Zuǒ Zhuàn] considered [Sòng Zǐ'āi] 以为卿,
to be unrighteous for abandoning Duke [Sòng], 不義宋公而出,
and consequently came to seek refuge. 遂來奔.
The record says: 書曰：「宋子哀來奔」,
this was to value him. 貴之也.
B6.14.13 The people of [Qí] settled Duke [Yì], 齊人定懿公，
and sent him to announce the difficulties, 使來告難，
therefore it is recorded as 故書以
"ninth month." 「九月」.
The [Qí] noble, [Qí Gōngzǐ Yuán], 齊公子元
did not approve of Duke [Yì]'s governance, 不順懿公之為政也，
and never called him "Duke," 終不曰「公」，
but called him "[Fūjǐshì]." 曰「夫己氏」.
B6.14.14 [Xiāng Zhòng] sent word to the King, 襄仲使告于王，
requesting [Zhāo Jī] from [Qí] by using the King's favor, 請以王寵求昭姬于齊，
saying: 曰：
"Having killed her son, 殺其子，
what use is there for her mother? 焉用其母？
Please accept her and punish her." 請受而罪之。」
In winter, 冬，
[Dān Bó] went to [Qí] to request [Zǐ Shū Jī], 單伯如齊，請子叔姬，
and the people of [Qí] detained him. 齊人執之.
They also detained [Zǐ Shū Jī]. 又執子叔姬.
A6.15 *Annals of Duke [Wén], fifteenth year* 《文公十五年經》
A6.15.1 In the fifteenth year, spring, 十有五年春，
[Jìsūn Hángfǔ] went to [Jìn]. 季孫行父如晉.
A6.15.2 In the third month, 三月，
[Sòng] [Sīmǎ Huásūn] came to form an alliance. 宋司馬華孫來盟.
A6.15.3 In summer, 夏，
the Earl of [Cáo] came to court. 曹伯來朝.
A6.15.4 The people of Qí returned the remains of Gōngsūn Áo.
A6.15.5 On the first day (shuò) of the sixth month, Xin Chou,
there was a solar eclipse.
Drums were beaten and sacrificial animals were used at the local shrine (shè).
A6.15.6 Dān Bó arrived from Qí.
A6.15.7 Xì Quē of Jìn led an army to attack Cài.
On Wù Shēn,
they entered Cài.
A6.15.8 In autumn,
the people of Qí invaded our western borders.
A6.15.9 Jìsūn Hángfǔ went to Jìn.
A6.15.10 In the eleventh month of winter,
the lords made an alliance at Hù.
A6.15.11 In the twelfth month,
the people of Qí came to return Zǐshū Jī.
A6.15.12 The Marquis of Qí 齊 attacked our western border.
Consequently, he attacked Cáo 曹,
and entered its outer city.
B6.15 *Commentary on the Fifteenth Year of Duke Wén* 文公
B6.15.1 In the spring of the fifteenth year,
Jì Wénzǐ 季文子 went to Jìn 晉,
for the sake of Dān Bó 單伯 and Zǐ Shūjī 子叔姬.
B6.15.2 In the third month,
Sòng Huá Ǒu 宋華耦 came to form an alliance;
all his officials followed him.
The *Chunqiu* 春秋 says, "Sima Huásūn 華孫 of Sòng 宋,"
valuing him.
The Duke gave him a feast.
He declined, saying:
"Your late minister Dū 督 offended Duke Shāng of Sòng 宋殤公,
and his name is on the records of the feudal lords.
I inherited his sacrifices;
how dare I disgrace Your Lordship?
Please allow me to accept your orders as a subordinate official."
The people of Lǔ 魯 considered him clever.
B6.15.3 In summer,
the Earl of Cáo 曹 came to court;
this was according to ritual.
The feudal lords would pay court to each other every five years,
in order to uphold the King's commands;
this was an ancient system.
B6.15.4 Some people of Qí 齊 plotted on behalf of the Mèng 孟 clan,
saying:
"Lǔ 魯
is close to you.
Decorate the coffin and place it at Tángfù 堂阜.
and Lǔ 魯 will surely take it."
They followed this advice.
A man from Biàn 卞 informed them.
Huìshū 惠叔 still destroyed
it to request it,
standing in court to await orders.
He was permitted.
They took
it and prepared it for burial.
The people of Qí 齊 escorted it.
The record says:
"The people of Qí 齊 returned the funeral of Gōngsūn Áo 公孫敖,"
for the Mèngshì 孟氏 family,
and it was also a matter of state.
The burial was conducted as for Gòng Zhòng 共仲.
Shēng Jǐ 聲己 did not view the body,
but set up curtains in the hall and wept.
Xiāng Zhòng 襄仲 wanted to forbid the weeping.
Huì Bó 惠伯 said,
"A funeral
is the end of kinship.
Even if one could not begin well,
It can be considered a good end.
Shǐ Yì had a saying:
"Brothers achieve excellence.
Helping the needy, congratulating the good, comforting the afflicted,
revering sacrifices, mourning the deceased,
though the emotions are different,
do not sever the love;
this is the way of kinship."
If you, my son, do not lose the Way,
why should you resent others?"
Xiāng Zhòng spoke.
He led his brothers to mourn him.
In later years,
his two sons came,
Mèng Xiànzǐ loved them,
and it became known throughout the state.
Someone slandered him,
saying,
"He intends to kill his sons."
Xiànzǐ told Jì Wénzǐ about it.
The two sons said,
"Our master is known for loving us,
and we are known for intending to kill his sons;
isn't that far from propriety?
Being far from propriety is worse than death."
One person died at the gate of Gōu Méng,
the other at the gate of Lì Qiū, both died.
B6.15.5 On the first day of the sixth month, *xīn chǒu*,
There was a solar eclipse.
To beat drums and use sacrificial animals at the earth altar
is not in accordance with ritual.
When there is a solar eclipse,
the Son of Heaven does not conduct normal affairs,
and beats drums at the earth altar.
The feudal lords use silk at the earth altar
and beat drums in the court
to manifest service to the spirits, instruct the people, and serve the ruler,
demonstrating hierarchical authority.
This is the ancient way.
B6.15.6 The people of Qí 齊 allowed Dān Bó 單伯, who had requested it, to be pardoned,
and sent him to deliver a message.
The record states: "Dān Bó 單伯 arrived from Qí 齊,"
valuing him.
B6.15.7 At the alliance of Xīnchéng 新城,
the people of Cài 蔡 did not participate.
Xì Quē 郤缺 of Jìn 晉, leading the upper and
lower armies, attacked Cài 蔡,
saying:
"The ruler is weak,
so we must not be negligent."
On the day of wùshēn 戊申,
they entered Cài 蔡,
and returned after making an alliance under the walls of the city.
Whenever a state is victorious,
it is said to have destroyed it;
when a large city is captured,
Rì rù zhī.
B6.15.8 In autumn,
the people of Qí invaded our western borders,
therefore Jì Wénzǐ informed Jìn.
B6.15.9 In the eleventh month of winter, the Marquis of Jìn, Duke of Sòng, Marquis of Wèi, Marquis of Cài, Marquis of Chén, Count of Zhèng, Viscount of Xǔ, and Count of Cáo formed an alliance at Hù,
to reaffirm the alliance of Xīnchéng,
and also to plan an attack on Qí.
The people of Qí bribed the Marquis of Jìn,
so they were unable to succeed and returned.
Because there was a difficulty with Qí,
therefore the Duke did not attend the meeting.
The *Shū* says: "The lords allied at Hù,"
there was nothing they could do.
In all cases when the lords meet,
if the Duke does not participate,
it is not recorded,
to avoid mentioning the ruler's shortcomings.
If he participates but is not recorded,
it is because he was late.
B6.15.10 The people of Qí came to return Zǐ Shū Jī,
because the king wanted it.
B6.15.11 The Marquis of Qí invaded our western borders,
saying that the lords were incapable.
Thereupon they attacked Cáo,
entering its outer city,
to punish them for coming to court.
Jì Wénzǐ said:
"The Marquis of Qí will probably not escape [punishment]?
If one is himself without propriety,
and demands propriety from those who possess it,
saying,
"Why do you practice propriety?"
Propriety is to accord with Heaven,
it is the Way of Heaven.
If one himself goes against Heaven,
and yet demands from others,
it will be difficult to avoid misfortune.
The *Shī* (Book of Poetry) says:
"Why do you not fear each other?
You do not fear Heaven."
The reason why the gentleman does not abuse the young and lowly
is that he fears Heaven.
In the *Zhōu Sòng* (Hymns of Zhōu) it says:
"Fearing the majesty of Heaven,
at these times preserve it."
If one does not fear Heaven,
what can he preserve?
To seize a state through disorder,
and uphold it by observing propriety,
one should still fear it will not last;
if one frequently acts without propriety,
he will not be able to maintain it."
A6.16 *Wén Gōng* (Duke Wén) 16th Year *Jīng* (Classic)
A6.16.1 In the spring of the sixteenth year,
Jìsūn Hángfǔ met with the Marquis of Qí at Yánggǔ,
but the Marquis of Qí did not proceed to an oath.
A6.16.2 In the summer, the fifth month,
the Duke did not observe the first day of the month on four occasions.
A6.16.3 In the sixth month, on *wùchén*,
Gōngzǐ Suì allied with the Marquis of Qí at Qīqiū.
A6.16.4 In autumn, the eighth month, on the day xīn-wèi,
Lady Jiāng shì, the Duke's wife, passed away.
A6.16.5 The Quán Terrace was destroyed.
A6.16.6 The people of Chǔ,
the people of Qín,
and the people of Bā extinguished Yōng.
A6.16.7 In winter, the eleventh month,
the people of Sòng assassinated their lord, Chǔjiù.
B6.16 *Zuǒ Zhuàn*, Sixteenth Year of Duke Wén
B6.16.1 In the spring of the sixteenth year,
in the king's first month,
there was peace with Qí.
The Duke was ill,
so he sent Jì Wénzǐ to meet with the Marquis of Qí at Yánggǔ.
He requested an alliance,
but the Marquis of Qí refused,

B6.16.2 In summer, the fifth month,
the Duke failed to observe the new moon four times due to his illness.
The Duke sent Xiāng Zhòng to present bribes to Qí Hóu,
therefore, they made a covenant at Qíqiū.
B6.16.3 A snake emerged from the Quán Palace
and entered the capital,

In the eighth month, on the day of xīnwèi,

B6.16.4 In Chǔ, there was a great famine.

The people of Yōng led the various Mán tribes in rebellion against Chǔ.
The people of Jūn led the hundred Pú and gathered at Xuǎn,

Wěi Jiǎ said,

If we can go there,

It would be better to attack Yōng.
The Jūn and the hundred Pú think that we are too famished to mobilize troops,
so they are attacking us.
If we send out troops,
they will certainly be afraid and return [home]."
they will surely be afraid and return.
The Bǎipú live dispersed;
"The Bǎi Pú live scattered,
they will each flee to their own towns,
each will flee to their own town.
who will have time to scheme against others?"
Who will have time to plot against others?"
So, he sent out an army.
Thereupon, he sent out an army.
After fifteen days,
In fifteen days,
the Bǎipú then withdrew.
From Lú onward,
they opened the granaries and ate together.
They encamped at Jùshì.
He sent Lú Jílí to invade Yōng,
reaching Yōng's Fāngchéng.
The people of Yōng pursued him,
and captured Zǐ Yángchuāng.
After three nights, he escaped,
saying:
"Yōng's army is numerous;
many barbarians are gathered there.
It would be better to call back the main army,
and also raise the King's troops;
only after joining forces should we advance."
Shī Shū said:
"It is not acceptable.
We should encounter them again to make them arrogant.
When they are arrogant and we are enraged,
then we can defeat them.
That is how our late lord Fénmào conquered Xíngxí."
They encountered them again.
and were defeated in all seven encounters.
Only the people of Bì, Tiáo, and Yú actually pursued them.
The Yōng people said:
"Chǔ is not worth fighting."
Consequently, they did not prepare defenses.
The Viscount of Chǔ, riding post horses,
assembled his army at Lín Pǐn,
dividing it into two divisions.
Zǐ Yuè advanced from Shí Xī,
and Zǐ Bèi advanced from Rèn, to attack Yōng.
The people of Qín and Bā followed the Chǔ army.
The various Mán tribes allied with the Viscount of Chǔ,
and consequently, Yōng was destroyed.
B6.16.5 Gōngzǐ Bào of Sòng was courteous to the people of the state.
When Sòng was afflicted by famine,
he exhausted his grain to lend to them.
Those aged seventy and above
all received gifts and provisions,
with rare and unusual delicacies added from time to time.
He visited the doors of the six ministers almost every day.
The talented men of the state
were all in his service;
From Qīn (親) down to Huán (桓) personally,
there was none who was not cared for.
Gōngzǐ Bào (公子鮑) was handsome and charming.
The Xiāng (襄) Consort wanted to have an affair with him,
but he refused.
So she helped him with gifts.
Zhāo Gōng (昭公) was without virtue,
and the people of the state supported Gōngzǐ Bào
in reliance on the Consort.
Thereupon, Huá Yuán (華元) became Right Preceptor,
Gōngsūn Yǒu (公孫友) became Left Preceptor,
Huá Ǒu (華耦) became Minister of War,
Lín Guàn (鱗矔) became Minister of Populace,
Dàng Yìzhū (蕩意諸) became Minister of Works,
and Gōngzǐ Zhāo (公子朝) became Minister of Justice.
Earlier,
the Minister of Works, Dàng (蕩), had died,
and Gōngsūn Shòu (公孫壽) resigned from his position as Minister of Works,
requesting that Yìzhū (意諸) be appointed to it.
Afterward, he told people,
"The ruler is without virtue,
and my office is close to him,
so I fear it will affect me.
If I abandon my office,
then my clan will have no protection.
A son
is like a second self;
I will temporarily put off death by it.
"Although he has lost his son,
he has not yet lost his clan."
Afterwards,
the Madam was going to have Gōng Tián Mèng Zhū kill him.
The Duke knew of it,
and gave away all his treasures.
Dàng Yì Zhū said:
"Why not go to the feudal lords?"
The Duke said:
"If I cannot (win over) even my high officials, down to my royal grandmother, and the people of the country,
which feudal lord would accept me?
Moreover, having already been a ruler,
and then to become someone's subject,
is not as good as death."
He gave all his treasures to his attendants
and had them leave.
The Madam had the Sīchéng (Minister of Works) leave the Duke.
He replied:
"If I, as his subject, were to flee his trouble,
what would I do for the lord later?"
In the winter, the eleventh month, on the day Jiǎyín,
Sòng Zhāo Gōng was going to hunt at Mèng Zhū,
before he arrived,
the Madam, Wáng Jī, had the Shuaidiàn attack and kill him.
Dàng Yì Zhū died with him.
The record says:
"The people of Sòng murdered their ruler Chǔ Jiù,"
(because) the ruler was without virtue.
Wén Gōng ascended the throne,
and made his younger brother Xū the Sīchéng.
Huá Ǒu died,
and (Wén Gōng) made Dàng Huī the Sīmǎ (Minister of War).
A6.17 *Annals, Year 17 of Duke Wén*
A6.17.1 In the spring of the seventeenth year,
the people of Jìn,
the people of Wèi,
the people of Chén,
and the people of Zhèng attacked Sòng.
A6.17.2 In the fourth month, on the day guǐhài,

In the sixth month, on the day guǐwèi,

A6.17.5 In the autumn,

A6.17.6 In the winter,
