B6.17 *Tradition, Year 17 of Duke Wén*
B6.17.1 In the seventeenth year, spring,
Xún Línfǔ 荀林父 of Jìn 晉, Kǒng Dá 孔達 of Wèi 衛, Gōngsūn Níng 公孫寧 of Chén 陳, and Shí Chǔ 石楚 of Zhèng 鄭 attacked Sòng 宋,
claiming the reason for their attack was:
"Why did you murder your ruler?"
They nevertheless installed Wén Gōng 文公 and returned.
The *Qīng* is not recorded,
because it missed its proper place.
B6.17.2 In summer, the fourth month, *guǐhài* 癸亥,
Shēng Jiāng 聲姜 was buried.
There was trouble with Qí 齊,
which is why it was delayed.
B6.17.3 The Marquis of Qí 齊 attacked our northern borders,
so Xiāng Zhòng 襄仲 requested a covenant.
In the sixth month,
they formed a covenant at Gǔ 穀.
B6.17.4 The Marquis of Jìn 晉 conducted a military review at Huángfǔ 黃父,
and then reassembled the feudal lords at Hù 扈,
to make peace with Sòng 宋.
The Duke did not attend the meeting,
because of the trouble with Qí 齊.
The text records "the feudal lords,"
because there was no merit.
Thereupon the Marquis of Jìn 晉 refused to meet with the Count of Zhèng 鄭,
because he suspected him of being disloyal to Chǔ 楚.
Zǐ Jiā 子家 of Zhèng 鄭 had the envoy seized
and gave him a letter,
to inform Zhào Xuānzǐ 趙宣子,
saying:
"It has been three years since our ruler ascended the throne,
and he summoned the Marquis of Cài 蔡
to assist him in serving your ruler.
In the ninth month,
the Marquis of Cài 蔡 entered our humble state to travel through.
Our city was troubled by the difficulties involving Hóu Xuānduō,
and therefore my ruler was unable to accompany Marquis Cài.
In the eleventh month,
we successfully subdued Hóu Xuānduō,
and followed Marquis Cài
to pay respects to you, the officials.
In the twelfth year, in the sixth month,
Guī Shēng assisted my ruler's heir apparent, Yí,
to request an audience with Marquis Chén from Chǔ and to pay respects to you lords.
In the fourteenth year, in the seventh month,
my ruler again paid respects
to finalize matters regarding Chén.
In the fifteenth year, in the fifth month,
Marquis Chén himself went from our city to pay respects to your lord.
Last year, in the first month,
Zhú Zhīwǔ went to pay respects to Yí.
In the eighth month,
my ruler went again to pay respects.
Because Chén and Cài are close to Chǔ,
and we dare not be disloyal to you,
this is due to the efforts of our city.
Although our city serves your lord,
Why is it impossible to avoid?
While in office,
once he went to Xiāng [襄],
and twice he appeared before your lord.
Yí [夷] and the two or three ministers of the orphaned one have followed each other to Jiàng [絳].
Although we are a small state,
there is nothing we can do to surpass this.
Now the great state says:
"You have not yet fulfilled my desires."
If our humble state perishes,
there is nothing more to add to it.
The ancients had a saying:
"Fearing the head and fearing the tail,
how much life remains for the body?"
It is also said:
"When a deer is dying, it does not choose its shade."
When a small state serves a great state,
if there is virtue,
it is like serving a person;
if there is no virtue,
it is like serving a deer.
Forced to take risks,
how can one choose in haste?
The decree is boundless,
we also know that we will perish.
We will gather all our resources to await you at Tiáo [鯈].
It is up to you to decide.
In the second year of Duke Wén [文公], sixth month, rénshēn [壬申],
Went to the court in Qí.
In the fourth year, the second month, réngxū day,
because of Qí's invasion of Cài,
also achieved a treaty with Chǔ.
Living between great states,
and obeying the orders of the strong,
how can that be a crime?
If the great states do not plan for this,
there is nowhere to escape death."
Jìn's Gǒng Shuò negotiated a peace treaty with Zhèng,
Zhào Chuān and Gōngxù Chí were taken as hostages.
Zhōu's Gān Chù defeated the Róng at Shēnchuí,
taking advantage of their drinking.
B6.17.6 In the tenth month of winter,
Zhèng's Crown Prince Yí and
Shí Chǔ were taken as hostages by Jìn.
B6.17.7 Xiāng Zhòng went to Qí
to attend the Gǔ Alliance.
He further said:
"I have heard that the people of Qí intend to consume the wheat of Lǔ.
From my observation,
they will not be able to.
The words of the ruler of Qí are deceitful.
Zāng Wénzhòng had a saying:
'If a ruler is deceitful,
he will surely die.'"
A6.18 *Duke Wén, Year Eighteen, Annals*
A6.18.1 In the spring of the eighteenth year,
on the day *dīngchǒu* of the second month,
the Duke died at the foot of the Terrace.
A6.18.2 The Earl of Qín, Yīng, died.
A6.18.3 In the summer, on the day *wùxū* of the fifth month,
the people of Qí assassinated their ruler, Shāngrén.
A6.18.4 In the sixth month, on the day *guǐyǒu*,
we buried our ruler, Duke Wén.
A6.18.5 In the autumn,
Gōngzǐ Suì and
Shūsūn Déchén went to Qí.
A6.18.6 In the tenth month of winter,
Zǐ died.
A6.18.7 The Lady of Jiāng returned to Qí.
A6.18.8 Jìsūn Hángfǔ went to Qí.
A6.18.9 Jǔ assassinated its ruler, Shùqí.
B6.18 *Commentary on the Eighteenth Year of Duke Wén*
B6.18.1 In the spring of the eighteenth year,
the Marquis of Qí prepared the army for an appointed time,
but fell ill.
The doctor said,
"He will not last until autumn;
he will die."
The Duke heard this
and consulted the oracle,
saying,
"Perhaps he will not reach the appointed time!"
Huì Bó ordered the tortoise shell.
Bǔ Chǔqiū interpreted the divination,
saying,
"The Marquis of Qí will not reach the appointed time,
and it is not due to illness;
Your Lordship will also not hear of it.
Ordering the tortoise shell to be consulted brings misfortune."
In the second month, on the day Dingchǒu (丁丑),
the Duke passed away.
B6.18.2 When Duke Yī of Qí (齊懿公) was a prince,
he argued with the father of Bǐng Chù (邴歜) over land
and did not win.
When he ascended the throne,
he dug up the father's feet and cut them off,
and then made Chù (歜) his servant.
He took Yán Zhí's (閻職) wife
and made Zhí (職) his chariot driver.
In the fifth month of summer,
Gōng yóu yú Shēn Chí. Duke (of Lu) went to play in the Shēn Pool.
Èr rén yù yú chí. Two men were bathing in the pool.
Chù yǐ pū chì Zhí. Chù struck Zhí with a beating rod.
Zhí nù. Zhí was angry.
Chù yuē: Chù said:
"Rén duó nǚ qī ér bù nù, "If someone steals your wife and you are not angry,
yī chì nǚ, to be struck once,
yōng hé shāng?" what harm is there?"
Zhí yuē: Zhí said:
"Yǔ yuè qí fù ér fú néng bìng zhě hé rú?" "What would you say to one who had his father's feet cut off and wasn't bothered by it?"
Nǎi móu shì Yì Gōng, Then they plotted to assassinate Duke Yì,
nà zhū zhú zhōng. and hid him in a bamboo thicket.
Guī, He returned,
shě jué ér xíng. abandoned his rank and left.
Qí rén lì Gōngzǐ Yuán. The people of Qí established Gōngzǐ Yuán.
B6.18.3 Liù yuè, June,
zàng Wén Gōng. Wén Gōng was buried.
B6.18.4 Qiū, Autumn,
Xiāng Zhòng, Zhuāng Shū rú Qí, Xiāng Zhòng and Zhuāng Shū went to Qí,
Huì Gōng lì gù, Huì Gōng had been established,
qiě bài zàng yě. and to pay respects at the funeral.
Wén Gōng èr fēi. Jìng Yíng shēng Xuān Gōng. Wén Gōng had two consorts. Jìng Yíng gave birth to Xuān Gōng.
Jìng Yíng bì, Jìng Yíng was favored,
ér sī shì Xiāng Zhòng. and had a secret affair with Xiāng Zhòng.
Xuān Gōng zhǎng, When Xuān Gōng grew up,
ér shǔ zhū Xiāng Zhòng. he was entrusted to Xiāng Zhòng.
Xiāng Zhòng yù lì zhī, Xiāng Zhòng wanted to establish him (as ruler),
Shū Zhòng bù kě. Shū Zhòng disagreed.
Zhòng
was received by the Marquis of Qí
and made a request of him.
The Marquis of Qí had just ascended the throne
and wanted to be on good terms with Lǔ,
B6.18.5 In the tenth month of winter,
Zhòng killed È and Shì,
and established Duke Xuān.
The *Shū*
says, "The son died,"
to avoid direct mention.
Zhòng, acting on the duke’s order, summoned Huì Bó.
His steward, Gōng Rǎn Wùrén, stopped him,
saying,
"If you enter, you will certainly die."
Shūzhòng said,
"It is permissible to die for the duke’s order."
Gōng Rǎn Wùrén said,
"If it is the duke's order,
it is permissible to die;
if it is not the duke’s order,
why listen?"
He did not listen
and entered,
and was killed and buried in a pile of horse dung.
Gōng Rǎn Wùrén took his family and fled to Cài,
and later returned to the Shūzhòng family.
B6.18.6 The Lady Jiāng returned to Qí,
On her departure for home
when she was about to leave,
she wept as she passed through the market,
saying:
"Heaven!
Zhòng Wéi is unprincipled,
killing the proper heir and establishing the illegitimate."
The people in the market all wept.
The people of Lǔ called her Āi Jiāng.
B6.18.7 The Lord Jǔ Jì Gōng gave birth to the eldest son, Pú,
and also gave birth to Jì Tuó.
He loved Jì Tuó and deposed Pú,
and moreover, he frequently acted without propriety towards the state.
Pú, relying on the people of the state, assassinated Jì Gōng,
and came to seek refuge with his treasured jade,
presenting it to Duke Xuān.
The Duke ordered that a邑(yì) be given to him,
saying:
"It must be conferred today!"
Jì Wénzǐ ordered the Minister of Justice to expel him from the borders,
saying:
"He must be gone today!"
The Duke asked the reason for this.
Jì Wénzǐ sent the Grand Historian Kè to reply, saying:
"The late Grand Master Zāng Wénzhòng
taught Háng Fǔ the proper way to serve a ruler.
Háng Fǔ upheld this and acted accordingly,
never daring to deviate,
It is said:
"If you see someone who is respectful to their lord,
serve them
as a filial son cares for their parents.
If you see someone who is disrespectful to their lord,
punish them
as a hawk chases after sparrows."
The late lord Zhōu Gōng 周公 established the *Zhōu Lǐ* 周禮 (Rites of Zhou)
and said:
"Use it to observe virtue,
virtue to manage affairs,
affairs to measure merit,
merit to feed the people."
He composed the *Oath* and said:
"Destruction is thievery,
concealing thievery is harboring.
Stealing wealth is robbery,
robbing tools is adultery.
Relying on the name of harboring,
depending on the use of adultery,
is a great ill-omenous virtue,
constant and without pardon.
It will not be forgotten in the nine punishments."
Xíng Fǔ 行父 returned and observed Jǔ Pú 莒僕,
and found nothing to emulate.
Filial piety, respect, loyalty, and trustworthiness are auspicious virtues;
thievery, robbery, and harboring adultery are ill-omenous virtues.
This Jǔ Pú 莒僕,
If they are filial and respectful,
then they will assassinate their ruler and father;
if they are loyal and trustworthy,
then they will steal precious jewels.
As for the person,
they are a thief;
as for the tools,
they are signs of wickedness.
Protecting them and giving them benefits
is like the ruler storing away evil.
If they are used for instruction, it will lead to darkness,
and the people will have nothing to follow.
They do not conform to goodness,
but dwell entirely in wicked virtues,
therefore, they should be removed."
"In the past, Gāoyáng Shì
had eight talented sons:
Cāngshū, Tuí'ái, Táoyǐn, Dàlín,
Mángjiàng, Tíngjiān, Zhòngróng, Shúdá,
who were unified, sagely, broad, profound,
discerning, trustworthy, earnest, and sincere.
The people of the world called them the 'Eight Excellent Ones' (Bā Kǎi).
Gāoxīn Shì
had eight talented sons:
Bófèn, Zhòngkān, Shūxiàn, Jìzhòng,
Bóhǔ, Zhòngxióng, Shūbào, Jìlí,
who were loyal, solemn, respectful, virtuous,
articulate, kind, benevolent, and harmonious.
The people of the world called them the "Eight Worthies" (Bā Yuán).
These were sixteen clans,
who for generations preserved their excellence,
not allowing their reputation to fall.
Even up to Yáo,
Yáo was unable to promote them.
Shùn, as a minister of Yáo,
promoted the Eight Worthies (Bā Kǎi),
and made them masters of Hòutǔ (后土),
to regulate all affairs,
so that everything was timely and orderly,
the earth was leveled, and heaven was completed.
He promoted the Eight Worthies (Bā Yuán),
and sent them to spread the five teachings in all directions:
fatherly righteousness, motherly kindness, brotherly friendship,
fraternal respect, and filial piety.
Within, there was peace, and without, there was accomplishment.
"In the past, Dì Hóngshì
had an unworthy son,
who concealed righteousness and hid treachery,
and loved to practice violent vices;
he was an ugly kind of evil thing.
Obstinate and unfriendly,
he associated with those like him,
and the people of the world called him Hùndūn (渾敦).
Shǎohào shì
had an unworthy son,
who destroyed trust and abandoned loyalty,
He embellishes wicked words;
he silences those who expose slander and promotes the mediocre and sycophantic;
he embraces slander and seeks out hidden faults;
in order to falsely accuse those of great virtue.
The people of the world call him "Qióngqí."
Zhuānxū had an unworthy son,
who could not be taught,
and did not understand what was said.
If told, he was obstinate;
if left alone, he was foolishly stubborn;
arrogant and defiant of enlightened virtue,
in order to disrupt the natural order.
The people of the world call him "Táowù."
These three clans
inherited their wickedness for generations,
increasing their evil reputation,
even up to the time of Yáo,
and Yáo was unable to remove them.
The Jìnyún clan
had an unworthy son
who was greedy for food and drink,
and covetous of wealth and goods.
He indulged in aggressive desires and extravagant living,
being impossible to satisfy.
He amassed and accumulated possessions,
without knowing any limits.
He did not share with the orphans and widows,
nor did he care for the poor and needy.
The people of the world compared them to the three evil ones,
and called them "Tāotiè."
Shùn served Yáo,
acting as host at the four gates,
banishing the clans of the four evil ones:
Húndùn, Qióngqí, Táowù, and Tāotiè,
casting them out to the four borders,
to ward off chī and mèi (types of demons).
Therefore, when Yáo died,
the world was as one,
united in supporting Shùn,
considering him the Son of Heaven,
because he promoted the sixteen worthy ministers
and removed the four evil ones.
Therefore, the *Yú Shū* (Book of Yú) enumerates Shùn's accomplishments,
saying: "He carefully embodied the five constant virtues,
and the five constant virtues were successfully followed."
There was no disobedience to teachings.
It says:
"He admitted them to the hundred offices,
and the hundred offices were properly ordered."
There was no neglect of affairs.
It says:
"He acted as host at the four gates,
and the four gates were harmonious."
There were no evil people.
"Shùn had twenty great accomplishments
and became the Son of Heaven.
Now, although Xíngfǔ has not yet obtained a single good person,
he has removed one evil one.
This is one-twentieth of Shùn's achievements.
It is one-twentieth of Shùn's achievements,
and it is hoped that he will be spared from misfortune!"
B6.18.8 Zú Dàozhāo, a scion of the Sòng Wǔ clan,
intended to support Sīchéng Xū 司城須 in causing rebellion.
In the twelfth month,
the Duke of Sòng 宋 killed his younger brother Xū 須 and Zhāo Gōngzǐ 昭公子,
and ordered the descendants of Dài 戴, Zhuāng 莊, and Huán 桓 to attack the Wǔ 武 clan at the residence of Sīmǎ Zǐbó 司馬子伯,
and consequently expelled the clans of Wǔ 武 and Mù 穆.
He appointed Gōngsūn Shī 公孫師 as Sīchéng 司城.
Gōngzǐ Zhāo 公子朝 died,
and he appointed Yuè Lǚ 樂呂 as Sīkòu 司寇
to pacify the people of the state.
Duke Xuān 宣公
A7.1 *Annals of the First Year of Duke Xuān*
A7.1.1 In the first year, in the spring,
in the first month of the royal calendar,
the Duke ascended the throne.
A7.1.2 Gōngzǐ Suì 公子遂 went to Qí 齊 to escort the daughter.
A7.1.3 In the third month,
Suì 遂 brought back Lady Fù Jiāng 婦姜 from Qí 齊 to be his wife.
A7.1.4 In the summer,
Jìsūn Xíngfù 季孫行父 went to Qí 齊.
A7.1.5 Jìn 晉 exiled its grand master Xū Jiǎfù 胥甲父 to Wèi 衛.
A7.1.6 The Duke met with the Marquis of Qí 齊 at Píngzhōu 平州.
A7.1.7 Gōngzǐ Suì went to Qí.
A7.1.8 In the sixth month,
the people of Qí seized the fields west of the Jì River.
A7.1.9 In autumn,
the Viscount of Zhū came to court.
A7.1.10 The Viscount of Chǔ and
the people of Zhèng invaded Chén,
and then invaded Sòng.
Zhào Dùn of Jìn led an army to rescue Chén.
The Duke of Sòng,
the Marquis of Chén,
the Marquis of Wèi, and
the Count of Cáo met the Jìn army at Fěilín and
attacked Zhèng.
A7.1.11 In winter,
Zhào Chuān of Jìn led an army to invade Chóng.
A7.1.12 The people of Jìn and
the people of Sòng attacked Zhèng.
B7.1 *Commentary on the First Year of Duke Xuān*
B7.1.1 In the first year, in the spring,
in the king's first month,
Gōngzǐ Suì went to Qí to escort the daughter back.
He respected the ruler's command.
B7.1.2 In the third month,
Suì arrived from Qí with the lady Fù Jiāng.
He honored the lady.
B7.1.3 In the summer,
Jì Wénzǐ went to Qí
to offer bribes to request a meeting.
B7.1.4 The people of Jìn punished those who did not obey orders,
exiling Xū Jiǎfù to Wèi,
and establishing Xū Kè.
Xiān Xīn fled to Qí.
B7.1.5 They met at Píngzhōu
to settle the ruler's position.
B7.1.6 Dōngmén Xiāngzhòng went to Qí
to acknowledge the agreement.
B7.1.7 In the sixth month,
the people of Qí took the fields west of the Jì River
on behalf of establishing the ruler,
as a bribe for Qí.
B7.1.8 When the people of Sòng assassinated Duke Zhāo,
Xún Línfǔ of Jìn led the armies of the various lords
to attack Sòng.
Sòng and Jìn made peace,
and Duke Wén of Sòng received the covenant from Jìn.
He also convened the lords at Hù,
intending to attack Qí on behalf of Lǔ,
but they all accepted bribes
and returned.
Duke Mù of Zhèng said:
"Jìn is not worth associating with."
Consequently, he received the covenant from Chǔ.
Upon the death of Duke Gòng of Chén,
the people of Chǔ were disrespectful.
Duke Líng of Chén received the covenant from Jìn.
In the autumn,
the Viscount of Chǔ invaded Chén,
and then invaded Sòng.
Zhào Dùn of Jìn led an army to rescue Chén and Sòng.
They met at Fěilín
to attack Zhèng.
Wěi Gǔ of Chǔ rescued Zhèng,
encountering them at Běilín,
and captured Xiè Yáng of Jìn.
The people of Jìn then returned.
B7.1.9 Jìn wanted to seek peace with Qín.
Zhào Chuān said:
"If I invade Chóng,
Qín is anxious about Chóng,
and will surely rescue it.
I will use this to seek peace."
In the winter,
Zhào Chuān invaded Chóng.
Qín did not make peace with them.
B7.1.10 The people of Jìn attacked Zhèng.
to avenge the battle of Běi Lín.
Thereupon, the Lord of Jìn became extravagant.
Zhào Xuānzi was in charge of the government,
and frequently gave advice, but it was not heeded.
Therefore, they did not contend with Chǔ.
A7.2 *The Annals of the Second Year of Duke Xuān*
A7.2.1 In the second year, in spring,
in the royal second month, on the day rénzǐ,
Sòng Huá Yuán led the army and the Zhèng noble, Gōngzǐ Guīshēng, led the army,
and they fought at Dàjí.
The Sòng army was utterly defeated,
and Huá Yuán of Sòng was captured.
A7.2.2 The Qín army attacked Jìn.
A7.2.3 In summer,
the people of Jìn,
the people of Sòng,
the people of Wèi,
and the people of Chén invaded Zhèng.
A7.2.4 In the ninth month, on the day yǐchǒu,
Zhào Dùn of Jìn assassinated his lord Yí Gāo.
A7.2.5 In the tenth month, on the day yǐhài,
the Heavenly King passed away.
B7.2 *Zuǒ Zhuàn*, Year 2 of Duke Xuān
B7.2.1 In the spring of the second year,
Gōngzǐ Guīshēng of Zhèng, having received orders from Chǔ, attacked Sòng.
Huá Yuán and Yuè Lǚ of Sòng met him in battle.
On the day rénzǐ in the second month,
they fought at Dàjí.
The Sòng army was utterly defeated.
Huá Yuán was captured,
Yuè Lǚ was taken prisoner, along with four hundred and sixty chariots and two hundred and fifty captives, and one hundred heads were cut off.
Kuáng Jiǎo ran over a man of Zhèng with his chariot;
the man of Zhèng fell into a well.
He turned his halberd upside down and pulled him out,
and Kuáng Jiǎo was captured.
The junzi (superior man) said,
"To violate ritual and disobey orders
is fitting to be captured.
*Róng*
and Zhāo were resolute and decisive
in listening to it, this is called ritual.
Killing the enemy is *guǒ* (decisive),
carrying out decisiveness is *yì* (resolute).
To exchange him is a disgrace."
When about to fight, Huá Yuán 華元 slaughtered sheep to feed the soldiers,
but his charioteer Yáng Zhēn 羊斟 did not participate.
When the battle came,
he said:
"For yesterday's sheep,
you were in charge;
for today's affair,
I am in charge."
He drove [the chariot] into the ranks of the army of Zhèng 鄭,
therefore they were defeated.
The junzi 君子 (gentleman) said
of Yáng Zhēn 羊斟, "He is inhuman.
Because of his personal grievance,
he ruined the state and destroyed the people.
What punishment could be greater than this?
The *Shī* 詩 (Book of Poetry) speaks of
'a man without goodness';
that is what it means by Yáng Zhēn 羊斟!
To injure the people in order to satisfy his desires!"
The people of Sòng 宋 used a hundred war chariots and a hundred teams of variegated horses to redeem Huá Yuán 華元 from Zhèng 鄭.
When half [of the ransom] had been paid,
Huá Yuán 華元 fled back home.
He stood outside the gate,
announced himself, and entered.
He saw Shū Zāng 叔牂,
and said:
"Were your horses all right?"
He replied:
"It is not a horse,
it is a man."
They joined together and came running.
In Sòng city,
Huá Yuán was inspecting the fortifications,
touring the defenses.
The city wall laborers sang:
"Wide are his eyes,
white is his belly,
he abandons his armor and returns.
Oh, think! Oh, think!
He abandons his armor and comes back."
He had his second charioteer say to them:
"Cattle have hides,
rhinoceros hides are still plentiful,
why abandon your armor?"
The laborers said:
"If we follow what has a hide,
what about the red lacquer?"
Huá Yuán said:
"Remove it!
Their mouths are many, and we are few."
B7.2.2 The Qin army attacked Jin,
to avenge Chóng,
and then besieged Jiāo.
In summer,
Zhào Dùn of Jin came to the rescue of Jiāo,
then from Yīndì,
together with the armies of the lords, invaded Zhèng,
to avenge the battle of Dàjí.
Dòu Jiāo of Chu came to the rescue of Zhèng,
saying:
"If they desire the feudal lords,
ér è qí nán hū?" [how can you despise the difficulties that come with them?”]
Suì cì yú Zhèng [Then he encamped in Zhèng]
yǐ dài Jìn shī. [to await the army of Jìn.]
Zhào Dùn yuē: [Zhào Dùn said:]
"Bǐ zōng jìng yú Chǔ, [“They are relying on Chǔ,]
dài jiāng bì yǐ. [they will probably perish.]
Gū yì qí jí." [Let us temporarily increase their affliction.”]
Nǎi qù zhī. [Then they departed.]
B7.2.3 Jìn Líng Gōng bù jūn: [Jìn Líng Gōng was not a ruler:]
Hòu liǎn yǐ diāo qiáng, [He heavily taxed the people to carve the walls,]
cóng tái shàng dàn rén, [shot at people from atop a terrace,]
ér guān qí bì wán yě; [and watched them dodge the pellets;]
Zǎifū ér xióng fán bù shú, [When the cook did not properly cook the bear paws,]
shā zhī, [he killed him,]
zhì zhū běn, [placed him in a basket,]
shǐ fùrén zài yǐ guò cháo. [and made a woman carry it past the court.]
Zhào Dùn, Shì Jì jiàn qí shǒu, [Zhào Dùn and Shì Jì saw his hand,]
wèn qí gù, [asked the reason for it,]
ér huàn zhī. [and were troubled by it.]
Jiāng jiàn, [When they were about to remonstrate,]
Shì Jì yuē: [Shì Jì said:]
"Jiàn ér bù rù, [“If remonstration is not heeded,]
then no one will continue it.
If the assembly requests to proceed first,
and you do not enter,
then your son will continue it."
Three times he advanced
to the eaves,
and then he looked at it,
saying,
"I know where I went wrong,
I will change it."
He bowed his head and replied,
"Who is without fault?
To err and be able to correct oneself,
nothing is greater than that.
The *Shi Jing* says:
'There is none who does not have a beginning,
but few are able to have an end.'
If this is the case,
then few will be able to remedy their faults.
If you, my lord, can have an end,
then the state will be secure,
and it is not only your ministers who will rely on you.
It also says:
'The royal robes have defects,
only Zhòng Shānfǔ can mend them,'
indicating the ability to correct faults.
If you, my lord, can mend your faults,
then the royal robes will not be abandoned."
Still, he did not change.
Xuān Zǐ repeatedly remonstrated,
the duke became troubled by it,
and sent Chú Ní to assassinate him.
He went in the morning,
the sleeping quarters were open,
dressed in full attire, preparing to attend court.
It was still early,
he sat and dozed.
Chú Ní withdrew,
sighed and said:
"Not forgetting reverence and respect,
he is a lord of the people.
To assassinate a lord of the people
is disloyal;
to abandon the command of the ruler
is untrustworthy.
To have one of these,
is not as good as death."
He killed himself by running into a locust tree.
In the ninth month of autumn,
the Lord of Jìn entertained Zhào Dùn with wine,
and hid armored soldiers,
planning to attack him.
His (Zhào Dùn's) right attendant, Tí Mí Míng, knew this,
rushed forward and ascended (the steps),
saying:
"Your servant attends Your Lordship's banquet,
"[To drink] past three rounds
is not in accordance with ritual."
Thereupon, he supported him to descend [from the chariot].
The Duke incited a large dog at him,
and it openly attacked and killed him.
Dùn said,
"To abandon a man and use a dog,
even if [the dog] is fierce, what use is it!"
Dòu Qiě was about to leave.
Tí Mímíng died for him.
Earlier,
Xuānzǐ was hunting at Shǒushān,
and lodged at Yìsāng.
He saw Líng Zhé starving,
and asked about his illness.
He said,
"I have not eaten for three days."
He fed him,
and left half of it.
He asked him about it.
He said,
"I have been serving as an official for three years,
and do not yet know if my mother is alive or not.
Now I am near her,
please allow me to leave it for her."
He made him finish it,
and prepared for him a basket of food and meat,
placing it in a sack to give to him.
Soon after, he served as an attendant for the duke,
reversing his halberd to defend the duke's followers
and save them.
He was asked why.
He replied,
"He was a starving man from Yìsāng."
When asked his name and address,
he did not tell and withdrew,
and then fled.
On the day yǐchǒu,
Zhào Chuān killed Duke Líng in the Peach Garden.
Xuān Zi had not yet left the mountains when he returned.
The Grand Scribe wrote:
"Zhào Dùn assassinated his ruler,"
and showed it to the court.
Xuān Zi said,
"That is not so."
The Grand Scribe replied,
"You are the chief minister,
you did not flee beyond the border,
and upon returning, you did not punish the murderer.
If it wasn't you, then who?"
Xuān Zi said,
"Alas!
The *Book of Odes* says:
'What I cherish,
brings upon myself this sorrow.'
It speaks of me."
Kǒngzǐ said:
"Dǒng Hú
was a good historian of ancient times;
his writing did not conceal.
Zhào Xuānzǐ
was a good high official of ancient times;
he accepted blame for upholding the law.
It is a pity
that he was spared only by fleeing the border."
Xuānzǐ sent Zhào Chuān to meet the young master Hēi Tún in Zhōu and install him [as ruler].
On rénshēn,
they held court at the Wǔ Temple.
B7.2.4 Initially,
during the revolt of Lì Jī,
they swore not to keep princes in groups,
and from then on, Jìn had no ducal clan.
When Duke Chéng ascended to the throne,
he made the legitimate sons of eunuch officials
and gave them land
to serve as the ducal clan.
He also made the remaining sons of eunuchs
remain as remaining sons.
Their sons of concubines were called "public officers".
Jìn thereby had ducal clan members, remaining sons, and public officers.
Zhào Dùn requested that Kuò be made a ducal clan member,
saying:
"He is the beloved son of the Jī family of the ruler.
Without the Jī family of the ruler
"Then this minister is a Dí person."
The duke permitted it.
In winter,
Zhào Dùn made the clan of carriages with yak-tail banners,
and had Bǐng Jì use his old clan to become a grand master of the ducal clan.
A7.3 *The Annals of the Third Year of Duke Xuān*
A7.3.1 In the spring of the third year,
in the first month of the king,
the mouth of the suburban ox was injured,
so they changed and divined for another ox.
The ox died,
so they did not perform the suburban sacrifice.
It was still the time of three full moons.
A7.3.2 The King Kuāng was buried.
A7.3.3 The Viscount of Chǔ attacked the Róng of Lùhún.
A7.3.4 In summer,
the people of Chǔ invaded Zhèng.
A7.3.5 In autumn,
the Red Dí invaded Qí.
A7.3.6 The army of Sòng besieged Cáo.
A7.3.7 In the tenth month, on the day bǐngxū,
Zhèng Bó Lán died.
A7.3.8 The burial of Duke Mù of Zhèng.
B7.3 *Commentary on the Third Year of Duke Xuān*
B7.3.1 In the spring of the third year,
not performing the suburban sacrifice
but performing the *wàng* sacrifice,
both were contrary to ritual.
The *wàng* sacrifice
is a type of suburban sacrifice.
Not performing the suburban sacrifice,
then there is also nothing to *wàng* towards.
B7.3.2 The Marquis of Jìn attacked Zhèng,
reaching Yǎn.
Zhèng and Jìn made peace,
and Shì Huì entered into an alliance.
B7.3.3 The Viscount of Chǔ attacked the Róng of Lùhún,
and then reached the Luo River,
displaying his troops on the border of Zhōu.
King Dìng sent Wángsūn Mǎn to comfort the Viscount of Chǔ.
The Viscount of Chǔ asked about the size
and weight of the tripods.
He replied,
"It lies in virtue, not in the tripods.
In the past, when the Xià dynasty possessed virtue,
distant regions sent depictions of their products,
They presented tribute metal from the nine provinces,
and cast cauldrons to represent the objects of those provinces,
preparing them with representations of all things,
so that the people would know the spirits and the wicked.
Therefore, when the people entered the rivers, marshes, mountains, and forests,
they would not encounter misfortune.
The chī (螭) and mèi wǎngliǎng (魅罔兩) spirits
would not be able to encounter them.
Thus, they were able to harmonize with those above and below,
in order to receive the blessings of Heaven.
When Jié (桀) possessed darkened virtue,
the cauldrons were moved to the Shang dynasty,
lasting for six hundred years.
When Zhòu (紂) of Shang was tyrannical,
the cauldrons were moved to the Zhou dynasty.
The glory of virtue,
though small,
is weighty.
Wickedness, perversity, darkness, and chaos,
though great,
are light.
Heaven assists bright virtue,
and has a limit to where it ends.
Chéng Wáng (成王) fixed the cauldrons at Jiá Rǔ (郟鄏),
predicting thirty generations
and seven hundred years,
which was ordained by Heaven.
Although the virtue of Zhou declined,
the mandate of Heaven had not yet changed.
The lightness or weight of the cauldrons
is not to be questioned."
B7.3.4 In summer,
the people of Chǔ (楚) invaded Zhèng (鄭),
because Zhèng (鄭) was formerly allied with Jìn (晉).
B7.3.5 In the third year of Sòng Wén Gōng's reign,
he killed his maternal younger brother Xū and Zhāo's son,
which was plotted by the Wǔ clan.
He ordered the descendants of Dài and Huán to attack the Wǔ clan at the residence of Sīmǎ Zǐbó,
and completely expelled the descendants of Wǔ and Mù.
The descendants of Wǔ and Mù used the army of Cáo to attack Sòng.
In autumn,
the Sòng army besieged Cáo,
to avenge the rebellion of the Wǔ clan.
B7.3.6 In winter,
Zhèng Mù Gōng died.
Initially,
Zhèng Wén Gōng had a humble concubine named Yān Jí,
who dreamed that an angel gave her an orchid,
saying:
"I am Bó Tiáo.
I am
your ancestor.
Use this to be your son.
Because the orchid has the fragrance of a kingdom,
people will be charmed by it."
Soon after, Wén Gōng saw her,
He gave her an orchid and had intercourse with her.
She declined, saying:
"I am not talented,
but fortunately I have a child.
If you don't believe me,
may I ask for the orchid as proof?"
The duke said:
"Agreed."
She gave birth to Duke Mù,
and named him Lán.
Duke Wén repaid the Zhèng ruler's concubine, named Chén Guī,
who gave birth to Zǐ Huá and Zǐ Zāng.
Zǐ Zāng committed a crime and fled.
He enticed Zǐ Huá
and killed him in Nánlǐ,
and had thieves kill Zǐ Zāng between Chén and Sòng.
He then married from Jiāng,
and gave birth to Gōngzǐ Shì.
He went to the court of Chǔ,
and the people of Chǔ poisoned him,
and he died at Yè.
He then married from Sū,
and gave birth to Zǐ Xiá and Zǐ Yú Mí.
Yú Mí died young.
Xiè Jià disliked Xiá,
and Duke Wén also disliked him,
so he was not established as heir.
The duke expelled the many princes,
Gōngzǐ Lán 公子蘭 fled to Jìn 晉 and
followed Duke Wén of Jìn 晉文公 in attacking Zhèng 鄭.
Shí Kuí 石癸 said:
"I have heard that when the Ji 姬 and Jí 姞 clans intermarry,
their descendants will surely be numerous.
Jí 姞
is an auspicious person,
the primary consort of Hòu Jì 后稷.
Now, Gōngzǐ Lán 公子蘭
is a maternal nephew of the Jí 姞 clan;
Heaven may be opening the way for him.
He will surely become the ruler,
and his descendants will surely be numerous.
Let us receive him first,
which can rival the favor of the prince."
Together with Kǒng Jiāngchú 孔將鉏 and Hóu Xuānduō 侯宣多, they received him,
swore an oath at the Grand Palace
and established him,
in order to make peace with Jìn 晉.
Duke Mù 穆公 fell ill
and said:
"If Lán 蘭 dies,
will I also die?
He is the reason for my existence."
He cut off [ties with] Lán 蘭 and died.
A7.4 *Xuān Gōng* Year 4 *Jīng*
A7.4.1 In the spring of the fourth year,
In the first month of the year,
the Duke and the Marquis of Qí made peace with Jǔ and Tán.
The people of Jǔ were unwilling.
The Duke attacked Jǔ,
and captured Xiàng.
A7.4.2 Duke Dào of Qín died.
A7.4.3 In the sixth month of summer, on the day yǐyǒu,
Gōngzǐ Guīshēng of Zhèng assassinated his lord, Yí.
A7.4.4 The Chì Dí invaded Qí.
A7.4.5 In autumn,
the Duke went to Qí.
A7.4.6 The Duke returned from Qí.
A7.4.7 In winter,
the Viscount of Chǔ attacked Zhèng.
B7.4 Commentary on the Fourth Year of Duke Xuān
B7.4.1 In the spring of the fourth year,
the Duke and the Marquis of Qí made peace with Jǔ and Tán,
but the people of Jǔ were unwilling.
The Duke attacked Jǔ,
and captured Xiàng,
This is not in accordance with ritual propriety.
To govern a state is done through ritual propriety,
not through chaos.
To attack without governing is
chaos.
To pacify chaos with chaos,
what governance is there?
Without governance,
how can ritual propriety be practiced?
B7.4.2 A person from Chǔ presented a soft-shelled turtle to Duke Líng of Zhèng.
Gōngzǐ Sòng and Zǐjiā were about to go in to see him.
The index finger of Zǐgōng moved,
and he showed it to Zǐjiā,
saying,
"Another day when I am like this,
I will certainly taste something unusual."
When they entered,
the cook was about to butcher the soft-shelled turtle.
They looked at each other and smiled.
The duke asked them about it,
and Zǐjiā told him.
When the ministers were eating soft-shelled turtle
soup, he summoned Zǐgōng but did not give him any.
Zǐgōng became angry,
dipped his finger into the pot,
tasted it, and left.
The duke was enraged
and wanted to kill Zǐgōng.
Zǐgōng and Zǐjiā plotted to act first.
Zǐjiā said,
"Even raising an old animal,
one still hesitates to kill it,
how much more so a ruler?"
He then turned around and slandered Zǐjiā.
Zǐjiā, fearful, followed him.
In summer,
they assassinated Líng Gōng.
The *Chūnqiū* states, "The Zheng nobleman Guīshēng assassinated his ruler Yí,"
(indicating) that his authority was insufficient.
The gentleman said,
"To be benevolent but not martial
means that one cannot achieve anything."
Generally, in cases of regicide,
if the title "ruler" is used,
it means the ruler was without principle;
if the title "minister" is used,
it is the minister's crime.
The people of Zhèng wanted to install Zǐliáng.
He declined, saying,
"In terms of worthiness,
Qùjí is not sufficient;
in terms of obedience,
then Gōngzǐ Jiān is the eldest."
Therefore, they installed Xiāng Gōng.
Xiāng Gōng intended to remove the Mù clan
and keep Zǐliáng.
Zǐ Liáng
said,
"The Mù lineage should be preserved;
this is indeed my wish.
If they are to be destroyed,
then all will perish.
What is the point of eliminating disease (qù jí)?"
Thus he spared them,
and they all became grand officers (dàfū).
B7.4.3 Initially,
the Chǔ Minister of War (Sīmǎ) Zǐ Liáng fathered a son named Yuè Jiāo.
Zǐ Wén said,
"He must be killed!
This child
has the appearance of a bear and tiger, and the voice of a jackal and wolf.
If he is not killed,
he will surely destroy the Ruò Áo lineage.
A proverb says,
'A wolf cub has a wild heart.'
This is a wolf;
how can he be kept?"
Zǐ Liáng would not allow it.
Zǐ Wén considered this a great sorrow.
When he was about to die,
he gathered his clan
and said,
"If Jiāo becomes involved in government,
then flee quickly,
would not extend to difficulties."
And he wept, saying,
"Even ghosts seek food;
wouldn't the ghosts of the Ruò Áo (若敖) clan be starving!"
When the *lìngyǐn* Zǐwén (子文) died,
Dòu Bān (鬭般) became *lìngyǐn*,
and Zǐ Yuè (子越) became *sīmǎ*.
Wěi Jiǎ (蒍賈) became *gōngzhèng*,
slandered Zǐ Yáng (子揚) and killed him.
Zǐ Yuè (子越) became *lìngyǐn*,
and he himself became *sīmǎ*.
Zǐ Yuè (子越) also disliked him,
so, using the excuse that he was of the Ruò Áo (若敖) clan,
he imprisoned Bó Yíng (伯嬴) at Liáoyáng (轑陽) and killed him,
then took up residence in Zhēngyě (烝野),
intending to attack the king.
The king offered the sons of the three ministers as hostages,
but he did not accept them.
He mustered his army at the banks of the Zhāng (漳) River.
In the autumn, on the *wùxū* day of the seventh month,
the ruler of Chǔ (楚) fought against the Ruò Áo (若敖) clan at Gāohǔ (皋滸).
Bó Fén (伯棼) shot at the king,
(his arrow) penetrated the *zhōu* (輈),
and reached the *gǔfū* (鼓跗),
sticking in the *dīngníng* (丁寧).
He shot again,
(his arrow) penetrated the *zhōu* (輈),
and pierced through the *lìgū* (笠轂).
The army was afraid
and retreated.
The king sent someone to inspect the army, saying:
"My late ancestor, King Wén (文王), conquered Xī (息)
and obtained three arrows.
Bó Fén (伯棼) stole two of them.
and they are all used up now."
He beat the drums and advanced,
and then destroyed the Ruò Áo clan.
Initially,
Ruò Áo married a woman from Yūn and
had Dòu Bóbǐ.
Ruò Áo died,
and Dòu Bóbǐ followed his mother and lived in Yūn.
He had illicit relations with the daughter of the lord of Yūn,
and she gave birth to Zǐ Wén.
The Lady of Yūn ordered the child to be abandoned in a dream forest.
A tiger nursed him.
The Lord of Yūn was hunting
and saw him.
He was afraid and returned.
The Lady told him about it,
and so he sent someone to retrieve the child.
The people of Chǔ called milk "gǔ"
and called tigers "yūtú,"
so he was named Gǔ Yūtú.
He married his daughter to Bóbǐ.
She was the mother of Zǐ Wén, who became Prime Minister.
His grandson, Zhēn Yǐn Kè Huáng, was sent on a mission to Qí.
On his return, he passed through Sòng
and heard of the rebellion.
His attendants said,
"We cannot enter."
Zhēn Yǐn said,
"If I abandon the ruler's command,
who else would receive it?
The ruler
is like Heaven.
Can one escape Heaven?"
Thereupon, he returned,
reported his mission,
and turned himself in to the Minister of Crime.
The King, thinking of Zǐ Wén's governance of the state of Chǔ,
said,
"Zǐ Wén has no heir;
how will this encourage good?"
He had him reinstated in his former position
and changed the order to allow him to live.
B7.4.4 In winter,
the Viscount of Chǔ attacked Zhèng,
and Zhèng did not submit.
A7.5 *The Annals for the Fifth Year of Duke Xuān*
A7.5.1 In the fifth year, in spring,
the Duke went to Qí.
A7.5.2 In summer,
the Duke returned from Qí.
A7.5.3 In autumn, the ninth month,
Gāo Gù of Qí came to escort Shū Jī.
A7.5.4 Shūsūn Déchén died.
A7.5.5 In winter,
Gāo Gù of Qí and Shū Jī came.
A7.5.6 The people of Chǔ attacked Zhèng.
B7.5 *Commentary to the Fifth Year of Duke Xuān*
B7.5.1 In the spring of the fifth year,
the Duke went to Qí.
Gāo Gù had the Marquis of Qí detain the Duke
and requested Shū Jī.
the Duke returned from Qí;
the writing
is an error.
B7.5.3 In autumn, the ninth month,
Gāo Gù of Qí came to escort the woman;
he did it himself.
Therefore, the text says, "escorted Shū Jī";
a minister escorted her himself.
B7.5.4 In winter,
they came,
and returned the horses.
B7.5.5 The Chǔ (楚) ruler attacked Zhèng (鄭).
Chén (陳) and Chǔ made peace.
Jìn (晉) Xún Línfù (荀林父) rescued Zhèng and
attacked Chén.
A7.6 *The Sixth Year of Duke Xuān*
A7.6.1 In the spring of the sixth year,
Jìn Zhào Dùn (趙盾) and
Wèi Sūn Miǎn (孫免) invaded Chén.
A7.6.2 In summer, the fourth month.
A7.6.3 In autumn, the eighth month,
locusts (appeared).
A7.6.4 In winter, the tenth month.
B7.6 *Commentary on the Sixth Year of Duke Xuān*
B7.6.1 In the spring of the sixth year,
Jìn and Wèi invaded Chén,
because Chén had submitted to Chǔ.
B7.6.2 In summer,
King Dìng (定王) sent Zǐfú (子服) to Qí (齊) to seek a consort.
B7.6.3 In autumn,
The Chì Dí 赤狄 attacked Jìn 晉,
besieging Huái 懷 and Xíngqiū 邢丘.
The ruler of Jìn 晉 wished to attack them.
Zhōngháng Huánzǐ 中行桓子 said,
"Make their people suffer hardship,
so as to fill their measure of iniquity.
Then they can be destroyed.
The *Zhōu Shū* 周書 says,
'Destroy the Róng 戎 and the Yīn 殷,'
this is what it means."
B7.6.4 In winter,
Duke Zhao 昭 (of Lǔ 魯) summoned Duke Huán 桓 (of Qí 齊) to escort the queen back from Qí 齊.
B7.6.5 The Chǔ 楚 people attacked Zhèng 鄭,
captured Chéng 成 and returned.
B7.6.6 The Zhèng 鄭 prince, Gōngzǐ Mànmǎn 公子曼滿, spoke with Wángzǐ Bóliao 王子伯廖,
desiring to become a high minister.
Bóliao 伯廖 told people,
"Lacking virtue and being greedy,
it is in the *Zhōu Yì* 周易, *Fēng* 豐 ䷶ changing to *Lí* 離 ䷝,
he will not escape it."
After a year,
the people of Zhèng 鄭 killed him.
A7.7 *Xuān Gōng Qī Nián Jīng* 宣公七年經
A7.7.1 In the seventh year, spring,
the lord of Wèi 衛 sent Sūn Liángfū 孫良夫 to come and form a covenant.
A7.7.2 In summer,
the Duke met with Marquis Qí to attack Lái.
A7.7.3 In autumn,
the Duke returned from attacking Lái.
A7.7.4 There was a great drought.
A7.7.5 In winter,
the Duke met with the Marquis of Jìn,
the Duke of Sòng,
the Marquis of Wèi,
the Count of Zhèng,
and the Count of Cáo at Hēirǎng.
B7.7 *Zuǒ Zhuàn*, Seventh Year of Duke Xuān
B7.7.1 In the spring of the seventh year,
Sūn Huánzǐ of Wèi came to pledge alliance,
and they began to communicate.
Furthermore, they plotted to meet with Jìn.
B7.7.2 In summer,
the Duke met with the Marquis of Qí to attack Lái,
but he was not involved in the planning.
Whenever an army goes out,
being involved in the planning is called "jí (及)",
and not being involved in the planning is called "huì (會)".
B7.7.3 The Red Dí invaded Jìn,
Taking the grain that faces the shade.
B7.7.4 Zhèng and Jìn made peace.
It was the plan of Gōngzǐ Sòng,
therefore, he assisted the Earl of Zhèng in holding the meeting.
In winter,
they made an alliance at Hēirǎng.
Wángshū Huángōng attended,
to discuss their discord.
When the Marquis of Jìn was established,
the Duke did not give court audience,
nor did he send a senior official on a diplomatic visit.
The people of Jìn detained the Duke at the meeting.
They made an alliance at Huángfǔ,
but the Duke did not participate in the alliance.
He avoided it with bribes.
Therefore, the alliance at Hēirǎng was not recorded,
to conceal it.
A7.8 *The Annals of the Eighth Year of Duke Xuān*
A7.8.1 In the eighth year, spring,
the Duke returned from the meeting.
A7.8.2 In summer, the sixth month,
Gōngzǐ Suì went to Qí,
but returned from Huáng.
A7.8.3 On Xīnsì,
there was a ceremony at the Great Temple.
Zhòng Suí died in Chuí.
On the day rénwǔ,
they still performed the Yì sacrifice.
Wàn entered,
and the yuè pipe was removed.
A7.8.4 On the day wùzǐ,
Lady Yíng Shì died.
A7.8.5 The Jìn army and the
White Di attacked Qín.
A7.8.6 The Chǔ people destroyed Shūliǎo.
A7.8.7 In the autumn, on the seventh month, jiǎzǐ,
there was a solar eclipse,
total.
A7.8.8 In winter, on the tenth month, jǐchǒu,
they buried my minor ruler, Jìng Yíng.
It rained, and they were unable to bury her.
On gēngyín,
at midday, they were able to bury her.
A7.8.9 They fortified Píngyáng.
A7.8.10 The Chǔ army attacked Chén.
B7.8 *Xuān Gōng* (Duke Xuan) Year 8 *Zhuàn* (Commentary)
B7.8.1 In the spring of the eighth year, the *Bái Dí* (White Di) and *Jìn* (Jin) made peace.
In the summer,
there was a meeting of *Jìn* to attack *Qín* (Qin).
The people of *Jìn* captured a spy from *Qín*
and killed him in the market of *Jiàng* (Jiang).
After six days, he revived.
B7.8.2 There was a matter at the Great Temple.
*Xiāng Zhòng* (Xiang Zhong) died and there was a *yì* ritual,
which was not in accordance with ritual.
B7.8.3 Because *Chǔ* (Chu) considered that *Zhòng Shū* (Zhong Shu) had rebelled,
they attacked *Shū Liǎo* (Shu Liao) and
destroyed it.
The Viscount of *Chǔ* expanded his territory.
Reaching the *Huá Ruì* (Hua Rui) River,
he formed an alliance with *Wú* (Wu) and *Yuè* (Yue) and returned.
B7.8.4 *Jìn Xū Kè* (Jin Xu Ke) suffered from a *gǔ* disease,
and *Xì Quē* (Xi Que) administered the government.
In the autumn,
*Xū Kè* was dismissed
and *Zhào Shuò* (Zhao Shuo) was made to assist the Lower Army.
B7.8.5 In the winter,
*Jìng Yíng* (Jing Ying) was buried.
There was a drought, and no hemp,
so they began to use *gé fú* (kudzu cloth).
Rain
prevented burial;
this is in accordance with ritual.
According to ritual,
when divining for a burial date,
one first chooses a distant day
to avoid causing grief.
B7.8.6 The city of Píngyáng 平陽 was leveled;
the *Shū*
records the time.
B7.8.7 Chén 陳 and Jìn 晉 were at peace.
The Chǔ 楚 army attacked Chén 陳
and returned after capturing Chéng 成.
A7.9 *Xuān Gōng* 宣公, year nine, *Jīng* 經
A7.9.1 In the ninth year, spring,
the king's first month,
the duke went to Qí 齊.
A7.9.2 The duke returned from Qí 齊.
A7.9.3 In summer,
Zhòngsūn Miè 仲孫蔑 went to the capital.
A7.9.4 The Marquis of Qí 齊 attacked Lái 萊.
A7.9.5 In autumn,
Gēnmóu 根牟 was captured.
A7.9.6 In the eighth month, the Viscount of Téng died.
A7.9.7 In the ninth month, the Marquis of Jìn, the Duke of Sòng, the Marquis of Wèi, the Earl of Zhèng, and the Earl of Cáo met at Hù.
A7.9.8 Xún Línfǔ of Jìn led an army to attack Chén.
A7.9.9 On the day of xīnyǒu, the Marquis of Jìn, Hēi Tún, died at Hù.
A7.9.10 In the tenth month, on the day of guǐyǒu, the Marquis of Wèi, Zhèng, died.
A7.9.11 The people of Sòng besieged Téng.
A7.9.12 The Viscount of Chǔ attacked Zhèng.
A7.9.13 Xì Quē of Jìn led an army to rescue Zhèng.
A7.9.14 Chén killed its grand officer, Xiè Yě.
B7.9 *Zuǒ Zhuàn*, Year 9 of Duke Xuān
B7.9.1 In the spring of the ninth year,
the king sent someone to come and request betrothal gifts.
In the summer,
Mèng Xiànzǐ paid a formal visit to the Zhou court.
The king considered him to possess proper etiquette
and generously rewarded him.
B7.9.2 In autumn,
Gēn Mú was taken;
it is said this was easily done.
B7.9.3 Zōu Zhāogōng died.
B7.9.4 There was a meeting at Hù,
to address those who were not harmonious.
The Marquis of Chén did not attend.
Xún Línfù of Jìn, leading the armies of the various lords, attacked Chén.
The Marquis of Jìn died at Hù,
and they returned.
B7.9.5 In winter,
the people of Sòng besieged Téng,
taking advantage of their mourning.
B7.9.6 Chén Línggōng, along with Kǒng Níng and Yí Xíngfù, had illicit relations with Xià Jī;
all wore inner garments that she had made
Xiè Yě remonstrated, saying:
"When dukes and ministers openly engage in licentiousness,
the people will have nothing to emulate,
and it will be known as unseemly.
Your lordships should cease it!"
The Duke said:
"I can reform."
The Duke told his two sons.
The two sons requested to kill him,
the Duke did not forbid it,
and so they killed Xiè Yě.
Kǒngzǐ said:
"The *Book of Odes* says:
'The people have many deviations,
Do not yourself create deviations.'
Is it not speaking of Xiè Yě!"
B7.9.7 The Viscount of Chǔ, because of the campaign against Lì,
attacked Zhèng.
B7.9.8 Xì Quē of Jìn rescued Zhèng.
The Earl of Zhèng defeated the Chǔ army at Liǔfén.
The people of the state were all happy,
but Zǐliáng alone worried, saying:
"This is a disaster for the state;
my death is not far off."
A7.10 *Annals of the Tenth Year of Duke Xuān*
A7.10.1 Tenth year, spring,
the Duke went to Qí.
A7.10.2 The Duke arrived back from Qí.
A7.10.3 The people of Qí returned the fields west of the Jì River to us.
A7.10.4 In the fourth month, on the day bingchen (丙辰),
there was a solar eclipse.
A7.10.5 On the day jisi (己巳),
Marquis Yuán of Qí (齊侯元) died.
A7.10.6 The Cuī (崔) clan of Qí (齊) fled to Wèi (衛).
A7.10.7 The Duke went to Qí (齊).
A7.10.8 In the fifth month,
the Duke returned from Qí (齊).
A7.10.9 On the day guisi (癸巳),
Chén Xià Zhēngshū (陳夏徵舒) assassinated his lord, Píng Gúo (平國).
A7.10.10 In the sixth month,
the army of Sòng (宋) attacked Téng (滕).
A7.10.11 Gōngsūn Guīfù (公孫歸父) went to Qí (齊).
The funeral of Duke Huì of Qí (齊惠公) took place.
A7.10.12 The people of Jìn (晉),
the people of Sòng (宋),
the people of Wèi (衛),
and the people of Cáo (曹) attacked Zhèng (鄭).
A7.10.13 In the autumn,
The Son of Heaven sent Wáng Jìzǐ 王季子 to pay a formal visit.
A7.10.14 Gōngsūn Guīfǔ 公孫歸父 led an army to attack Zhū 邾,
and captured Yì 繹.
A7.10.15 There was a great flood.
A7.10.16 Jìsūn Hángfǔ 季孫行父 went to Qí 齊.
A7.10.17 In winter,
Gōngsūn Guīfǔ 公孫歸父 went to Qí 齊.
A7.10.18 The Marquis of Qí 齊 sent Guó Zuǒ 國佐 to pay a formal visit.
A7.10.19 There was a famine.
A7.10.20 The Viscount of Chǔ 楚 attacked Zhèng 鄭.
B7.10 *Zuǒ Zhuàn* of the Tenth Year of Duke Xuān 宣公
B7.10.1 In the spring of the tenth year,
the Duke went to Qí 齊.
Because Qí 齊 had been subjugated by us,
they returned the fields west of the Jì River 濟西.
B7.10.2 In summer,
Duke Huì of Qí 齊 died.
Cuī Zhù 崔杼 was favored by Duke Huì 惠公.
Gāo 高 and Guó 國 feared his oppression,
so after the Duke died, they drove him out,
and he fled to Wèi 衛.
The text says "the Cuī 崔 clan",
which does not imply his guilt;
moreover, it names him by clan,
not by name.
The armies of the various lords attacked Zhèng [鄭],
captured Chéng [成], and then returned.
B7.10.7 In autumn,
Liú Kānggōng [劉康公] came to return the visit.
B7.10.8 The army attacked Zhū [邾]
and captured Yì [繹].
B7.10.9 Jì Wénzǐ [季文子] made his first official visit to Qí [齊].
B7.10.10 In winter,
Zǐjiā [子家] went to Qí [齊],
because of the attack on Zhū [邾].
B7.10.11 Guó Wǔzǐ [國武子] came to return the visit.
B7.10.12 The Viscount of Chǔ [楚子] attacked Zhèng [鄭].
Jìn's [晉] Shì Huì [士會] rescued Zhèng [鄭],
chasing the Chǔ [楚] army north of the Yǐng [潁] River.
The armies of the various lords garrisoned Zhèng [鄭].
B7.10.13 Zhèng's [鄭] Zǐjiā [子家] died.
The people of Zhèng [鄭] punished the rebellion of Duke Yōu [幽公],
desecrated Zǐjiā's [子家] coffin,
and banished his clan.
They reburied Duke Yōu [幽公],
and gave him the posthumous name
"Líng" [靈].
A7.11 *Annals of Duke Xuān, Year 11* [宣公十一年經]
A7.11.1 In the eleventh year, spring,
the king's first month.
A7.11.2 In summer,
Chǔ zǐ,
Chén hóu,
Zhèng bó formed an alliance at Chénlíng.
A7.11.3 Gōngsūn Guīfù met with the people of Qí to attack Jǔ.
A7.11.4 In autumn,
the Marquis of Jìn met with the Dí people at Cuán Hán.
A7.11.5 In the tenth month of winter,
the people of Chǔ killed Chén Xià Zhēngshū.
A7.11.6 On the day dinghai,
the Chǔ ruler entered Chén.
A7.11.7 He installed Gōngsūn Níng and
Yí Xíngfù in Chén.
B7.11 "Zuǒ Zhuàn, Year 11 of Duke Xuān"
B7.11.1 In the spring of the eleventh year,
the Chǔ ruler attacked Zhèng, reaching Lì.
Zǐ Liáng said:
"Jìn and Chǔ do not devote themselves to virtue
but contend with arms;
it is acceptable to side with whoever comes.
Jìn and Chǔ are not trustworthy,
how can we have trust with them?"
Therefore, they followed Chǔ.
In summer,
Chǔ formed an alliance at Chénlíng;
Chén and Zhèng submitted.
B7.11.2 Zǐ Zhòng, the Left Yin of Chǔ, invaded Sòng;
the king awaited him at Yán.
Xì Chéngzǐ 曰:
"Wú wén zhī,
fēi dé,
mò rú qín,
fēi qín,
hé yǐ qiú rén?
Néng qín,
yǒu jì.
Qí cóng zhī yě.
《Shī》 yuē:
'Wén Wáng jì qín zhǐ.'
Wén Wáng yóu qín,

kuàng guǎ dé hū?" Xì Chéngzǐ said, "I have heard that if one lacks virtue, nothing is better than diligence. If one is not diligent, how can one seek the help of others? If one is diligent, there will be successors. People will follow him. The *Book of Poetry* says, 'King Wén was already diligent.' Even King Wén was diligent, how much more so should those who lack virtue be?"
B7.11.5 In winter,
the ruler of Chǔ, because of the rebellion of the Xià clan in Chén,
attacked Chén.
He told the people of Chén,
"Do not move!
I will deal with the Shǎo Xī clan."
Then he entered Chén,
killed Xià Zhēngshū,
and quartered him at the Lì Gate.
He then made Chén a county.
The Marquis of Chén was in Jìn.
Shēn Shūshí was sent on a mission to Qí,
returned,
reported back
and withdrew.
The king sent someone to reprimand her,
saying:
"Xià Zhēngshū 夏徵舒 acted against the proper way,
murdering his lord.
I, the lesser one, led the lords to punish and execute him.
The lords and the heads of the counties all congratulated me.
You alone did not congratulate me.
What is the reason?"
She replied,
"May I offer an explanation?"
The king said,
"You may."
She said,
"Xià Zhēngshū 夏徵舒 murdered his lord,
his crime was great.
To punish and execute him
was the righteousness of the lord.
But people also have a saying:
'Someone leads an ox to tread upon another's field,
and then has the ox taken away.'
That the ox treaded on the field
is indeed a transgression,
but to take away the ox
is too severe a punishment.
The lords who followed you
said it was to punish the guilty.
Now you annexed Chén 陳,
coveting its wealth.
"To summon the feudal lords under the guise of punishing,
and then to return home with plunder,
wouldn't that be inappropriate?"
The king said,
"Excellent!
I had not heard of this before.
To return it,
is that possible?"
He replied,
"We commoners would say
'taking from his bosom and giving it back to him.'"
So he restored the fief of Chén.
In the countryside, he took one person and brought him back,
calling it Xiàzhōu.
Therefore, the history says, "The Viscount of Chǔ entered Chén.
He installed Gōngsūn Níng and Yí Xíngfù in Chén."
The history
is observant of ritual propriety.
B7.11.6 In the campaign against Lì,
the Count of Zhèng fled home.
From that time on, Chǔ did not achieve its ambition.
Zhèng, having accepted the alliance at Chénlíng,
also sought favor from Jìn.
A7.12 *Xuān Gōng* Year Twelve - Scripture
A7.12.1 In the twelfth year, spring,
the funeral of Duke Líng of Chén was held.
A7.12.2 The Chǔ ruler besieged Zhèng.
A7.12.3 In the sixth month, yǐ mǎo day of summer, Jìn's Xún Línfǔ led the army and fought against the Chǔ ruler at Bì,
the Jìn army was utterly defeated.
A7.12.4 In the seventh month of autumn.
A7.12.5 In the twelfth month of winter, on the wù yín day, the Chǔ ruler extinguished Xiāo.
A7.12.6 The people of Jìn,
the people of Sòng,
the people of Wèi,
and the people of Cáo formed an alliance at Qīngqiū.
A7.12.7 The Sòng army attacked Chén.
The people of Wèi rescued Chén.
B7.12 *Commentary on the Twelfth Year of Duke Xuān*
B7.12.1 In the spring of the twelfth year,
the Chǔ ruler besieged Zhèng for seventeen days.
The people of Zhèng divined whether to make peace, but it was not auspicious;
they divined whether to make a stand at the Grand Palace and send out chariots from the alleys, which was auspicious.
Auspicious.
The people of the state gathered in great numbers,
and those guarding the battlements all wept.
The ruler of Chǔ retreated his army.
The people of Zhèng repaired their city walls.
He advanced again to besiege it,
and after three months, conquered it.
He entered through the Huáng Gate
and proceeded to the Kuílù Road.
The Count of Zhèng, with his upper body bare and leading a sheep,
went out to meet him,
saying:
